# Enemy design UI covers Gym scene buttons (AH-0MUAYB7O4009LWBF)

## Headline

Gym editor/control panels are anchored to the top-left of the viewport and cover
the in-scene HUD labels (lives, power-ups, minerals). All gym panels should be
re-anchored to the bottom-left so the HUD stays visible.

## Problem statement

Every gym scene that exposes a plain-DOM tuning panel positions it at
`top: 8px; left: 8px` (`#gym-config-panel`) or `top: 8px; left: 260px`
(`#enemy-gym-panel`). The Phaser HUD renders its lives / power-up / weapon /
mineral rows at the top-left of the canvas (`HUD` is constructed at `(8, 8)`),
so the panel overlays the labels a designer is actively trying to read and tune
against. The original report called these "buttons"; the operator corrected this
to the lives/power-up labels.

## Users

- **Game designer / developer** tuning ship, enemy and boss configs in the gym
  scenes, who needs the live HUD (lives, active power-ups, weapons, minerals)
  visible while the tuning panel is open.
- **QA / playtester** verifying gym scenes, who needs both the HUD and the panel
  controls usable simultaneously.

### User stories

- As a designer tuning an enemy in the gym, I want the editor panel out of the
  way of the HUD so I can see lives/power-ups change as I tune.
- As a tester opening the Player gym, I want the tuning panel anchored
  consistently (bottom-left) across every gym scene.

## Acceptance criteria

- All gym panels are anchored to the **bottom-left** of the viewport instead of the top: `#gym-config-panel` (Player), `#enemy-gym-panel` (Enemies) and `#boss-gym-panel` (Boss), sharing consistent placement rules.
- Every panel has a `max-height` bounded to the viewport (minus a reserve) with internal vertical scrolling (`overflow-y: auto`), so a tall panel never extends above the viewport or re-covers the top-left HUD.
- With a panel open, the top-left HUD labels (lives / power-ups / weapons / minerals) are fully visible and unobscured.
- The in-canvas controls (`EXPLODE`, `SHOOT`, and the Boss `DAMAGE` button) and the status line are **repositioned to the bottom-right** so they remain visible and interactive while the panel occupies the bottom-left; the hint line stays clear of the panel.
- The Boss panel (`boss-gym-panel`, currently without any positioning CSS) receives the same bottom-left anchoring / `max-height` styling as the other panels.
- Automated tests assert the panels' bottom-left anchoring (e.g. via a shared CSS class/rule or computed style), the `max-height`/scroll constraint, and the bottom-right control repositioning; testing/validation criterion.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (in particular `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §8.5 and any Game Design Document references to the gym panel).
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The game canvas is a fixed `960 × 540` design surface rendered with
  `Phaser.Scale.FIT`; DOM panels are `position: fixed`, in CSS pixels, and do
  **not** scale with the canvas.
- Panels are plain DOM appended to `#game-container`; each scene removes its
  panel on `SHUTDOWN` and clears stale panels on rebuild (test isolation).
- happy-dom (the test environment) performs no real layout, so tests cannot
  assert pixel geometry — they must assert the CSS rule/class or the intended
  inline style.
- No behavioural/API changes to panel contents; this is a presentation fix.
- The boss panel currently has class `gym-panel` but no CSS rule for it — this
  is a pre-existing gap to fold into the fix.

## Existing state

- `src/style.css`:
  - `#gym-config-panel { position: fixed; top: 8px; left: 8px; ... }`
  - `#enemy-gym-panel { position: fixed; top: 8px; left: 260px; ... }`
  - No rule for `#boss-gym-panel` or `.gym-panel`.
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — standalone HUD constructed at `(8, 8)` (top-left), depth
  `HUD_DEPTH` (1000).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPlayer.ts` — builds `#gym-config-panel`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.ts` — builds `#enemy-gym-panel` (~21 rows).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.ts` — builds `#boss-gym-panel` (spawn-interval control).
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — places `EXPLODE` at `(10, 480)`,
  `SHOOT` at `(120, 480)`, status text at `(10, 504)`; creates the HUD.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.ts` — adds `DAMAGE` at `(240, 480)`.

## Desired change

Re-anchor every gym panel to the bottom-left of the viewport (shared class or
per-id rules), capped with a viewport-relative `max-height` and internal
scrolling so tall panels stay on-screen below the HUD. Apply consistent styling
to the currently-unstyled boss panel. Move the in-canvas `EXPLODE`/`SHOOT`/
`DAMAGE` controls and the status line to the bottom-right so they remain usable
alongside the panel. Update documentation and add regression tests for the
anchoring and control placement.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/style.css` — Move panel anchoring from `top` to `bottom`; add a shared
  `.gym-panel` rule (and/or `#boss-gym-panel`) so all panels share bottom-left
  placement plus a viewport-relative `max-height` with `overflow-y: auto`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.ts` — apply the shared panel class/id consistently
  (already sets `className = 'gym-panel'`); move the `DAMAGE` button to the
  bottom-right.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — reposition the in-canvas
  `EXPLODE`/`SHOOT` buttons and status line to the bottom-right; keep the hint
  line clear of the panel.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — update §8.5 panel surface notes and
  the HUD-controls description (§ around line 156).
- Test files (e.g. `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.test.ts`, `GymPlayer.test.ts`,
  `GymBoss.test.ts`, or a new `src/style.test.ts`) — assert bottom-left
  anchoring, the `max-height`/scroll constraint, and the bottom-right control
  coordinates.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items

- **AH-0MT99I2OC0014MNZ** – Create E3 Tank gym scene (completed)
- **AH-0MUDYS2SZ004H123** – Asteroids spawn randomly offscreen (open)
- **AH-0MTFRQR42001M8WQ** – Scheme-aware input tests for affected gym scenes (completed)

### Repository file matches

- `README.md`
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (§8.5 Gym surface — GymEnemies + editor panel)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md`

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** bottom-left is free of HUD elements — the HUD is top-left, so
  this holds.
- **Risk:** the enemy editor panel is taller than the 540 px viewport; mitigated
  by the agreed `max-height` + `overflow-y: auto` (AC2).
- **Risk:** bottom-left is occupied by the in-canvas `EXPLODE`/`SHOOT`/`DAMAGE`
  controls; mitigated by the agreed bottom-right repositioning (AC4).
- **Risk:** bottom-right placement must not collide with the top-right
  `← INDEX` button or the centred hint line; verify when repositioning.
- **Risk:** happy-dom cannot verify real overlap; mitigation is to assert the
  anchoring rule/class and the control coordinates explicitly, and document the
  visual expectation for manual verification.
- **Scope-creep risk:** reworking panel layout/compaction beyond a height cap is
  a larger design task; record as a separate work item rather than folding into
  this fix.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q:** Which UI element is actually being covered — which buttons?
  **A (operator, interactive):** "Buttons is the wrong word, it's actually the
  lives/powerup etc. labels." — i.e. the top-left HUD labels.
- **Q:** Does this affect only the Enemy gym scene or all gym scenes with a panel?
  **A (operator, interactive):** "all scenes with a panel (player too, for
  example)".
- **Q:** What should the fixed positioning be?
  **A (operator, interactive):** "move it so it is aligned bottom left".
- **Q:** The enemy editor panel is taller than the 540 px game viewport; how
  should tall panels be handled? **A (operator/producer, interactive):**
  "(1) a" — option (a) `max-height` + internal scroll.
- **Q:** Bottom-left is occupied by the `EXPLODE`/`SHOOT`/`DAMAGE` controls; how
  should the overlap be resolved? **A (operator/producer, interactive):**
  "(2) reposition to bottom right".

# Bullets from the players ship should always fall on the beat

## Problem statement

Player auto-fire currently uses per-weapon cooldowns started at collection time (`src/utils/weapons.ts`, `Player.tryFire`), so shots drift relative to any musical pulse and different active weapons fire out of phase. Make every player shot land on a shared musical grid: player fire is globally quantised to an **80 BPM** beat, and every weapon's fire rate is an exact subdivision of that beat. The values are configurable rather than hard-coded.

## Users

- **Player** — wants the ship's shots to feel rhythmically locked to a consistent 80 BPM pulse, so the auto-fire has a musical cadence even with no background music.
- **AI agents / developers** — need a single, pure beat-clock module and a catalogue-wide invariant so any current or future weapon (e.g. the planned 20 BPM quarter-time large/explosive bullet) can be added without accidentally firing off the beat.

### Example user stories

- As a **player**, I want my ship's bullets to leave on the beat, so the auto-fire feels deliberate and rhythmic rather than mechanically drifting.
- As a **player**, I want every weapon I collect to keep firing in time with the same beat, so switching weapons never makes the rhythm stumble.
- As a **developer**, I want a weapon's fire rate to be expressed as a subdivision of the beat and validated by a test, so I cannot add an off-grid weapon by mistake.
- As a **developer**, I want the BPM and per-weapon subdivisions to be configurable, so the feel can be tuned (and tested) without editing hard-coded literals.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Pure, configurable 80 BPM beat clock.** A new pure, unit-testable module (e.g. `src/utils/beat.ts`) derives the beat period from a **configurable** BPM (default **80 BPM** → 750 ms/beat), tracks a beat anchor/time origin, and exposes a quantisation helper that maps an arbitrary elapsed time to the next beat/subdivision tick (`nextTick(t)`, `isOnBeat/fireTimeFor(interval, t)`, etc.). No `Date`/frame coupling; deterministic given an input time.
- [ ] **AC2 — All player fire is globally quantised.** Player auto-fire (`Player.tryFire` and its callers in `CombatScene`/`GymWeapons`) emits shots only on ticks of the shared beat clock, phase-locked to the scene/beat anchor — never off-grid — regardless of when a weapon is collected or the frame rate. All simultaneously active weapons fire on the same shared grid (no independent, drifting cooldowns). Tests assert every emitted shot time is an exact grid tick.
- [ ] **AC3 — Per-weapon subdivisions + catalogue-wide invariant.** Each weapon's fire interval is an exact subdivision of the beat: **cannon 375 ms (160 BPM, 2/beat)**, **spread 750 ms (80 BPM, 1/beat)**, **dual 750 ms (80 BPM, 1/beat)**, **rapid 125 ms (480 BPM, 6/beat)**. A catalogue-wide test asserts every `WeaponDefinition.fireRateMs` satisfies `beatPeriodMs % fireRateMs === 0` (equivalently `fireRateMs × n === beatPeriodMs` for a positive integer `n`), so the future 20 BPM quarter-time weapon and any other new weapon are on-grid by construction.
- [ ] **AC4 — All values configurable.** BPM, the per-weapon subdivisions/fire rates, and the quantisation behaviour are configurable through the project's existing config plumbing (`src/core/rules.ts` and/or `src/core/config.ts`/`constants.ts`; persisted where the existing pattern persists), with sane defaults — no scattered hard-coded beat/rate literals. Tests assert a config override changes the firing cadence.
- [ ] **AC5 — Testing/validation.** Unit tests cover the beat module (period from BPM, quantisation boundaries/edge cases, config override), the catalogue invariant (AC3), and `Player.tryFire`/auto-fire emitting only on grid ticks with multiple active weapons phase-locked. Scene-level tests (gameHarness) assert real bullet spawns land on grid ticks across multiple frames and are framerate-independent. All tests serve a distinct behaviour.
- [ ] **AC6 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries — in particular GDD §2.3/§4.4 (the "Cannon fires every ~400 ms" wording and the weapon fire-rate description) and any beat/config tuning docs.
- [ ] **AC7 — Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Engine/stack:** Phaser v4 + TypeScript, Vite, Vitest (locked). No external art/audio assets.
- **Silent timing grid only:** per producer, the beat is an internal scheduling contract — **no audible metronome and no background music** (GDD §7.3/§8 keep music out of MVP scope). No beat audio/visual indicator is in scope.
- **Player bullets only:** enemy fire timing is unchanged (the item is titled "from the players ship").
- **Scope:** applies to all scenes that auto-fire the player (PlayScene via `CombatScene`, and the gym scenes reusing `Player`), through one shared beat module — not per-scene duplicates.
- **Beat anchor:** the beat clock is anchored at scene/player start and advances with game time (pauses with the game if paused).
- **No behaviour change beyond timing:** weapon patterns, bullet visuals, lifetimes, cumulative+timed semantics and Reset behaviour are unchanged; only fire timing changes.

## Existing state

- `src/utils/weapons.ts` defines `WEAPON_CATALOGUE` with hard-coded `fireRateMs` (cannon 400, spread 600, dual 500, rapid 125) and `bulletLifetime` values; heading/pattern math is pure.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` holds per-weapon cooldowns in `_weaponCooldowns` and `tryFire(dt)` re-arms a fired weapon's cooldown to its own `fireRateMs` (independent timers, phase set by collection time). Cumulative + timed semantics (`equipWeapon`, `resetWeapon`, `tickWeaponTimers`) are implemented and tested.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` (`_autoFire`) and `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts` (`_autoFire`) call `player.tryFire(dt)` each frame and spawn bullets via `createBulletsFromHeading`/`angleToVelocity`.
- **No beat/BPM/clock infrastructure exists anywhere in `src/`**; there is no music system (GDD §7.3 out-of-MVP).
- Config precedent: `src/core/rules.ts` (localStorage-persisted `GameRules`, e.g. power-up spawn interval) and `src/core/config.ts`/`configTypes.ts` (CSV-backed ship config). `src/core/constants.ts` holds `WEAPON_TIMEOUT_MS` etc.
- Related completed work: AH-0MTC1TEXR006I5XR (weapon catalogue + auto-fire), AH-0MUD9R3070063DDR (`tryFire` extraction), AH-0MTV7RITM009LJF6 (cumulative/timed weapons), AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0 (bullet lifetimes).

## Desired change

1. Add a pure **beat module** (`src/utils/beat.ts`): BPM → beat period, beat anchor, and quantisation helpers (`nextSubdivisionTick`, `shotTimeFor`, `isOnGrid`). Configurable BPM (default 80).
2. Re-express each `WeaponDefinition` fire rate as a **beat subdivision** (cannon 2/beat, spread 1/beat, dual 1/beat, rapid 6/beat) derived from the beat period; add the catalogue-wide on-grid invariant test.
3. Replace per-weapon free-running cooldowns in `Player.tryFire` with **phase-locked scheduling**: a weapon's next shot time is the smallest multiple of its interval at/after the current beat-clock time (anchored at the shared beat origin), so every shot lands on a grid tick and active weapons stay in phase. Collection may delay the first shot to the next grid tick (by design).
4. Wire the shared beat clock into `CombatScene._autoFire` and `GymWeapons._autoFire` (and any other `Player.tryFire` callers) so the scene supplies/uses the same clock.
5. Make BPM and the per-weapon subdivisions **configurable** through the existing config plumbing with defaults, rather than literals.
6. Update unit + scene-harness tests (existing `weapons.test.ts`, `Player.test.ts`, `GymWeapons.test.ts`, `CombatScene` tests) and documentation (GDD §2.3/§4.4, README).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/utils/beat.ts` — **NEW** — pure, configurable 80 BPM beat clock + quantisation helpers.
- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — fire rates re-expressed as beat subdivisions; catalogue-wide on-grid invariant.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — `tryFire`/cooldown model → phase-locked scheduling on the shared beat clock.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — `_autoFire` drives the shared beat clock.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts` — `_autoFire` drives the shared beat clock.
- `src/core/rules.ts` / `src/core/config.ts` (and/or `src/core/constants.ts`) — configurable BPM + per-weapon subdivisions with defaults.
- `src/utils/weapons.test.ts`, **NEW** `src/utils/beat.test.ts`, `src/entities/Player.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.test.ts` — coverage for quantisation, invariant and scene emission.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §2.3/§4.4; `README.md` — document the beat-aligned fire model.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Gameplay-feel change:** current rates (cannon 400 → 375 ms; spread 600 → 750 ms; dual 500 → 750 ms; rapid 125 unchanged) slightly change DPS/cadence, and collection now delays the first shot to the next grid tick. Assumption: acceptable and intended ("must always fall on the beat").
- **Definition of "the beat" without music:** resolved by the producer — silent internal grid; no audible/visual reference. The beat is only observable through bullet cadence and tests.
- **Config surface choice:** the producer requires configurability, but the exact home (localStorage rules vs CSV ship config vs constants) is a planning decision; the ACs require at least one tested override path.
- **Phase-locking and multiple weapons:** cumulative weapons with different subdivisions must share the anchor; an implementation that keeps independent cooldowns will drift — the AC2 test guards this.
- **Frame quantisation edge cases:** shots must be attributed to the correct grid tick under variable `dt` (including large deltas), and remain framerate-independent — explicit boundary tests required.
- **Scope-creep risk:** audible beat/music, enemy fire quantisation, and beat-synced visuals are out of scope; record as linked work items rather than folding in.

## Related work

- **AH-0MTC1TEXR006I5XR** (completed) — "Weapon power-ups (3 patterns + reset) with auto-fire and weapon gym scene": origin of `WEAPON_CATALOGUE`, the fire-rate constants and `Player` auto-fire this item re-times.
- **AH-0MUD9R3070063DDR** (completed) — "Extract auto-fire with onWeaponFired hook": the `tryFire` auto-fire architecture being changed.
- **AH-0MTV7RITM009LJF6** (completed) — "Make weapons both cumalative and time out": cumulative per-weapon timers/cooldowns.
- **AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0** (completed) — "Bullets should have a distance and should wrap around the screen": per-weapon bullet lifetimes adjacent to the fire-rate config.
- **AH-0MTGS8TWU006WTFX** (completed) — "Wire shoot audio into GymWeapons._autoFire()": fire cues whose cadence follows the fire rate.
- **AH-0MT7UW0Y80062NU1** (completed) — "Bring simple audio effects into MVP scope in GDD": the audio-scope boundary (no music).
- **GDD (AH-0MT7O8KCY0059RA5)** — §2.3 auto-fire (~400 ms wording), §4.4 weapon fire rates/lifetimes, §7.3 audio (music out of scope), §8 future scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Beat semantics — (a) per-weapon beat-subdivision intervals with independent cooldowns, or (b) a single 80 BPM clock with every shot snapped to the next grid tick?" — Answer (producer, interactive): **(b) global beat quantisation**. Source: interactive reply.
- Q2: "What is the beat reference — (a) silent internal grid only, (b) audible metronome, or (c) visual beat indicator?" — Answer (producer, interactive): **(a) silent internal grid only** (no music; consistent with GDD §7.3). Source: interactive reply.
- Q3: "Per-weapon subdivisions and the catalogue-wide invariant?" — Answer (producer, interactive): **as recommended** — cannon 375 ms (160 BPM, 2/beat), spread 750 ms (80 BPM, 1/beat), dual 750 ms (80 BPM, 1/beat), rapid 125 ms (480 BPM, 6/beat); invariant `beatPeriodMs % fireRateMs === 0` enforced for the whole catalogue. Source: interactive reply.
- Producer note (interactive, given alongside the answers to Q1–Q3): **all values must be configurable** (BPM, per-weapon subdivisions, quantisation behaviour). Source: interactive reply.

> Prior answers changed: none — all answers above are the final accepted versions.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0** – Bullets should have a distance and should wrap around the screen (completed)
- **AH-0MUFGUR9C003XD77** – GitHub Pages deploy rejects release tags (environment policy allows only dev) (in-progress)
- **AH-0MT985VRY009JXLZ** – Gym index scene (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: add, always, assert, based, beat (+30 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: add, always, based, beat, bullet (+29 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: add, always, assert, based, belongs (+28 more)

## Plan (plan_complete)

Decomposed into 8 child work items (test-first / vertical-slice), all at
stage `intake_complete`:

**Phase 1 — Foundation**
- Implement pure, configurable 80 BPM beat clock module (AH-0MUGPSOVM006Z1OJ)

**Phase 2 — Grid + invariant**
- Refactor weapon fire rates as beat subdivisions and add catalogue-wide invariant (AH-0MUGQBN5T009U4YG)
- Make BPM and per-weapon subdivisions configurable via existing config plumbing (AH-0MUGY84L1004H2UP)

**Phase 3 — Emission + wiring**
- Replace Player.tryFire per-weapon cooldowns with phase-locked beat scheduling (AH-0MUGQCMNA0061J4A)
- Wire the shared beat clock into CombatScene and GymWeapons auto-fire (AH-0MUGY7ZUO008QSUX)

**Phase 4 — Verification + handoff**
- Scene-level tests: verify real bullet spawns land on grid ticks (AH-0MUGY89LE006WVDQ)
- Update documentation: GDD sections, README, code comments (AH-0MUGY8DPC005ERM9)
- Run full test suite and fix any failures (AH-0MUGY8HHU006XMU9)

**Dependency edges:** T2→T1, T3→T1, T4→T3, T5→{T1,T2}, T6→T4,
T7→{T2,T3,T4,T5}, T8→{T6,T7}.

**Vertical-slice phasing:** every implementation task carries its own
code + tests + comments (test-first within the task); T6 is the
cross-cutting scene-harness verification gate, T7 the documentation
slice, T8 the project-wide regression gate. Between phases, review and
update the next items' descriptions before starting them.

**Approval gate:** requested — effort is Medium scale. Recorded as a
`question (plan approval gate)` comment; `needs-producer-review` is set.

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-09-25 — Initial plan: 8 children created, dependency edges wired,
  six automated review stages run, AC coverage review returned `proceed`
  (100 %). Review improvements: added T5→T2 dependency; added T5 AC6
  (invariant preserved under config override); added explicit
  parent-AC traceability bullets to all children. Effort/risk estimate
  refreshed.

### Appendix — planning session

No **new** clarifying questions were required in this planning session.
The three design-defining questions (Q1 global beat quantisation,
Q2 silent internal grid only, Q3 per-weapon subdivisions + catalogue-wide
invariant) were answered by the producer during intake and are recorded
in the Appendix above, together with the producer's "all values must be
configurable" note. This plan is a mechanical decomposition of those
accepted answers — no new assumptions were introduced.

# Reduce Volume of Player Thrusters — Intake Brief

## Problem Statement

Player thruster hum is too loud. The maximum gain (`THRUSTER_HUM_MAX_VOLUME`) of `0.15` should be reduced by 50% to `0.075` so the thruster sound sits more comfortably in the mix without drowning out other cues.

## Users

- Player experiencing the game, hearing the thruster hum alongside other SFX (shoot, pickup, enemies, music).

## User Stories

- As a player, I hear the thruster hum at roughly half its current loudness, so it doesn't overpower other game audio.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Halved volume ceiling:** `THRUSTER_HUM_MAX_VOLUME` in `src/audio/effects.ts` is changed from `0.15` to `0.075`. All thruster hum output is now at most 50% of its former level.
- **AC2 — GDD §7.3 updated:** The Game Design Document's Player Audio Character table and thruster hum description are updated to reflect the new `≤ 0.075` volume ceiling.
- **AC3 — No behavioural regressions:** Thruster gain envelope, rise/decay timing, detune drift, noise filtering, and all other thruster characteristics remain unchanged — only the maximum volume target is halved.
- **AC4 — Tests updated:** Any existing tests asserting `THRUSTER_HUM_MAX_VOLUME === 0.15` are updated to expect `0.075`. Full project test suite passes with no regressions.

## Constraints

- 50% reduction only — no other audio parameters change.
- Must not affect other SFX (shoot, pickup, enemy audio, master SFX volume).
- Procedural audio only — no external assets.

## Existing State

- `THRUSTER_HUM_MAX_VOLUME = 0.15` in `src/audio/effects.ts` (line 42).
- GDD §7.3 documents thruster hum at `≤ 0.15`.
- All thruster hum paths multiply their gain target by `THRUSTER_HUM_MAX_VOLUME` (e.g. `updateThrusterSound` line: `const targetGain = clamped * THRUSTER_HUM_MAX_VOLUME`).
- `effects.test.ts` asserts against `THRUSTER_HUM_MAX_VOLUME`.

## Desired Change

- Update `THRUSTER_HUM_MAX_VOLUME` from `0.15` to `0.075`.
- Update GDD §7.3 to reflect the new volume ceiling.
- Update any test assertions referencing the old value.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/audio/effects.ts` — Change `THRUSTER_HUM_MAX_VOLUME` from `0.15` to `0.075`
- `src/audio/effects.test.ts` — Update assertions expecting `THRUSTER_HUM_MAX_VOLUME` (existing references use the constant, so may auto-adjust)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — Update §7.3 thruster hum entry: change `≤ 0.15` to `≤ 0.075`

## Related Work

- **AH-0MTFOSOHN001Q620** — Player thruster SFX (original thruster hum implementation)
- **AH-0MTK9ZSOX009SB1K** — Thruster hum: jet-engine roar — remove buzzy sawtooth
- **AH-0MUA8B6MT006M1KS** — SFX master volume + mute plumbing in effects.ts

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Minimal change risk:** This is a single-constant change in the code path; regressions are unlikely.
- **Perceptual quality:** The hum is quieter but should still be audible — at `0.075` it remains within the `≤ 0.2` player-cue ceiling and is proportional to other player cues.
- **Test auto-adjustment:** Tests reference `THRUSTER_HUM_MAX_VOLUME` as a constant, so most should automatically pick up the new value; spot-check for hard-coded `0.15` assertions.
- **Scope-creep risk:** Adjustments to other SFX volumes, music levels, or EQ changes are out of scope — track as `discovered-from:AH-0MUAYB8S50029QB8` work items.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions

- Q1 — Volume reduction target: "Reduce volume by 50%" — Answer: Halve `THRUSTER_HUM_MAX_VOLUME` from `0.15` to `0.075`. Source: operator confirmation.
- Q2 — GDD update: Should §7.3 be updated? — Answer: Yes, to `≤ 0.075`. Source: operator confirmation.
- Q3 — Audio assets: External files needed? — Answer: No, procedural audio only. Source: operator confirmation.

# Intake Brief: Divers should not return (AH-0MUAYB957002EMYV)

## Planning status (re-planned 2026-09-28)

The original freeze-based brief (2026-09-26) was rejected by the producer and by audit, and the implementation merged under this item (commit `0c529c58`, "Hold formation drift while a Diver is away") does **not** describe the required behaviour. The producer gave a definitive replacement specification on 2026-09-27 (comments `AH-C0MUKCONWH000U5XG` and `AH-C0MUKD1JVC004PR7D`). This brief has been rewritten to that specification; the superseded freeze design and its acceptance criteria have been removed. The re-anchor target is the Diver's attack-end location, which is the **player's position snapshotted at dive start** — a moving target, not a fixed point.

## Headline

After a Diver completes its dive attack, it does **not** return to a formation slot. The enemy **unit** re-forms around the location where the attack finished — the unit's formation is defined relative to the units' positions, so the remaining units shift to keep their relative offsets around the new anchor. The formation-hold/freeze behaviour added by this item (commit `0c529c58`) is obsolete and must be removed.

## Problem statement

Today a Diver dives toward the player, pauses for 500 ms, then glides back onto its formation slot, chasing a cluster that has kept drifting. The producer's requirement is that there is **no return target at all**: the Diver stays where its attack ended and the rest of the unit re-forms around that location, preserving the units' relative arrangement. The interim "freeze the whole cluster while a Diver is away" design does not satisfy this and is rejected.

## Producer's confirmed specification (2026-09-27)

- "No, there is NO return target. They do not return. They simply go back to their unit formation (relative to one another's position) around the location their attack finished." — producer, recorded in comment `AH-C0MUKCONWH000U5XG`.
- Interpretation confirmed by the producer ("yes, that's what I want"): the **whole enemy unit** re-anchors to the Diver's attack-end location and re-forms around it, with the other enemies shifting to keep their relative offsets around the new anchor — comment `AH-C0MUKD1JVC004PR7D`.
- Earlier producer phrasing (same day): "dive to the attack position, freeze for a moment then return to their formation in their current position. They should NOT go back to their original position, nor should they go to where their position would be if they continued drifting."

## Superseded decisions

- Intake **Q1-A** ("they still return, but to their slot in the *current* formation") is superseded — there is no return.
- Intake **Q2-B** ("freeze the whole formation's drift while any Diver is diving/returning") is **rejected**. The whole formation-hold seam is obsolete:
  - `Diver.requiresFormationHold()` and the `FormationHoldSeam` on `EnemyEntity` / `FormationSceneEntity`;
  - the hold gates in `GymFormationScene.tick()` (`formationBaseX` + wrap) and `PlayScene._moveEnemies()` (`driftX`/`driftDir`);
  - the `PlayScene` observability getters `getFormationDriftX()` / `getFormationDriftDir()`;
  - the freeze tests added to `Diver.test.ts`, `GymFormationScene.test.ts` and `PlayScene.test.ts`, plus the hold documentation added to `README.md`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §7.6 and GDD §4.1 E2.
- Intake **Q3-A** (keep the diagonal dive and the straight glide from the dive target to the current slot) is partially superseded: the diagonal dive and the pause stay, but the **glide back is removed**.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1 — The freeze/hold behaviour is removed.** No entity seam can freeze the formation drift. `GymFormationScene.tick()` advances `formationBaseX` (and fires the right-edge wrap/respawn) unconditionally, and `PlayScene._moveEnemies()` advances `driftX`/`driftDir` unconditionally, while a Diver is `DIVING`/`PAUSING`. `Diver.requiresFormationHold()` and the optional interface members are gone, and so are the freeze tests and hold documentation. *Verification:* a scene test asserts the base/drift advances while a Diver is in a non-`FORMATION` state; a repo search finds no `requiresFormationHold` references.
2. **AC2 — There is no return glide.** The Diver never moves back toward its dive-start slot or a drift-extrapolated slot. The `RETURNING` state and `_handleReturn()` are removed; the state machine is `FORMATION → DIVING → PAUSING → FORMATION`. *Verification:* a test asserts that from the first tick after `PAUSING` ends the Diver is in `FORMATION`, that its position never moves toward the old slot, and that `DiverState.RETURNING` no longer exists.
3. **AC3 — The unit re-forms around the attack-end location.** When an attack finishes, the formation anchor is re-based on **both axes** so that the attacking Diver's own formation slot coincides with its attack-end position (the player position snapshotted at dive start), and **every** other unit shifts by the same delta, preserving the grid's relative offsets. *Verification:* a scene test with at least one non-Diver unit asserts that after the attack ends the Diver sits at its attack-end position and every other unit's position equals `newAnchor + itsOffset` — i.e. every unit shifted by the same delta as the Diver's slot. A second test with the player at two different positions asserts the re-anchor follows the target rather than a fixed screen point.
4. **AC4 — Dive, pause and attack are unchanged.** The diagonal quadratic-bezier dive toward the player position snapshotted at dive start, the 500 ms pause, the spread-shot firing, the dive/pause rotation and facing, the dive audio and the explosion behaviour are all preserved, and non-Diver entities (Scout/Tank/Phaser/Swarm/Asteroid/Boss) behave exactly as before apart from the shared re-anchor shift. *Verification:* the pre-existing dive/pause/facing/fire tests stay green; a formation with no Diver drifts exactly as it does today.
5. **AC5 — Gym↔game parity.** The re-anchor behaviour is implemented once and consumed by both the game and the gyms: the gym base `GymFormationScene` (and therefore `GymDiver` and the other gym scenes that extend it) and `PlayScene` run the same Diver logic and the same re-anchor rule; only the scene-specific anchor bookkeeping may differ. *Verification:* the repo-wide duplicate-body/parity guard in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` passes, and both scenes have a re-anchor test.
6. **AC6 — Tests, docs and the full suite.** New deterministic tests cover the removal of the freeze and the re-anchor in both scenes (single Diver, a Diver alongside a non-Diver unit, and a no-Diver control); documentation is updated to describe the re-anchor behaviour and to drop the freeze (notably `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, GDD §4.1 E2, and `README.md` if it mentions the hold); the full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Remove the obsolete seam completely.** Revert the behavioural parts of commit `0c529c58` (the seam, both gates, the observability getters) and its freeze tests/docs. Do not leave a dormant `requiresFormationHold` seam.
- **One shared re-anchor rule, both scenes.** The anchor computation belongs in the shared core or a shared helper consumed by `GymFormationScene` and `PlayScene`; the scenes must not grow divergent copies (gym↔game parity convention).
- **Preserve the attack.** Do not change the dive shape, the 500 ms pause, dive/pause timing, `DIVER_*` constants, audio or VFX.
- **No new audio/VFX and no timing/config-default changes.** Use the existing `DIVER_*` constants.
- **Do not fold in the unrelated docs item** `AH-0MUEI8HSU000QLEA` (GDD describes the dive as vertical/x-locked while the code is diagonal) — that stays separate.
- **Out of scope:** closing formation gaps / restructuring the internal layout while a Diver is away (intake `Q2-C`) and wrap-only relocation (`Q2-D`) were offered and not selected; record such ideas as separate linked work items rather than adding them here.

## Existing state

- `src/entities/Diver.ts` runs a four-state machine (`FORMATION → DIVING → PAUSING → RETURNING → FORMATION`). The dive is a diagonal quadratic bezier from the formation slot to the player position snapshotted at dive start (`AH-0MTGBOKLC006N8UX`); the pause is 500 ms (`AH-0MU0EIDQQ003S1JT`); `_handleReturn()` glides from the dive target onto the slot evaluated each frame from the live `baseX`/`baseY` (`AH-0MTEI361E000IXYB`).
- The formation origin is `formationBaseX`/`formationBaseY` in `GymFormationScene` and `s.startX + driftX` / `s.startY` per spawned group in `PlayScene`; each entity's position is `origin + formationOffset * spacing`. Neither origin is re-basable today.
- `setAimTarget(player.x, player.y)` is pushed to entities every frame by both scenes (`GymFormationScene` line ~1325, `PlayScene` line ~1126), and `Diver._startDive()` snapshots the target — so the attack-end location is **the player's position as it was when the dive started** (a moving target), not a point near the formation. In a player-less gym the Diver keeps the default stand-in target (screen bottom-centre).
- Commit `0c529c58` (merged to `dev`) added the obsolete freeze seam described under Superseded decisions.
- Open `AH-0MUEI8HSU000QLEA` records that GDD §4.1 still describes a vertical/x-locked dive while the implementation is diagonal (pre-existing, not caused by this item).

## Desired change

1. **Remove the freeze seam.** Delete `Diver.requiresFormationHold()`, the `FormationHoldSeam` from `EnemyEntity` and `FormationSceneEntity`, the hold gates in `GymFormationScene.tick()` and `PlayScene._moveEnemies()`, the `getFormationDriftX()`/`getFormationDriftDir()` getters, and the associated freeze tests and documentation.
2. **Remove the return.** Delete the `RETURNING` state and `_handleReturn()`; when the pause elapses the Diver transitions straight to `FORMATION`.
3. **Add a re-anchor request seam.** When the pause elapses (the moment the attack finishes), the Diver requests a re-anchor at its current (attack-end) position. The request carries the Diver's own formation offset so the scene can compute `delta = attackEnd − (origin + offset * spacing)`.
4. **Re-base the origin (both axes).** The scene applies `origin += delta` for the whole unit, so the Diver's slot now equals the attack-end position and every other unit shifts by the same delta (relative offsets preserved). In `GymFormationScene` this moves `formationBaseX`/`formationBaseY`; in `PlayScene` it needs a unit-level anchor offset (X and Y) applied to every formation entity's origin. Re-anchoring Y is expected and correct — the warren follows the player's snapshotted position, it is not pinned to the screen bottom.
5. **Keep the existing per-frame positioning.** After the re-anchor, the Diver is in `FORMATION` and its next `applyFormationPosition()` places it at the (new) anchor plus its offset — exactly the attack-end position — so there is no snap.
6. Implementation order (test-first): (1) add the failing tests (no-freeze; no-return; re-anchor with a non-Diver unit; no-Diver control) and remove the obsolete freeze tests; (2) remove the freeze seam and the `RETURNING` state/`_handleReturn()`; (3) add the re-anchor request and the origin re-base in both scenes; (4) full suite and docs.

## Open questions

- **RESOLVED (2026-09-28) — vertical component of the re-anchor.** An earlier draft of this brief assumed the attack-end was fixed at the screen bottom, which is wrong: the target is the player's live position snapshotted at dive start, so it moves with the player. The re-anchor therefore follows the Diver to that (moving) location in **both axes** — Option A. Only a player-less gym uses the bottom-centre stand-in.
- **OPEN QUESTION 2 (non-blocking, documented assumption unless corrected) — multiple / desynchronised Divers.** Divers normally share the hold timer and dive together; their snapshotted targets are the same point, so simultaneous re-anchors are idempotent. If Divers become desynchronised (destruction + later respawn) they finish attacks at different positions; the assumed rule is **the most recent attack-end wins**. Confirm or specify.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/entities/Diver.ts` — remove `requiresFormationHold()` and the `RETURNING` state/`_handleReturn()`; transition `PAUSING → FORMATION` and expose the re-anchor request seam.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — remove the hold gate; re-base `formationBaseX`/`formationBaseY` on the re-anchor request; replace the `requiresFormationHold?` member on `FormationSceneEntity` with the re-anchor seam.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — remove the hold gate and the `getFormationDriftX`/`getFormationDriftDir` getters; apply the unit re-anchor delta to every formation entity's origin in `_moveEnemies()`.
- `src/entities/enemyFactory.ts` — replace `FormationHoldSeam` on the `EnemyEntity` union with the re-anchor seam.
- `src/entities/Diver.test.ts` — remove the hold/seam tests; add the state-machine (no `RETURNING`) and attack-end re-anchor tests.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts` — remove the freeze tests; add re-anchor / no-freeze tests.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — remove the freeze tests; add re-anchor / no-freeze tests.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — replace the §7.6 hold description with the re-anchor behaviour.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — GDD §4.1 E2: describe the re-anchor instead of the formation hold.
- `README.md` — drop the hold wording if present.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — this is the third attempt at this behaviour.** The requirement must be nailed before implementation. Mitigation: the requirements are now confirmed and captured in AC1–AC6; the remaining desynchronised-Diver rule is a documented assumption (Open Question 2).
- **Risk — whole-wave relocation (intended behaviour, but a difficulty change).** The wave re-anchors to the player's snapshotted position on every Diver attack, so the unit tracks the player across the arena. This is the confirmed intent; it is a material difficulty/pacing change (collision pressure, arena positioning) and should be watched in playtest. Mitigation: keep the re-anchor in the single shared rule so tuning it later (e.g. clamping or a max shift) is one change, and note the tuning surface in the docs.
- **Risk — two origin implementations.** `GymFormationScene` has a mutable `formationBaseX`/`formationBaseY`; `PlayScene` has per-group `startX`/`startY` plus a global `driftX`. A shared re-anchor helper is required so the two paths cannot diverge.
- **Assumption — attack end = end of `PAUSING`.** The re-anchor fires when the pause elapses, i.e. at the position where the Diver fired, before any return motion. (This is the same position as the end of the dive, because the pause holds position.) The position is the player's location snapshotted at dive start.
- **Assumption — most recent attack-end wins** for desynchronised Divers (Open Question 2).
- **Assumption — non-Diver entities are unaffected** except by the shared re-anchor delta.
- **Scope-creep risk:** gap-closing/restructuring (`Q2-C`) and wrap-only relocation (`Q2-D`) were offered and not selected; any such ideas should be recorded as linked work items rather than added here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

### Prior intake answers (now superseded — retained for traceability)

- **Q1 — Does "Divers should not return" mean they must not return at all, or that they must not return to the stale start point?** — Answer (producer, interactive): "1. a" → they still return, but to their slot in the *current* formation. **Superseded** by the 2026-09-27 specification: there is no return.
- **Q2 — What does "the cluster of enemies should not move from their current location other than to restructure the formation" require in practice?** — Answer (producer, interactive): "2. b" → freeze the whole formation's drift while any Diver is diving/returning. **Rejected** by the producer on 2026-09-27.
- **Q3 — Is the dive/return geometry in scope?** — Answer (producer, interactive): "3. a" → keep the current diagonal dive and the straight glide from the dive target to the current slot. **Partially superseded**: the dive and pause stay; the glide back is removed.

### 2026-09-27 producer exchanges (current authority)

- Q (Map): "Is the whole enemy unit re-anchored to the attack-end location, or do only the returning Divers re-form among themselves while the rest of the cluster stays put?" — Answer (producer): *"yes, that's what I want"* — the whole enemy unit re-anchors to the Diver's attack-end location and re-forms around it (the other enemies shift to keep their relative offsets around the new anchor). Final: whole-unit re-anchor. Source: comment `AH-C0MUKD1JVC004PR7D`.
- Q (Map): "Do the Divers return to a formation slot at all?" — Answer (producer): *"No, there is NO return target. They do not return. They simply go back to their unit formation (relative to one another's position) around the location their attack finished."* Final: no return target. Source: comment `AH-C0MUKCONWH000U5XG`.
- Research note: the dive target is the player's live position (`setAimTarget(player.x, player.y)` in `GymFormationScene` line ~1325 and `PlayScene` line ~1126), snapshotted in `Diver._startDive()`. The re-anchor therefore follows the player's snapshotted position, not a fixed screen point.

### Resolved during re-planning

- **RESOLVED 1 — vertical component of the re-anchor.** Q (agent): "The confirmed re-anchor target seems to be the player's position; my draft assumed that was fixed at the screen bottom and would drag the wave down." Answer (producer, 2026-09-28): *"The player moves, why would you assume that they are always on the bottom?"* Research: `Diver._startDive()` snapshots `this.target`, which both scenes refresh every frame from `player.x`/`player.y` (`GymFormationScene` line ~1325, `PlayScene` line ~1126) — the attack-end is the player's dive-start position wherever that is. The concern was unfounded. **Final: Option A — re-anchor on both axes to the (moving) attack-end location.**

### Open question

- **OPEN QUESTION 2 — desynchronised Divers (directed to the producer, non-blocking).** Assumed rule: the most recent attack-end wins. Confirm or specify.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-09-26 — `/skill:plan` auto-complete pass against the original freeze brief (stage → `plan_complete`).
- 2026-09-27 — producer rejected the freeze design (comments `AH-C0MUKC0FG9000J5KT`, `AH-C0MUKCBB98008FTSW`, `AH-C0MUKCONWH000U5XG`, `AH-C0MUKD1JVC004PR7D`); item reopened (`status=open`, `stage=intake_complete`).
- 2026-09-28 — `/skill:plan` re-plan (session `herdr-1790581007-375045-9534`): rewrote the brief and ACs to the producer's re-anchor specification; removed the superseded freeze ACs; documented the superseded intake answers. Raised a vertical-component question, then **resolved** it after the producer pointed out the target is the moving player, not a fixed screen bottom (Option A: both axes). Stage advanced to `plan_complete`.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MTECNI8K008FSKH** – Implement: Core scene — enemy live aim tracking (completed)
- **AH-0MUE2MG91005XHA8** – Tests: Config store (in-memory registry, boot load, dev write) (completed)
- **AH-0MTFP7EIC004F1MN** – Enemy Design tooling (completed)

# Speed Power Up Should Increase All Speeds

## Problem statement

The P5 Speed Boost power-up currently increases only the player ship's movement speed (thrust and max-speed) by 50 %. It does **not** affect rate of fire, so an active Speed Boost does not deliver the intended "all speeds" boost. This change extends P5 so it increases the player's rate of fire as well as their movement speed, and updates the GDD and related descriptions to match.

## Users

- **Player** — when collecting a Speed Boost (P5), expects both faster movement and faster firing for the 10-second duration.
  - *"As a player, when I collect a Speed Boost (P5) I expect to move 50 % faster **and** fire 50 % faster for 10 seconds."*
- **Game designer / producer** — expects the Game Design Document to describe P5 accurately as affecting all speeds.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1** — With P5 active, the player's **rate of fire increases by 50 %** (effective fire interval `fireRateMs` is scaled by `1 / 1.5`, i.e. the ship fires 1.5 × as often) in the playable game (`PlayScene`).
- **AC2** — The fire-rate multiplier is applied **live every frame** and returns to 1 immediately when P5 expires; re-collecting P5 refreshes the full 10 s duration (never additive); an active P5 continues to apply through a respawn.
- **AC3** — Movement speed and rate of fire derive from a **single source of truth** in `EffectsRegistry` (one P5 multiplier value of 1.5), and P5's duration, multiplier value and registry semantics are otherwise unchanged.
- **AC4** — **Gym parity:** every gym scene that can obtain P5 applies the same P5 multipliers as the game — `GymPowerUpsUtility` (round-robin P5 drop) and the shared `GymFormationScene` (P5 via the hold-full choice, inherited by the combat gyms). This includes applying the **movement** multiplier wherever it is currently missing, so gyms remain the parity reference for both speeds.
- **AC5** — **Unit tests** cover: P5 active → effective fire rate boosted / cooldown scaled; P5 expired → fire rate back to normal; re-collect refreshes duration; multiplier is non-additive and survives respawn.
- **AC6** — **Documentation updated:** the GDD P5 entry states that the Speed Boost increases movement speed **and** rate of fire by 50 % for 10 s; module doc comments (`effects.ts`, `types.ts`), power-up `description` strings and README references are updated to match. (CHANGELOG.md is excluded — managed by the ship skill release pipeline.)
- **AC7** — **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- P5 duration (10 s) and multiplier value (1.5 ×) must not change; the registry remains the single authority for the multiplier.
- The registry module must stay engine-agnostic (no Phaser imports).
- Gyms must always match the game (producer-confirmed principle) — do not implement the game change without the matching gym change.
- GDD is currently the only spec that describes P5; it must be updated as part of this work (no separate spec to change).

## Existing state

- `EffectsRegistry.speedMultiplier()` (src/powerups/effects.ts) returns `P5_SPEED_MULTIPLIER` (1.5) while P5 is active, else 1. It is the single authority for P5.
- `Player.setSpeedMultiplier()` (src/entities/Player.ts) scales `thrust` and `maxSpeed` about the base config; friction is untouched.
- `Player.tryFire(dt)` (src/entities/Player.ts) advances per-weapon cooldowns using the raw `getWeaponById(weaponId).fireRateMs` — **no multiplier is applied**.
- `CombatScene._autoFire(dt)` (src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts) calls `player.tryFire(dt)` and spawns bullets for the returned weapon ids.
- `PlayScene` tick applies `player.setSpeedMultiplier(this.effectsRegistry.speedMultiplier())` but nothing for fire rate.
- `GymPowerUpsUtility` applies `setSpeedMultiplier(...)` each frame but no fire-rate multiplier.
- GDD §4.4 (docs/Game Design Document.md) P5 row: *"Increases movement speed by 50 % for 10 seconds"* — movement only.

## Desired change

1. Add a P5 fire-rate multiplier accessor to `EffectsRegistry` (e.g. `fireRateMultiplier()` returning `P5_SPEED_MULTIPLIER` while active, else 1). Keep a single constant so movement and fire rate cannot diverge.
2. Extend `Player` to accept and apply a live fire-rate multiplier in `tryFire(dt)` (scale the effective interval/cooldown), mirroring `setSpeedMultiplier` and re-applied every frame.
3. Wire the multiplier into `PlayScene` tick alongside the existing speed-multiplier application, and into the gym scene(s) that collect P5.
4. Update the GDD P5 entry, `effects.ts` / `types.ts` doc comments, power-up `description` strings and README references.
5. Add unit tests at the registry, `Player` and scene levels.

**Assumption (documented, producer-confirmed direction):** "increase rate of fire by 50 %" is interpreted as an effective **1.5 × fire rate** — the fire interval is divided by 1.5 (`fireRateMs / 1.5`), so the ship fires 50 % more often per unit time. This matches the movement multiplier so "all speeds" scale identically.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — Add `fireRateMultiplier()` (or equivalent) returning the P5 multiplier; update P5 doc comment.
- `src/powerups/types.ts` — Update P5 `description` string to mention rate of fire.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — Add live fire-rate multiplier state + application in `tryFire()`.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — Apply the fire-rate multiplier each tick (alongside `setSpeedMultiplier`).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.ts` — Apply the fire-rate multiplier each tick (gym parity).
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — Apply the P5 movement + fire-rate multipliers (P5 reachable via the hold-full choice); closes the pre-existing movement-parity gap.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — Possibly route the multiplier through `_autoFire` if the Player API is not the chosen seam.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — Update P5 row/description.
- `README.md` — Update power-up summary reference if it mentions P5 movement-only.
- Tests: `src/powerups/effects.test.ts`, `src/entities/Player.test.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.test.ts`.

## Related work

- **AH-0MU8QURXB008DWM7** — "PlayScene: apply P5 Speed Boost multiplier live" (completed, shipped v0.1.4). Added the movement-speed application to PlayScene; **rate of fire was explicitly not included**, which is the gap this item closes.
- **AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1** — "Document gym-parity principle in AGENTS.md" (discovered-from:AH-0MUAYB9JS0025YUB). Verification found the gym-parity rule is **not** stated in the repo-local `AGENTS.md`; this follow-up adds it.
- Parent epic context: AH-0MU8QTLYN003JV8M (Playable game fine-tuning, if applicable).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk:** "all speeds" could be read to include bullet speed, enemy drift, etc. Scope is bounded to **player movement speed + player rate of fire** only; anything wider becomes a linked follow-up work item, not scope here.
- **Interpretation risk:** multiplying rate vs dividing interval. Mitigation: document the 1.5 ×-rate interpretation explicitly (above) and cover it with a test asserting the effective cooldown.
- **Gym divergence risk:** if the multiplier is applied only in `PlayScene`, gyms drift from the game. Mitigation: AC4 + the shared registry accessor make parity mechanical.
- **Respawn interaction:** multiplier must be re-applied each frame (not cached at collect time) so it survives respawn and expiry — covered by AC2/AC5.
- **Pre-existing gym gap:** `GymFormationScene` can collect P5 (hold-full choice) but never applied the movement multiplier even before this item. AC4 folds that fix in as part of parity; if it proves non-trivial it can be split into a linked follow-up.
- **Assumption:** no dedicated balance config value is needed; P5 keeps the existing single 1.5 constant for both axes.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MTAFH1ZF003EGDF** – Add ship deceleration when no inputs, with slider to control deceleration rate (completed)
- **AH-0MUDYS2SZ004H123** – Asteroids spawn randomly offscreen (open)
- **AH-0MU7JTEA6002GE37** – Playable game — fine-tuning and follow-up fixes (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: contexthub, fire, hell, increase, item, movement, power, project, rate, should, speed, speeds, well, work
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: fire, hell, increase, item, movement, power, project, rate, should, speed, speeds, well, work
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: belongs, fire, hell, item, movement, power, project, rate, should, speed, work

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1: Does P5 Speed Boost increase fire rate?** — Answer (Producer, interactive reply, 2026-09-25): *"Confirmed - all speeds, update documentation and descriptions."* The GDD previously described movement only; this is a confirmed design change, and docs/descriptions are to be updated. Source: interactive reply in session.
- **Q2: By what factor?** — Answer (Producer, interactive reply, 2026-09-25): *"Yes"* confirming the same 50 % (1.5 ×) factor as movement speed. Source: interactive reply in session.
- **Q3: Should gym scenes match the game? Is the gym-parity principle clear in the repo-local AGENTS.md?** — Answer (Producer, interactive reply, 2026-09-25): *"yes - gym scenes should always match the game. This should be clear in the local AGENTS.md - verify it is clear."* Research: `grep -ni 'gym\|parity\|reference' AGENTS.md` found **no** gym-parity guidance, so the principle is **not** clear. Discovered work created: **AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1** "Document gym-parity principle in AGENTS.md" (docs, discovered-from:AH-0MUAYB9JS0025YUB). This item therefore applies the parity requirement directly in AC4.
- **Prior related answer (context):** AH-0MU8QURXB008DWM7 comment (agent `pi`, 2026-09-21): *"Confirm whether rate-of-fire is already included."* — verified in code that it was **not** included; this item addresses it.

# Intake Brief — Asteroids drop collectable minerals that fill the ship's hold and grant a power-up choice

## Problem statement

Destroying a small asteroid currently only awards score and (for large/medium rocks) splits them; it never yields a collectable resource. We want destroyed small asteroids to leave behind **minerals** — small gold dots — that are collected by flying into them (by the player ship or by a non-asteroid enemy). Player collection fills a **ship's hold** (mineral store); when the hold is full the game pauses and offers **three power-ups**, one of which the player keeps **permanently for the run** (until death). Enemy collection builds a per-enemy mineral count that is partly spilled back as fresh minerals when that enemy is destroyed.

## Users

**Primary user — the player** during a PlayScene run (and in the new asteroids-only gym).

- *As a player, I want destroyed asteroids to drop collectable minerals, so that clearing rocks feels rewarding and feeds a progression loop.*
- *As a player, I want a visible hold counter, so that I know how close I am to my next reward.*
- *As a player, when my hold is full, I want to choose one of three power-ups to keep for the rest of the run, so that mineral gathering compounds into a build.*
- *As a player, I want enemies to be able to steal minerals and spill them on death, so that mineral gathering is contested and tactical.*

**Secondary users — developers/QA** validating the mechanic in the gym index.

- *As a developer, I want an asteroids-only mineral gym, so that I can observe drop/collect/re-drop and the hold-full choice in isolation.*
- *As a developer, I want the mechanic tunable through the game-rules config, so that balance can be adjusted without code changes.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Mineral drop on small-asteroid destruction.** Destroying a `small` asteroid spawns one or more **mineral** drops (small gold dots) at the destruction site; `large`/`medium` destructions do not themselves spawn minerals (their split children, once `small`, do). Minerals are **not** hit by bullets and cause **no damage or collision response** on contact with the player or an enemy.
- **AC2 — Player collection fills the hold.** Flying the player ship into a mineral removes it and increases the ship's mineral store by the configured collection amount (default **1**), up to the configured capacity (default **20**); the store is shown on the HUD (e.g. `Minerals: n/20`).
- **AC3 — Enemy collection and re-drop.** Every **non-asteroid** enemy that overlaps a mineral absorbs it (mineral removed, no damage) and increments that enemy's tracked mineral count; when that enemy is destroyed, **25–50 %** (configurable) of its collected count is re-spawned as individual mineral drops scattered at the explosion site.
- **AC4 — Hold-full power-up choice.** When the mineral store reaches capacity, the game pauses and a modal overlay presents **three distinct** power-up options; selecting one applies it to the player as a **permanent effect for the current run** (including weapon drops, which do not expire as they normally do), resumes play, and **resets the store to 0 carrying any overflow** (store = collected − capacity).
- **AC5 — Pluggable selection strategy.** The three offered options come from a pluggable strategy interface; the default implementation is a **random selection across the full existing drop pool (P3–P9 plus weapon drops)**, drawing distinct entries. Swapping the strategy requires no change to the choice scene or PlayScene wiring.
- **AC6 — Tunability.** Collection amount (default 1), hold capacity (default 20), and the re-drop fraction range (default 25–50 %) are read from the game-rules config (`src/core/rules.ts`) with sensible defaults and corrupt-config fallback, matching the existing rules pattern.
- **AC7 — Asteroids-only mineral gym.** A new gym scene (asteroids only) is registered in the gym index and demonstrates: small-asteroid mineral drops, player hold fill, HUD counter, enemy collection, re-drop on enemy death, and the hold-full choice overlay. Existing gym scenes spawn **100 random mineral drops on initialisation**.
- **AC8 — Testing/validation.** The mechanic is covered by meaningful automated tests (mineral lifecycle/collection rules, enemy count + re-drop distribution bounds, hold overflow arithmetic, choice-strategy distinctness and permanence, scene wiring) with coverage reported; the full project test suite passes with the new changes.
- **AC9 — Documentation.** GDD (§4.4/§4.5/§6.4 as appropriate) and README are updated to describe minerals, the hold, enemy collection/re-drop, the choice overlay and the new gym; code comments added on new modules.
- **AC10 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- Reuse the existing drop infrastructure where sensible (the `PowerUp` grow/hold/shrink lifecycle, `EffectsRegistry`, spawner/placement modules, `HUD`, `icons`, audio cues) rather than forking it.
- All new numeric values default to the operator-stated values (collection **1**, capacity **20**, re-drop **25–50 %**) and are configurable via `src/core/rules.ts` with corrupt-JSON fallback, mirroring the existing pattern.
- The choice overlay must pause gameplay at the SceneManager level (mirroring `PauseScene`) so no further collection/damage occurs while choosing.
- Permanence is scoped to the run: chosen power-ups and the mineral store reset on death/restart (they do **not** persist across `GameState.startGame()` or into the leaderboard).
- UK English throughout; do not edit `.pi/`, `skill/`, or agent-infrastructure directories.

## Existing state

- `src/entities/Asteroid.ts` — three tiers (`large`/`medium`/`small`); large/medium split into two smaller rocks; small destroys cleanly; 1 HP; never fires; `PlayScene._splitAsteroid` registers children with `WaveManager`.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_onEnemyKilled` awards score and rolls a power-up drop (`_maybeDropPowerUp`, ~15–20 %); drops are only collectable by the player; `_hitPlayer` handles shield absorb / life loss.
- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts` — common enemy container with `destroySelf()`/`destroy()`; no per-enemy resource state today.
- `src/powerups/PowerUp.ts` — grow→hold→shrink→despawn lifecycle, >3 % collection gate; `spawner.ts` has `RoundRobinSpawner`/`WeightedRandomSpawner`; `placement.ts` avoids overlaps.
- `src/powerups/types.ts` — P3–P9 plus weapon drops (spread/dual/rapid/reset); `effects.ts` holds the `EffectsRegistry` (timed P3/P5/P6, instant P4, stacking P7/P9, permanent-life P8, timed weapons).
- `src/core/GameState.ts` — run state (`lives`, `score`, `level`, `bossDefeated`, `gameState`) with `startGame()` reset; the natural home for a mineral store.
- `src/core/rules.ts` — persisted game-rules config (spawn interval + drop weights) with `loadRules()`/`saveRules()`; the pattern to follow for new tunables.
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — standalone HUD rendering lives and one row per active effect/weapon.
- `src/scenes/PauseScene.ts` — the existing modal-overlay pattern (SceneManager pause + launched scene).
- Gym framework: `src/scenes/gym/` (`GymPowerUps`, `GymPowerUpsCombat`, `GymWeapons`, `GymEnemies`, `GymBoss`, `GymPlayer`, `core/GymFormationScene`) with index auto-discovery (`src/utils/gymDiscovery.ts`, `GymIndex.ts`). There is **no** asteroids gym today.
- No mineral/cargo/hold concept exists anywhere in the codebase or worklog.

## Desired change

1. **New `Mineral` collectable** — small gold dot, no bullet interaction, no damage; collected on overlap by player or a non-asteroid enemy; persists until collected.
2. **Small asteroids drop minerals** — spawned at the destruction site in `PlayScene._onEnemyKilled` when `getSizeTier() === 'small'`.
3. **Per-enemy mineral count** — `BaseEnemy` tracks collected minerals; all non-asteroid types absorb overlapping minerals; on destruction 25–50 % of the count is re-spawned as individual dots at the explosion site.
4. **Ship's hold** — `GameState` gains a mineral store + capacity; HUD shows the counter; player overlap adds the configured amount.
5. **Hold-full choice** — a paused modal overlay offers three distinct power-ups; the chosen effect is permanent for the run; the store resets with overflow carried.
6. **Pluggable choice strategy** — an interface with a default random-across-all-drops implementation.
7. **Config tunables** — collection amount, capacity, re-drop fraction range in `rules.ts`.
8. **Asteroids-only mineral gym** — new gym scene + index registration; existing gyms pre-seed 100 random minerals on init.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/entities/Mineral.ts` — **New.** Gold-dot collectable: visual, spawn-at, player/enemy overlap semantics, no bullet/damage behaviour.
- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts` — Per-enemy mineral count, `collectMineral()`, and a re-drop count/position helper called on destruction.
- `src/core/GameState.ts` — Mineral store, capacity, `addMinerals()`/overflow arithmetic, reset on `startGame()`.
- `src/core/rules.ts` — New tunables: `mineralCollectAmount`, `mineralHoldCapacity`, `mineralRedropMin`/`mineralRedropMax` (+ defaults/merge).
- `src/core/constants.ts` — Mineral visual/size/depth constants (canonical values).
- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — **New.** Pluggable `PowerUpChoiceStrategy` interface + default random-across-all-drops implementation.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — Support marking a chosen effect permanent for the run (no timer decrement / never expires).
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — Permanent weapon equipping (a chosen weapon does not time out).
- `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` — **New.** Paused modal overlay offering three picks (mirrors `PauseScene` navigation).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — Wire mineral spawn on small-asteroid kill, player/enemy overlap collection, re-drop on enemy death, hold-full → launch choice, store reset/overflow.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymMinerals.ts` — **New.** Asteroids-only gym demonstrating the full mechanic.
- `src/scenes/gym/` (existing scenes / `core/GymFormationScene.ts`) — Seed 100 random mineral drops on init.
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — Mineral store row (`Minerals: n/20`).
- `src/utils/gymDiscovery.ts` / `src/scenes/GymIndex.ts` — Register the new gym scene.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` / `README.md` — Document the mechanic and gym.

## Related work

- **AH-0MU8BZ2ZM004J47F** — *Asteroids as an enemy* (parent of the asteroid implementation; mineral drops extend its destruction flow).
- **AH-0MU44M9NQ0006613** — *Collect drops with effects and HUD* (the drop-collection + HUD pattern to reuse).
- **AH-0MTCNZPHN003C5E1** — *Power-up core lifecycle + tunable constants* (the `PowerUp` lifecycle to reuse).
- **AH-0MTCNZX16007ECPS** — *Power-up catalogue + effects (P5, P8, P9)* (the effect registry the permanent choice builds on).
- **AH-0MU9LPZ0G0015292** — *In-game menu* (the `PauseScene` overlay pattern to mirror for the choice modal).
- **AH-0MTVYCM2N002NKE4** — *Player pickup pickups as soon as they touch* (pickup-on-contact semantics).
- **AH-0MUAYB3OU0087H9W** — *Collected powerups need some feel* (related collection feedback/juice).
- **AH-0MTCPL9NA0025ZUI** — *In-Game spawning should not be round robin* (weighted drop pool used by the default choice strategy).
- **AH-0MU6VSKZT006HBTR** — *Leaderboard: game-over score entry and localStorage display* (run-scoped state reset interaction).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk:** mineral-based progression could expand into trading/upgrades/economy. This brief is limited to drop → collect → hold → one permanent power-up choice; further economy ideas should become linked work items, not scope here.
- **Assumption:** minerals are stationary (no drift/despawn) and persist until collected; no lifetime is specified. If drift/lifetime is desired it will be added as a tunable.
- **Assumption:** the one mineral per small-asteroid destruction count is configurable via a drop-amount tunable (default 1) rather than a random range.
- **Assumption:** "permanent until death" means the chosen effect persists for the run and resets with the rest of `GameState`; it is not written to the leaderboard.
- **Assumption:** the three offered options are guaranteed distinct; if the pool cannot supply three distinct entries it degrades gracefully (fewer options).
- **Risk:** pausing for the choice mid-wave could interact with wave timers/invulnerability timers; the overlay must use SceneManager pause (as `PauseScene` does) so all timers freeze consistently.
- **Risk:** making selected weapons permanent touches `Player`/`EffectsRegistry` semantics that the existing `WeaponEffect` timer model assumes; tests must lock the "chosen weapon never expires" behaviour.

## Open Questions

None outstanding — all three interview rounds answered (see Appendix).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

**Round 1**

- **Q1: What should happen when an enemy touches a mineral?** — Answer (operator, interactive reply): Keep a **count** of how many minerals the enemy has collected; when the enemy is destroyed, **25–50 %** of them are left behind by the explosion (as individual drops).
- **Q2: Which asteroid tiers drop minerals, and how many?** — Answer (operator, interactive reply): **Small asteroids only**.
- **Q3: Where do the three offered power-ups come from?** — Answer (operator, interactive reply): Make the selection process **pluggable**, starting with a **random selection across all power-ups (including weapons)**.

**Round 2**

- **Q4: Enemy collection scope and re-drop shape?** — Answer (operator, interactive reply): **All enemy types except asteroids** collect; the re-drop is **individual dots**; (asteroids are excluded from collecting, so split-child inheritance does not apply).
- **Q5: Choice presentation, hold reset, permanence?** — Answer (operator, interactive reply): (a) the game **pauses** with a modal overlay; (b) the hold **resets to 0 with overflow held**; (c) the chosen power-up is **permanent for the run even if normally timed**, and the three options are distinct.
- **Q6: Scope and tunability?** — Answer (operator, interactive reply): a **new asteroids-only gym scene**; **existing gym scenes should have 100 random mineral drops when initialised**; the tunable-via-`rules.ts` and HUD-counter assumptions were **confirmed**.

# Pop SFX: playPowerUpCollectPopSound()

## Headline
Add a short percussive pop sound to src/audio/effects.ts, distinct from the existing two-tone ascending chime (playPowerUpCollectSound()). It is played whenever a power-up drop is collected.

## Problem statement
Power-up collection currently uses playPowerUpCollectSound() -- a cheerful two-tone ascending chime. The producer wants a genuinely pop-like sound that is audibly distinct from this chime.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 -- Sound design: playPowerUpCollectPopSound() is a short (<= 100 ms) percussive pop, synthetically distinct from playPowerUpCollectSound(). The wave type and frequency contour must be clearly different.
- AC2 -- Safe no-op: Without an AudioContext (headless tests), the function degrades to a safe no-op -- no throw.
- AC3 -- Unit test: A test in src/audio/effects.test.ts asserts the function exists, is callable, and that it produces the expected synthesis parameters (wave type, frequency contour, duration, volume <= 0.2) against a mock AudioContext.
- AC4 -- Distinct from other cues: The pop is distinguishable from the collection chime and all other audio cues by wave type or frequency contour.

## Key Files

- src/audio/effects.ts -- Add playPowerUpCollectPopSound() function.
- src/audio/effects.test.ts -- Add unit test for the pop cue (mock + no-op paths).

# Absorb Animation Module: shared collectAnimation.ts with unit tests

## Headline
Create a new shared module src/powerups/collectAnimation.ts that exposes:
1. A pure-logic state-stepper function (move drop position toward ship, shrink scale, morph/shear over a tunable duration)
2. A thin Phaser-facing entry point (spawn an animation on a Graphics object, update it per frame, destroy on completion)

## Problem statement
On collection, drops currently have their Graphics destroyed immediately. We need a reusable animation that makes drops visually suck into the ship -- position converges on the ship, scale shrinks to zero, and the shape/shear morphs during the animation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 -- Pure state stepper: stepCollectAnimation(state, shipX, shipY, dt) advances position toward the ship using linear interpolation (lerp), shrinks scale toward 0, and applies a shear/morph rotation. All inputs and outputs are plain objects -- no Phaser types.
- AC2 -- Tunable parameters: The animation has a configurable duration (default target <= 0.3 s), speed constant, and the step function is deterministic given the same inputs.
- AC3 -- Phaser entry point: spawnCollectAnimation(graphics, dropX, dropY, shipX, shipY, duration) creates and returns a handle with update(dt), isComplete(), and destroy() methods. The Graphics object is destroyed on completion.
- AC4 -- Morph/shear: During animation, the drop shape is morphed (shear/rotation) to evoke the impression of being sucked/elongated toward the ship. This is a single generic treatment for all drop types.
- AC5 -- Unit tests: Tests cover position convergence, scale shrink, shear progression, completion detection, and safe no-op when Graphics is null.
- AC6 -- Reuse pattern: The module mirrors the architecture of src/powerups/magnet.ts (pure logic + scene seam) and src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts (pure state + thin Phaser entry point).

## Key Files

- src/powerups/collectAnimation.ts -- New file: pure step function + Phaser entry point.
- src/powerups/collectAnimation.test.ts -- New test file: convergence, scale, morph, completion.

# PlayScene: wire absorb animation + pop SFX into collection path

## Headline
Wire the new pop SFX and absorb animation into PlayScene._collectDrop so that collection provides immediate tactile feedback.

## Problem statement
PlayScene._collectDrop currently: applies the effect, destroys the drop's Graphics immediately, then plays the pickup cue. We need to replace the immediate destroy with starting the absorb animation and playing the pop SFX.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 -- Gameplay effect fires immediately: The effect (registry apply, lives update, P4 bullet clear) fires on the same frame as overlap, exactly as today.
- AC2 -- Pop SFX plays immediately: playPowerUpCollectPopSound() is called on collection alongside the existing per-type pickup cue.
- AC3 -- Absorb animation starts: spawnCollectAnimation() is called with the drop's current position and the ship's world position. The drop's Graphics stays alive and is updated each frame by the animation.
- AC4 -- Drop destroyed on animation complete: When the absorb animation completes, the drop's Graphics is destroyed and the drop is removed from the active drops array.
- AC5 -- No double-apply: The drop is marked as absorbing so the overlap gate does not re-collect it during the animation.
- AC6 -- Unit test: Extend PlayScene tests to verify the absorb animation starts on collection, the pop SFX plays, and the drop is cleaned up after animation.

## Key Files

- src/scenes/PlayScene.ts -- Modify _collectDrop to start animation instead of destroy; add frame update for animation; add pop SFX call.
- src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts -- Extend collection tests for absorb animation and pop cue.

# Reusable in-canvas focus manager (AH-0MU9LKQEP008LCX9-C1)

## Summary

Create the reusable in-canvas focus manager that tracks focusable controls, cycles focus on Tab/arrow keys, activates on Enter/Space, renders a visible focus style, and cleans up on shutdown.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1:** Focus manager exposes `register(control, actionCallback)` and `unregister(control)` APIs.
- **AC2:** On registration, the first control is focused by default.
- **AC3:** Tab cycles forward through registered controls with wrap-around; Shift+Tab cycles backward.
- **AC4:** Arrow keys (up/down for vertical, left/right for horizontal — configurable) cycle focus with wrap-around.
- **AC5:** Enter and Space activate the focused control by invoking its action callback.
- **AC6:** The focused control receives a visible focus style (brighter colour + highlight border); unfocused controls restore their prior style.
- **AC7:** `shutdown()` removes all keyboard event listeners and clears the registry.
- **AC8:** Unit tests cover: default focus, Tab/Shift+Tab cycling (including wrap), arrow-key cycling (including wrap), Enter/Space activation, and shutdown cleanup.

## Key Files

- `src/utils/focusManager.ts` (new) — FocusManager class with register/unregister, keyboard handling, focus styling, shutdown.
- `src/utils/focusManager.test.ts` (new) — Unit tests for all ACs above.

## Dependencies

- None (core utility, implemented first)

## Test: Asteroid behaviour during the transition period (Phase 2)

**Related to:** AH-0MU8TWF1H007OG2L — Asteroids should not explode when time runs out, instead carry them over

**Goal:** Verify that carried-over asteroids keep moving, remain shootable, and can ram the player during the level/wave transition period, while non-asteroid enemy movement/fire stays suspended.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

1. During the transition (`transitionTimer > 0`), a carried-over asteroid continues to move (its position changes across ticks in line with its velocity).
2. During the transition, a player bullet overlapping a carried-over asteroid destroys it (`getAliveCount()` decreases and the asteroid's `alive` flag is false).
3. During the transition, player-asteroid overlap costs the player one life.
4. During the transition, non-asteroid enemy movement/fire remains suspended and enemy-bullet-vs-player collisions do not occur.
5. After the transition completes, normal gameplay resumes with any un-destroyed carried-over asteroids still present.

**Implementation approach:**
- Add `it()` cases in `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`
- Boot a play scene, force a wave timeout so an asteroid carries over into the transition, then tick through the transition:
  - Assert position/velocity continuity
  - Fire a player bullet at the asteroid during the transition and assert it is destroyed
  - Move the player onto the asteroid during the transition and assert a life is lost
  - Assert suspended enemy behaviour is unchanged

**Key Files:**
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — add new test cases

**Phase:** 2 of 3 (transition-period asteroid behaviour)

**Depends on:** Phase 1 implementation
