# CSV codec: RFC 4180 parser, serialiser, typed coercion, validation

Implement the CSV codec module (`src/core/csv.ts`) that parses flat CSV rows into typed `EnemyConfig` / `ShipConfig` objects and serialises them back.

**Context:**

The codec is the foundation of the CSV-based configuration system. It is used by the boot loader (to parse committed CSVs), the Vite plugin (to validate writes), and the config store (to re-read after writes). It must be dependency-free and hand-rolled (no new runtime dependencies).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Parser.** `parseCsvRows(csv: string): Record<string, string>[]` parses an RFC 4180 CSV string with a header row into an array of objects. Empty rows and comment lines (starting with `#`) are skipped. A leading BOM (U+FEFF) is stripped.

2. **Serialiser.** `serializeEnemyConfigs(configs: EnemyConfig[]): string` and `serializeShipConfig(config: ShipConfig): string` produce a CSV string with a header row and one row per config. Output round-trips through `parseCsvRows` → coercion. Colours are formatted as `0xRRGGBB`.

3. **RFC 4180 quoting.** Fields containing commas, double-quotes, or newlines are wrapped in double quotes, with internal quotes escaped as `""`. The parser reverses this correctly.

4. **Typed coercion.** `coerceEnemyConfig(row, defaults)` and `coerceShipConfig(row, defaults)` convert raw string values to typed fields: numbers via `Number(...)`, enums validated against `EnemyFormationKind` / `EnemyShotPattern` / `ControlScheme`, colours via `parseInt(value, 16)`.

5. **Validation.** A validator returns a typed result `{ ok: boolean; errors: string[] }`. Missing required fields, malformed numbers, invalid enums, and invalid hex colours are reported. Coercion falls back to `defaults` for every invalid field — never produces `undefined`, `NaN`, or an invalid enum.

6. **Column mapping.** A documented, stable column order per config type (exported as constants) maps CSV headers to typed fields. Unknown headers are ignored; missing headers fall back to defaults.

7. **No runtime dependencies.** The codec uses only the TypeScript/JavaScript standard library.

**Key Files:**

- `src/core/csv.ts` — new codec module (to be created).
- `src/core/enemyConfig.ts` — `EnemyConfig`, enums, `DEFAULT_ENEMY_CONFIGS`.
- `src/core/config.ts` — `ShipConfig`, `ControlScheme`, `DEFAULT_CONFIG`.

**Dependencies:**

- `src/core/csv.test.ts` — the codec test suite (created by the sibling "Tests: CSV codec" task; implementation must make those tests pass).

**Deliverables:**

- `src/core/csv.ts` — the CSV codec implementation.
- Exported column-order constants for enemy and ship configs.

# Leaderboard entry screen should show position in table

**Issue type:** feature · **Priority:** medium

> **Original request (preserved):** "When entering a high score into the
> leaderboard the leaderboard display the position of the players score in the
> leaderboard, filling in the initials as they are typed. Highlight that line
> somehow."

## Problem statement

On game over, a qualifying player types their three initials but receives no
feedback about where their score will land until they submit and return to the
menu. The ranked table on the game-over screen stays static, so the player
cannot tell whether the run is about to rank #1 or #10.

## Users

- An arcade player who has just finished a run and is entering their initials on
  the game-over screen.

  > **User story:** As a player entering my initials after a high score, I want
  > to see my score inserted into the leaderboard at the position it will take,
  > with my initials filling in live and my row highlighted, so that I know how
  > well I did before I commit.

## Existing state

- `GameOverScene` (`src/scenes/GameOverScene.ts`) renders a static leaderboard
  via `renderLeaderboard` (`src/ui/leaderboardView.ts`) and prompts for
  3-letter initials using the shared `FocusManager`.
- `src/core/Leaderboard.ts` owns persistence and ranking
  (`getEntries`, `addEntry`, `isQualifying`, `MAX_ENTRIES = 10`); `rank` is
  recomputed on read and never trusted from storage.
- Keystrokes currently update only the initials field text; the table is not
  re-rendered, and there is no marker for the player's prospective position.
- `LeaderboardScene` (main menu) renders the same table through the shared
  helper and must remain unchanged.

## Desired change

While a **qualifying** score is being entered on the game-over screen:

1. Compute the prospective entry's rank from the current table and the final
   score.
2. Show the player's row at that rank **immediately on screen open**, with
   initials rendered as placeholders until typing begins (Q2 answer:
   immediately).
3. Fill in the initials live as they are typed and update the row on every A–Z
   key and Backspace.
4. Highlight the player's row with a distinct colour plus a leading marker
   (Q1 answer: option A).
5. When the table already holds 10 entries, insert the prospective row at its
   true rank and drop the current lowest entry, so at most 10 rows are shown
   (Q3 answer: insert and drop).
6. On submit, the persisted entry occupies the same rank the preview showed.
7. Non-qualifying scores show no prospective row (explanatory message
   unchanged).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Live prospective row shown immediately:** For a qualifying score,
  the game-over leaderboard shows exactly one row representing the player's
  prospective entry as soon as the screen opens, at the rank it will occupy.
  The row's initials render as placeholders until typing begins.
- [ ] **AC2 — Live initials:** Each A–Z key press and Backspace updates that
  row's initials immediately (typed letters shown, unfilled slots rendered as
  placeholders), before any submit.
- [ ] **AC3 — Highlight:** The prospective row is visually distinguishable from
  every other row by a distinct colour plus a leading marker (e.g. `▶`).
- [ ] **AC4 — Correct placement and cap:** The prospective row is inserted by
  score descending with the same stable tie-break as `Leaderboard.addEntry`;
  the table never shows more than `MAX_ENTRIES` (10) rows, and when full the
  current lowest entry is displaced.
- [ ] **AC5 — Qualifying only:** Non-qualifying scores render no prospective
  row and write nothing to storage.
- [ ] **AC6 — Submit consistency:** After submit, the persisted entry occupies
  the same rank shown by the preview.
- [ ] **AC7 — Regression:** `LeaderboardScene` (main-menu table) is unchanged
  and existing GameOverScene/Leaderboard tests continue to pass.
- [ ] **AC8 — Testing/validation:** New unit tests cover rank insertion
  (including equal-score ties and full-table displacement), immediate preview
  visibility before typing, live initials update, highlight marker/colour,
  Backspace-to-empty, and non-qualifying behaviour.
- [ ] **AC9 — Documentation:** All related documentation is updated to reflect
  the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs
  site entries.
- [ ] **AC10 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- Keyboard-only entry through `FocusManager` is retained; no on-screen
  keyboard is added.
- Reuse `src/ui/leaderboardView.ts` for rendering where practical so the
  game-over and main-menu tables stay consistent.
- `Leaderboard.ts` remains the single owner of ranking and persistence; a pure,
  testable helper for the prospective rank is preferred over duplicating sort
  logic in the scene.
- No new dependencies.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the prospective rank uses the same stable tie-break as
  `addEntry` — a new equal score ranks after existing equal-score entries.
- **Assumption:** the prospective row's date column shows today's ISO date
  (`todayISO()`), matching the eventual persisted entry.
- **Assumption:** highlighting applies only to the game-over entry screen; the
  main-menu `LeaderboardScene` table is unchanged.
- **Risk (scope creep):** extra polish (animation, sound, online leaderboard)
  is recorded as separate linked work items, not added to this scope.
- **Risk:** re-rendering rows on each keystroke could leak text objects; the
  implementation should destroy/replace preview rows rather than accumulate
  them.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/Leaderboard.ts` — add a pure helper to compute the prospective
  ranked preview (reusing the existing `sortAndRank` semantics).
- `src/ui/leaderboardView.ts` — support a highlighted/preview row in
  `renderLeaderboard` (or a sibling helper).
- `src/scenes/GameOverScene.ts` — render and refresh the prospective row on
  initials changes.
- `src/scenes/GameOverScene.test.ts` — tests for the preview behaviour.
- `src/ui/leaderboardView.test.ts` (new if no existing coverage) — tests for
  highlighted/preview row formatting.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §5 — document the live preview-row UX.
- `README.md` §Leaderboard — update the game-over description.

## Related work

- **Implement game-over qualifying, date and full leaderboard (AH-0MUD9ZOM4001LACR)**
  (completed) — built the game-over table this feature extends.
- **Test: Game-over leaderboard UX (AH-0MUD9ZNN30065ZLP)** (completed) —
  existing test coverage for the game-over leaderboard flow.
- **Keyboard entry / `FocusManager` work (AH-0MU9LKQEP008LCX9)** (completed) —
  initials-entry focus model reused here.
- **Implement GameOverScene — scoring, lives, game-over flow
  (AH-0MU731426003FE71)** (completed) — scene this feature modifies.
- **Implement Leaderboard persistence module (AH-0MUD9ZOAR0099DJZ)** (completed)
  — ranking API used for placement.
- **Docs: GDD and README leaderboard updates (AH-0MUD9ZP94006OYL4)**
  (completed) — docs to amend.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUGXDVPH005TIZL** – Create Dev Utilities gym scene with curve editor and wave preview (open)
- **AH-0MT7URFNN004Z01L** – Remove combo bonus from GDD and clarify lives model (completed)
- **AH-0MT7UTPH3001B6IE** – Settle engine selection on Phaser - remove engine options B and C from GDD (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: ac3, ac4, ac5, acceptance, add (+265 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, ac5 (+239 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: ac1, ac4, add, added, animation (+201 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

- **Q1 — Highlight treatment.** How should the player's prospective row be
  highlighted? Options: A) distinct colour plus a leading marker (e.g. `▶`);
  B) blinking/pulsing row; C) background panel behind the row; D) other.
  **Recommended:** A. — **Answer (producer, interactive reply):** "A".
- **Q2 — Preview visibility before typing.** Should the prospective row be
  visible immediately when a qualifying game-over screen opens (initials shown
  as placeholders), or only after the first letter is typed?
  **Recommended:** visible immediately. — **Answer (producer, interactive
  reply):** "immediately".
- **Q3 — Full-table behaviour.** When the table already holds 10 entries and
  the score qualifies, should the preview insert at its true rank and drop the
  current lowest entry (keeping 10 rows), or temporarily show an 11th row?
  **Recommended:** drop the lowest. — **Answer (producer, interactive reply):**
  "insert and drop".

# Diver docs stale: dive described as x-locked but implemented as diagonal (AH-0MUEI8HSU000QLEA)

## Problem statement

The Diver (E2) documentation still describes the dive as a **vertical drop with
x locked at the formation slot**, but the implemented and shipped behaviour
(AH-0MTGBOKLC006N8UX) is a **diagonal parabolic dive** toward the player
position snapshotted at dive start. The resulting docs contradict the code and
can mislead future implementation, tuning, and parity work.

## Users

- **Player / observer** — reads (or is described) the Diver as a predictable
  vertical threat; the real dive is diagonal toward the snapshotted player
  position, so the stated behaviour is wrong.
- **Developer / maintainer** — relies on `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`
  as the authoritative guide for enemy behaviour and gym/game parity; stale
  "x locked" wording risks re-introducing a vertical-only dive or mis-scoping
  related fixes.
- **Producer / reviewer** — needs the GDD and the implementation guide to agree
  on the dive contract so acceptance criteria for Diver work are unambiguous.

### Example user stories

- As a **developer**, I want the Diver documentation to describe the actual
  diagonal dive so that I do not implement or test against a vertical-only
  trajectory.
- As a **player-facing designer**, I want the GDD to state that a mid-dive aim
  change does not alter the in-flight arc, so the Diver's dodge window is
  understood correctly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Stale x-locked descriptions corrected:** The three known locations
  describe the dive as diagonal (both x and y follow the quadratic bezier from
  the formation slot to the player position snapshotted at dive start) and no
  longer state that x is locked:
  - `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §1 catalog row (E2, "Vertical dive
    toward player (x locked at formation slot)").
  - `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §7.3 (live aim tracking, "Dives are
    x-locked at the formation slot.").
  - `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.1 (E2 Diver, "Dives straight down toward
    the player (x locked at its formation slot — a vertical trajectory)").
- [ ] **AC2 — Snapshot semantics documented:** The docs state that the dive
  target is snapshotted at dive start, so a mid-dive aim change does not alter
  the in-flight arc (§7.3 already carries this; it must remain consistent and be
  reflected in the corrected dive description).
- [ ] **AC3 — No stale vertical-only/x-locked Diver statements remain:** A
  repository search of `docs/` for the Diver dive finds no remaining
  x-locked / vertical-only trajectory claims for E2; the correction is
  cross-referenced to the superseding work item AH-0MTGBOKLC006N8UX.
- [ ] **AC4 — All related documentation is updated:** The three locations above
  are updated consistently (including the GDD and the implementation guide), and
  any relevant code comments remain accurate — including the stale comment at
  `src/entities/Diver.test.ts:128-130` ("x is locked at the dive-start slot"),
  which the producer confirmed (OPEN QUESTION 1, answer (a)) is in scope as a
  **comment-only** edit (no assertion or behavioural change).
- [ ] **AC5 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Docs-only change** — no production code or runtime behaviour change; no test
  changes are expected. AC5 is a guard against accidental regressions. Exception
  (producer-confirmed, OPEN QUESTION 1 answer (a)): a **comment-only** edit to
  `src/entities/Diver.test.ts:128-130` is in scope under AC4 — no assertion or
  behavioural change.
- **Preserve existing documented semantics** — the formation-hold-while-away
  behaviour (`DIVING`/`PAUSING`/`RETURNING`, §7.6) and the "snapshot at dive
  start" seam decision are correct and must not be altered.
- **Keep GDD and implementation guide consistent** — both documents must describe
  the same dive contract; do not diverge or restate one as authoritative over the
  other without a reference.
- **Do not touch `CHANGELOG.md`** — it is managed by the ship skill's release
  pipeline.
- **No scope creep** — do not rewrite unrelated enemy documentation; record any

# Ship config controlScheme does not survive game server restart

## Problem statement

Saving the player ship's control scheme (e.g. **Asteroids**) from the Player gym scene writes the value to `src/data/ship-config.csv`, but restarting the game server (`npm run dev`) loads the built-in default (`fourDirectional`) instead of the persisted value, because the boot loader that reads the CSV is never actually invoked in the runtime path.

## Users

Developer/designer tuning the player ship in the gym, who expects a saved value to be the single source of truth across sessions.

- As a designer, I want to save `controlScheme=asteroids` in the Player gym and have it still be asteroids after restarting `npm run dev`, so that I do not have to re-apply my tuning every session.
- As a developer, I want the CSV documented as "read at boot" to actually be read at boot, so the documented persistence contract holds.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** — On application boot (dev and production), the config store is hydrated from the persisted CSV **before** any scene reads `loadShipConfig()` / `loadEnemyConfig()`. Verify: after saving `controlScheme=asteroids` in the Player gym and restarting `npm run dev`, the Player gym boots in Asteroids mode and `loadShipConfig().controlScheme === 'asteroids'`.
- **AC2** — A regression test fails against the current code and passes after the fix: it asserts the runtime boot path calls `loadConfigs()` (or the store is otherwise hydrated from CSV) before the first scene consumes the config; `loadShipConfig()` then reflects the CSV value rather than `DEFAULT_CONFIG`.
- **AC3** — Editing `src/data/ship-config.csv` by hand and restarting `npm run dev` yields the edited values (matches README "Configuration (CSV)" §Boot / §Editing by hand).
- **AC4** — Failure fallback is preserved: if the CSV fetch/read fails, the game still boots with built-in defaults and does not throw.
- **AC5** — A testing/validation criterion: automated tests cover the boot-hydration path (success and failure) and run in `npm test`.
- **AC6** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- **AC7** — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- No `localStorage` for config values — the committed CSV remains the single source of truth.
- `loadShipConfig()` / `loadEnemyConfig()` must remain **synchronous** for scene callers.
- `loadConfigs()` must never throw — a failed fetch falls back to built-in defaults so the game still boots.
- Production/static builds remain read-only (write path is dev-only and unchanged).
- Boot hydration must complete before scene construction so the first frame is correct (no flash of default scheme).

## Existing state

- `src/core/configStore.ts` defines `loadConfigs()` which fetches both CSVs (dev) or reads the bundled CSVs (production) and populates the in-memory registry.
- `loadConfigs()` is currently referenced only by the config-store tests (`configStore.test.ts`, `configStore.integration.test.ts`) — **it is never called from the runtime boot path** (`src/main.ts`, `src/core/Game.ts`, `src/core/gameConfig.ts`).
- `getRegistry()` lazily creates an empty registry whose `ship` is `DEFAULT_CONFIG` (`controlScheme: 'fourDirectional'`), so before `loadConfigs()` runs, `loadShipConfig()` returns the default.
- Saving from the gym (`GymPlayer._onSave` → `saveShipConfig`) writes the CSV **and updates the in-memory registry**, which is why the change works within the session but is lost on restart.
- The Vite dev-server plugin (`vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts`) writes the CSV atomically and the file on disk does contain the saved value (`git status` shows `M src/data/ship-config.csv`).
- README "Configuration (CSV)" documents that the store "reads both CSVs ... at startup" and that "edit a cell ... refresh `npm run dev` — the new values are live" — the documented contract is not met.

## Desired change

Wire the existing `loadConfigs()` into the application boot sequence so the CSV-backed registry is populated before the Phaser game and its scenes are constructed. The minimal fix is to make the entry point asynchronous: `await loadConfigs()` in `src/main.ts` before `new Game()` (or an equivalent async boot wrapper around `Game`), preserving the documented default-fallback behaviour.

Secondary (out of scope, tracked separately): the dev write path strips the `#` comment header from `src/data/ship-config.csv` on save, losing the human-readable column documentation. Reported as a discovered item, not part of this fix.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/main.ts` — Entry point; hydrate the config store (`await loadConfigs()`) before constructing `Game`.
- `src/core/Game.ts` — May need an async boot hook/wrapper if hydration is owned here instead of `main.ts`.
- `src/core/gameConfig.ts` — Builds the Phaser config; ensure hydration precedes scene registration/start.
- `src/core/config.ts` — Re-export `loadConfigs` if the entry point consumes the public config facade.
- `src/core/configStore.ts` — Existing `loadConfigs()`; confirm idempotence and non-throwing fallback remain intact.
- `src/main.test.ts` (new) or `src/core/Game.boot.test.ts` (new) — Regression test asserting boot hydration ordering.
- `README.md` — "Configuration (CSV)" section: confirm/adjust boot wording once the path is real.

## Related work

- `AH-0MTF0EFNZ000RPVD` — Alternative player control (introduced `controlScheme` + persistence; completed).
- `AH-0MTFRQR41000V57V` — Scheme-aware input routing in gym scenes (completed).
- `AH-0MTFRQR42001M8WQ` — Scheme-aware input tests for affected gym scenes (completed).
- `AH-0MTFPDKDU006QUDC` — Player cannot be moved in enemy and power-up gym scenes (consumes saved `controlScheme`; completed).
- `AH-0MTZWZ9TE009CVUA` — Create a CSV file to maintain enemy configurations (parent epic, open).
- `AH-0MUE2MGM0001XEH9` — CSV seed data files (parent task, open).
- `AH-0MUE2MGZM0016U3L` — Config store: in-memory registry, boot load, dev write (blocked; the "boot load" half is the deliverable this bug affects).
- `README.md` — "Configuration (CSV)" (`src/data/ship-config.csv`, boot contract, dev write path).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — ship movement/control scheme tuning.

### Automated related-work report

- **AH-0MTHG5K6O008BCNJ** – Docs and README for enemy config pipeline (completed)
- **AH-0MT7VE4SX0005A8V** – Add a Magnet power up (completed)
- **AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT** – Create gym scene for power-ups with spawning, collection, and standalone HUD (completed)

Repository file matches: `README.md`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, `docs/Game Design Document.md` (matched terms: config, csv, boot/loads, ship, scheme, save, restart, vite, plugin).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the only reason the restart loses the value is the missing `loadConfigs()` call; verified by grep (no runtime references) and the symptom match (in-session save updates the registry, restart does not).
- **Risk — boot sequencing:** adding `await` before game construction must not delay first paint unacceptably or break existing boot tests; mitigate by keeping the fetch fast and falling back to defaults without throwing.
- **Risk — test environment:** happy-dom/vitest do not have a real dev server; tests must mock `fetch` (the existing config-store tests already do this) — cover the boot path with the same seam.
- **Risk — scope creep:** comment-header stripping, and CSV edits not being live without a restart, are adjacent defects. Recorded as discovered items rather than folded into this fix.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q:** What exactly do you mean by "restart of the game server" — (a) stop/start `npm run dev`, (b) `npm run build && npm run preview`, (c) something else?
  **Answer (operator):** (a) stop/start `npm run dev`. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q:** When you say "That works" — does the Save button show a "Saved" confirmation, or "Save failed"?
  **Answer (operator):** confirmation. Source: interactive reply. Evidence: `GymPlayer._onSave` shows `Saved` when `saveShipConfig()` returns `ok: true`, which requires the dev PUT to succeed.
- **Q:** After the restart, does the ship default back to `fourDirectional`, or show some other unexpected behaviour?
  **Answer (operator):** back to default. Source: interactive reply.
- **Research summary:** `loadConfigs()` exists and is tested but is never invoked by `src/main.ts` / `src/core/Game.ts` / `src/core/gameConfig.ts`; `getRegistry()` falls back to `DEFAULT_CONFIG` (`fourDirectional`), so restart reverts to the default. The persisted CSV on disk does contain `asteroids`, confirming the write path works and the read path is the defect.

Saving ship (or enemy) config from the gym overwrites `src/data/ship-config.csv` with only the header row + data row, dropping the `#` comment block that documents every column, enum values, and how to add entries.

**Why it matters:** the committed CSVs are documented as the "single, human-editable source of truth" (README "Configuration (CSV)"). After the first gym save, the human-readable column documentation is lost, making the file harder to hand-edit.

**Reproduction:** open the Player gym, change any value, click Save. Inspect `src/data/ship-config.csv` — the leading `#` comment lines are gone (see the `M src/data/ship-config.csv` diff on the working tree).

**Suggested approach:** have the dev-server plugin preserve the original comment prefix when rewriting the file, or move the column documentation out of the CSV (e.g. README/schema) so it is not destroyed by writes.

# Set Asteroids as the default ship control scheme and accept headerless CSV seed format

## Problem statement

The Player gym `Save` writes `src/data/ship-config.csv` through the dev-server CSV plugin in a **headerless** form (no leading `#` comment block, no trailing newline) and with `controlScheme=asteroids`. The committed built-in `DEFAULT_CONFIG.controlScheme` is `fourDirectional`, so the seed tests fail:

- `src/data/csv-seed.test.ts` — header-comment assertion, `controlScheme` default mismatch, trailing-newline assertion.
- `src/core/configStore.integration.test.ts` — AC5 production fallback (`loadShipConfig()` no longer equals `DEFAULT_CONFIG`).

**Producer decision (2026-09-24):** Asteroids is the intended default control scheme, and the seed-file tests must no longer require the CSV comment header or a trailing newline. This supersedes acceptance criterion **AC5 (comment header)** of *CSV seed data files (`AH-0MUE2MGM0001XEH9`)* and retires the premise of the open bug *Gym config save strips the CSV comment header block (`AH-0MUF6NJ83003Y1J4`)*.

## User story

As a game designer, I want the player ship to default to the **Asteroids** control scheme and the CSV seed files to be allowed to use the headerless format produced by the gym Save, so that the committed default matches my saved tuning and the seed tests no longer block gym saves.

## Expected behaviour

- `DEFAULT_CONFIG.controlScheme === 'asteroids'` (built-in fallback used when the CSV cannot be read).
- The committed `src/data/ship-config.csv` holds a single ship row with `controlScheme=asteroids` (gym-saved format).
- The seed tests for `ship-config.csv` no longer assert a leading `#` comment header or a trailing newline; all remaining assertions pass.
- The full suite passes; the build passes.

## Scope

In scope:

- `src/core/configDefaults.ts` — default control scheme.
- `src/data/ship-config.csv` — committed seed value.
- `src/data/csv-seed.test.ts` — drop the ship-config header/trailing-newline requirements.
- Any other test that hard-codes the old default and must follow the new one.

Out of scope:

- Changing the dev-server write path (comment-header stripping) — behaviour is now accepted.
- Changing `enemy-configs.csv` or its tests (left intact).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Default scheme.** `DEFAULT_CONFIG.controlScheme === 'asteroids'` in `src/core/configDefaults.ts`. Verify: unit/seed test assertion via `coerceShipConfig`.
2. **Seed CSV.** `src/data/ship-config.csv` contains exactly one ship row with all fields matching `DEFAULT_CONFIG`, including `controlScheme=asteroids`, and parses via the CSV codec.
3. **Relaxed ship-config seed requirements.** `src/data/csv-seed.test.ts` no longer asserts a leading `# ` comment header or a trailing newline for `ship-config.csv`; the remaining seed assertions pass.
4. **Suite green.** `npm test` passes in full (no failures).
5. **Documentation.** `README.md` (Configuration (CSV)) and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (§8.2) describe the headerless `ship-config.csv` format and that the `#` comment header is optional and not preserved by the gym Save.

## Verification

- Build (process gate, enforced by the implement workflow before commit): `npm run build` (`tsc --noEmit && vite build`) -> exit 0 at commit `18ed334`.

## References

- Epic: Create a CSV file to maintain enemy configurations (`AH-0MTZWZ9TE009CVUA`).
- Superseded/related: `AH-0MUE2MGM0001XEH9` (CSV seed data files, AC5), `AH-0MUF6NJ83003Y1J4` (header-strip bug), `AH-0MUESFKCD004SI1V` (controlScheme persistence feature).

# Allow `v*` release tags to deploy to the `github-pages` environment (reproducible policy + docs)

## Problem statement

`.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml` triggers on `v*` tag pushes, but the repository's `github-pages` environment has a custom deployment branch policy that allows only the `dev` branch. Every release tag is therefore rejected by environment protection, so the Pages deploy fails, the failed check run lands on the release-branch HEAD, and the ship release wrapper's `waitForPRMerge()` always falls back to a manual merge.

## Users

- **Operator (release runner):** runs the ship release and expects it to auto-merge and publish without the manual-merge fallback.
- **Player:** expects each release to be live and playable at `https://sorratheorc.github.io/AI_Hell/`.
- **Future maintainer:** sets up or recovers the repository and needs a reproducible, documented way to configure the Pages environment policy.

### Example user stories

- As a release runner, I want pushing a `v*` release tag to deploy to GitHub Pages without environment-protection rejection, so that the release PR's checks pass and the ship wrapper merges the PR automatically.
- As a future maintainer, I want a documented, idempotent script that configures the `github-pages` environment deployment policy, so I do not have to rediscover the `dev`-only policy failure.
- As a player, I want every release to be published automatically at the project Pages URL.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Tag policy present.** The `github-pages` environment has a deployment policy for tags matching `v*`, in addition to the existing `dev` branch policy. Verify: `gh api repos/SorraTheOrc/AI_Hell/environments/github-pages/deployment-branch-policies --jq '.branch_policies[] | "\(.type):\(.name)"'` outputs both `branch:dev` and `tag:v*`.
- **Reproducible, idempotent setup script.** `scripts/setup-github-pages-environment.sh` exists, is executable, adds the `v*` tag policy only when missing, and is safe to re-run (second run makes no change and exits 0). It fails loudly with a clear message when `gh` is missing or unauthenticated. Verify: `bash -n` syntax check plus running it twice and inspecting the API result.
- **Deploy succeeds end to end.** Re-running workflow run `35993333739` (tag `v0.1.5`) completes with both the `build` and `deploy` jobs `success`, and `https://sorratheorc.github.io/AI_Hell/` serves the game. Verify: `gh run view 35993333739 --json conclusion,jobs` and an HTTP request to the Pages URL.
- **Tag-only trigger preserved.** `.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml` still triggers only on `v*` tag pushes; non-tag events (push to `main`/`dev`, pull requests) do not deploy. Verify: workflow YAML inspected and unchanged.
- **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.**
- **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- Only a `v*` tag policy may be added; the existing `dev` branch policy must be preserved.
- The workflow's tag-only trigger semantics must not change (superseding Github Hosted Alpha (`AH-0MU9P20Q2003D2V0`) AC5 is out of scope).
- The fix must live in this repository plus the GitHub repository setting; the global ship skill must not be edited (out of repository scope).
- Applying the setting requires a `gh` token with repository admin; if unavailable, the operator applies it manually and the script/documentation records the requirement.

## Existing state

- `.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml` triggers on `push` of tags matching `v*`; the `deploy` job targets environment `github-pages`.
- Environment `github-pages` has `custom_branch_policies: true` with exactly one policy: `branch:dev`. No tag policy exists.
- Release flow (`merge-dev-to-main.sh`) tags `vX.Y.Z` on the release merge commit, pushes the tag and the release branch, then opens the PR to `main`. The tag push triggers the deploy, whose rejection leaves a failed check on the release-branch HEAD, blocking `run-release.js`'s `waitForPRMerge()`.
- Evidence: workflow run `35993333739` (`event: push`, `headBranch: v0.1.5`) — `build` succeeded, `deploy` failed with zero steps (environment protection rejection).
- No `scripts/` directory exists and README has no deployment/Pages configuration section.

## Desired change

- Add a `tag:v*` deployment policy to the `github-pages` environment (keeping `branch:dev`).
- Add an idempotent, documented setup script that applies and verifies the policy via `gh api`.

- **Assumption:** The `gh` token has repository-admin rights to modify environment policies; otherwise the operator applies the policy manually and the script reports the required command.

# Intake Brief — ship producer-review gate remediation hint uses wrong `wl` flag casing

**Work item:** ship producer-review gate remediation hint uses wrong wl flag casing (AH-0MUFGUYFC001A2OB)
**Headline:** The ship skill's producer-review gate prints a remediation command with camelCase `--needsProducerReview`, which `wl` rejects; the gate must emit the kebab-case `--needs-producer-review` so an operator or agent can clear the flag by copying the hint verbatim.

## Problem statement

When the ship producer-review gate (exit 9) reports a blocking work item, its human-facing remediation block instructs the operator to run:

```
wl update <id> --needsProducerReview false --json
```

`wl update` does **not** accept camelCase flags; the correct flag is `--needs-producer-review` (verified via `wl update --help`: `--needs-producer-review <true|false>`). The printed command therefore fails with `error: unknown option '--needsProducerReview'`, leaving the operator unable to clear the flag using the hint. The same remediation builder is reused by the final-validation gate (exit 12), so both gates emit the broken hint.

## Users

- **Primary:** an operator (or agent acting for them) running a release and following the remediation hint printed by a failing ship gate.
- **Secondary:** maintainers of the ship skill who must keep the gate's copy-paste remediation in sync with the `wl` CLI.

Example user stories:

- **US1 — operator clears a blocked release:** As an operator whose release is blocked by exit 9, I want the printed remediation command to run successfully when pasted, so that I can clear the producer-review flag and proceed with the release without guessing the flag name.
- **US2 — agent remediates autonomously:** As a release agent that scrapes the gate's remediation output, I want the emitted command to use the exact `wl` flag spelling, so that automated remediation does not fail with "unknown option".

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1:** `buildProducerReviewRemediationCommand(id)` emits `wl update <id> --needs-producer-review false --json` (kebab-case), and no longer emits the camelCase `--needsProducerReview` flag. Verified by a unit test asserting the exact command string.
- **AC2:** The exit-9 producer-review gate and the exit-12 final-validation remediation paths both surface the corrected command, since both consume the shared builder. Verified by asserting the remediation text embedded in `checkProducerReviewStatus` / final-validation output.
- **AC3:** The emitted command is valid for the installed `wl` CLI: `wl update <id> --needs-producer-review false --json` parses (no "unknown option"). Verified by an integration assertion that parses the emitted flag against `wl update --help` output, or by a documented manual verification step in the work item comment.
- **AC4:** The existing unit test that asserts the remediation string contains `needsProducerReview` is updated to assert the kebab-case form, so the suite remains green against the corrected builder. Verified by the ship test suite.
- **AC5:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the change, including code comments (`buildProducerReviewRemediationCommand` JSDoc), `skill/ship/SKILL.md`, and `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md`, and no other remediation hint emits camelCase flags. Verified by inspection/grep for emitted command hints and the repository's doc-hygiene checks. **Planning clarification (review stage 1):** only the *CLI flag spelling* is in scope. The JSON field name `needsProducerReview` (as emitted by `wl --json`) and the documentation sentences that describe that field — including `skill/ship/SKILL.md` and `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` — must remain camelCase; changing them would be incorrect. No repository doc-hygiene test currently asserts CLI flag casing, so AC5 is verified by a targeted `grep` for `--needsProducerReview` in emitted command strings (expected: zero hits) rather than by an automated docs assertion.
- **AC6:** Full project test suite passes with the new changes (run from the canonical skills repo, see Constraints).

## Constraints

- **Repository boundary / cross-repo target:** the ship skill is **not** vendored into the AI_Hell game repo; its canonical source is the **SorraAgents** skills repo at `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js`. `~/.pi/agent/skills` is a symlink to `SorraAgents/skill`. The fix therefore lands in SorraAgents (`dev` branch), and the AI_Hell audit scope cannot verify the changed files directly — cross-repo verification must be recorded in a work-item comment (established precedent: Fix Discord notification projectRoot (AH-0MTXLWCWO005OSCZ)).
- **Single source of truth:** `check-final-validation.js` imports `buildProducerReviewRemediationCommand` from `check-audit-gate.js`, so there must be exactly one definition; do not duplicate the command string.
- **Repository-boundary rule:** the change is agent-infrastructure (`.pi/`/`skill/`); it must be implemented via the implement skill with explicit authorisation, not edited inline during intake/plan.
- Do not alter gate semantics, exit codes, or blocking conditions — this is a string/flag-format correction only.

## Existing state

- `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` (line ~283) defines `buildProducerReviewRemediationCommand`, returning a block whose second line is:
  `wl update ${workItemId} --needsProducerReview false --json`.
- `checkProducerReviewStatus` attaches this remediation to each blocking item (exit 9).
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-final-validation.js` imports and reuses the same builder (line ~525) for exit 12.
- `tests/unit/test-check-audit-gate.mjs` (≈line 520) asserts only that the returned string contains `wl update <id>` and the substring `needsProducerReview`; this substring test passes with the buggy camelCase and will need updating (AC4).
- `wl update --help` documents `--needs-producer-review <true|false>`.
- No other camelCase `--needsProducerReview` occurrence exists in the skill (grep confirmed one site only).

## Desired change

Change the emitted flag from `--needsProducerReview` to `--needs-producer-review` in the single remediation builder, update its JSDoc, and update the affected unit test to assert the kebab-case form. Confirm the audit-runner remediation path already uses kebab-case (it does) so the two no longer diverge.

## Key Files

> **Planning clarification (review stage 2):** all paths below are relative to the canonical **SorraAgents** skills repo root (`~/projects/SorraAgents`), not the AI_Hell working tree (AI_Hell vendors no copy). `tests/unit/test-check-audit-gate.mjs` (~line 520) is the regression test for `buildProducerReviewRemediationCommand` and is the AC1/AC4 test surface.

- `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` — one-line flag correction in `buildProducerReviewRemediationCommand` + JSDoc tidy (canonical source, SorraAgents repo).
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-final-validation.js` — consumer of the shared builder; verify exit-12 path renders the corrected hint (no string duplication expected).
- `tests/unit/test-check-audit-gate.mjs` — update the `buildProducerReviewRemediationCommand` assertion to require `--needs-producer-review` (regression guard).
- `skill/ship/SKILL.md` — if any remediation example/flag spelling appears, keep it consistent.
- `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` — document/confirm the kebab-case remediation flag.

## Related work

- **discovered-from:AH-0MUFE1N36007X48T** — Set Asteroids as the default ship control scheme and accept headerless CSV seed format (the release during which the bad hint was observed; shipped v0.1.5).
- **Fix Discord notification projectRoot (AH-0MTXLWCWO005OSCZ)** — precedent for a ship-skill bug tracked in the AI_Hell worklog but fixed in the SorraAgents skills repo with cross-repo verification.
- **SA-0MS4TJR2R0043UHO — Extend getCandidateItems and add checkProducerReviewStatus** (SorraAgents) — introduced the producer-review gate and its remediation output.
- **SA-0MS4TXDPB003EUKA — Add producer-review gating step to run-release.js** (SorraAgents) — the exit-9 gate.
- **SA-0MS4TXDPR006HO2W — Update documentation for producer-review gating** (SorraAgents) — docs for the gating behaviour.
- Related PR: release v0.1.5 (https://github.com/SorraTheOrc/AI_Hell/pull/5).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk (scope creep):** while fixing the hint, it is tempting to reword the whole remediation block or add auto-remediation. Out of scope — keep to the flag correction and the regression test; raise separate work items for any improvement.
- **Risk (false-negative audit):** because the changed files live in SorraAgents, the AI_Hell audit runner cannot see them. Mitigation: record the SorraAgents commit hash and a cross-repo verification note on this work item, as done for AH-0MTXLWCWO005OSCZ.
- **Risk (test coupling):** the current substring assertion (`needsProducerReview`) is weak and passes the bug. Mitigation: assert the exact kebab-case flag string (AC1/AC4).
- **Assumption:** `wl`'s accepted flag is stable as `--needs-producer-review` (confirmed against installed `wl update --help`).
- **Assumption:** no repository-override/vendored copy of the ship skill exists in AI_Hell (confirmed: no `skill/` directory, no `check-audit-gate.js` under the AI_Hell tree).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required for this item: the seed context supplied a precise problem statement, a single identified location, a verified root cause, and an explicit suggested fix. All remaining facts (CLI flag spelling, test assertion, cross-repo target, duplicate-string check) were resolved by repository and worklog research, so no producer input was solicited.

Follows the established AH-0MTXLWCWO005OSCZ precedent of fixing in SorraAgents and recording cross-repo verification. Source: `git -C ~/.pi/agent/skills rev-parse --show-toplevel` → `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents`; `wl search needsProducerReview` (SorraAgents store).
- **Q (implicit — is this a duplicate?):** — Resolved by research: no matching work item exists in either store (`wl search "flag casing"`, `wl search "remediation hint"`, `wl search needsProducerReview`). Source: worklog searches, 2026-09-27.

# Add Pages deploy trigger regression test

## Summary

Test-first verifier feature for *GitHub Pages deploy rejects release tags (environment policy allows only dev)* (`AH-0MUFGUR9C003XD77`). Adds an automated regression test that pins the **tag-only trigger contract** of `.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml`, so a future workflow edit cannot silently start deploying on branch pushes or pull requests.

## User story

As a future maintainer, I want an automated test that fails if the Pages deploy workflow starts triggering on non-tag events, so the tag-only release contract is protected without manual YAML review.

## Context

- Parent acceptance criterion **AC4** requires that `.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml` still triggers only on `v*` tag pushes, and that non-tag events (push to `main`/`dev`, pull requests) do not deploy.
- The workflow currently declares `on.push.tags: ['v*']` and a `deploy` job targeting environment `github-pages`.
- This item is created and completed **before** the environment-policy implementation items (test-first ordering).

## Scope

In scope:

- A hermetic vitest test that reads `.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml` from the repository root and asserts its trigger shape.

Out of scope:

- Changing the workflow (no change is expected for this fix).
- Calling the live GitHub API.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml` still triggers only on `v*` tag pushes; non-tag events (push to `main`/`dev`, pull requests) do not deploy.
- The test asserts the only trigger is `push` with `tags: ['v*']` — no `branches`, no `pull_request`, and no `workflow_dispatch`.
- The test asserts the workflow contains a `deploy` job targeting the `github-pages` environment and a `build` job the deploy needs.
- The test is hermetic (reads only the checked-out workflow file) and runs as part of `npm test` with no new runtime dependency (`npm run build` and `npm test` both pass).

## Minimal Implementation

- Add a vitest test (e.g. `scripts/deploy-pages-workflow.test.ts`, or co-located under `src/` if `scripts/` has no test wiring) that reads the workflow file using `node:fs` relative to the repo root.
- Parse the workflow text with focused assertions (regex/string checks or `yaml` if already available transitively); avoid adding a production dependency for a single test.
- Assert: `push.tags` is exactly `['v*']`; no `push.branches`; no `pull_request` / `workflow_dispatch` trigger keys; `jobs.deploy.environment.name == 'github-pages'`.
- Confirm the test is picked up by the existing `vitest.config.ts` include globs; adjust the include pattern only if the file lives outside the current test roots.

## Deliverables

- New automated trigger-contract test.
- `npm test` green including the new test.

## Dependencies

None.

## Key Files

- `.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml` — The workflow whose trigger contract is asserted (no change expected).
- `vitest.config.ts` — Test include globs; may need to cover the new test location.
- `scripts/deploy-pages-workflow.test.ts` — New hermetic regression test.

# Add idempotent Pages environment setup script

## Summary

Adds a reproducible, executable `scripts/setup-github-pages-environment.sh` that adds the `tag:v*` deployment policy to the `github-pages` environment via `gh api`, only when it is missing, and never removes the existing `dev` branch policy. Ships with automated tests (test-first inside the item).

## User story

As a future maintainer, I want a documented, idempotent script that configures the `github-pages` environment deployment policy, so I do not have to rediscover the `dev`-only policy failure that blocked every `v*` release tag.

## Context

- Parent acceptance criterion **AC2** requires `scripts/setup-github-pages-environment.sh` to exist, be executable, add the `v*` tag policy only when missing, be safe to re-run (second run makes no change, exits 0), and fail loudly when `gh` is missing or unauthenticated.
- There is currently **no** `scripts/` directory in the repository.
- The live environment already has exactly one policy: `branch:dev`. The script must preserve it.

## Scope

In scope:

- The setup script and its hermetic tests.

Out of scope:

- Applying the policy to the live repository (see *Apply tag policy and verify deploy*), and README documentation (see *Document Pages environment policy*).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `scripts/setup-github-pages-environment.sh` exists, is executable, adds the `v*` tag policy only when missing, and is safe to re-run (second run makes no change and exits 0).
- The script preserves the existing `dev` branch policy and adds only a `tag:v*` policy (never deletes or rewrites existing policies).
- It fails loudly with a clear, actionable message when `gh` is missing or unauthenticated (non-zero exit, no partial writes).
- Automated tests cover add-once, idempotent second run, dev-policy preservation, and fail-loud-without-`gh`/auth, using a stubbed `gh` on `PATH` (no live API calls).
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (`bash -n` syntax check, `npm test`, and `npm run build` all pass).

## Minimal Implementation

- Script: accept an optional `--repo <owner/name>` (default: resolve from the current clone via `gh repo view --json nameWithOwner`). Preflight `command -v gh` and `gh auth status`; exit non-zero with an actionable message otherwise.
- Read existing policies with `gh api repos/$REPO/environments/github-pages/deployment-branch-policies`; if a policy with `type == "tag"` and `name == "v*"` is present, print "already configured" and exit 0 without any write.
- Otherwise `POST` `{"name":"v*","type":"tag"}` to the same endpoint, then `GET` again to verify the policy is present (fail loudly if verification fails).
- Tests: create a temp `gh` stub executable that logs argv and returns canned JSON, prepend its directory to `PATH`, run the script with `bash`, and assert the recorded calls (no POST on second run; POST payload on first run; `dev` never deleted) plus exit codes. Keep all tests hermetic.

## Deliverables

- `scripts/setup-github-pages-environment.sh` (executable).
- Hermetic script tests wired into `npm test`.
- Green `npm test` / `npm run build`.

## Dependencies

None (sequenced after *Add Pages deploy trigger regression test*).

- `scripts/setup-github-pages-environment.test.ts` — New hermetic tests using a stubbed `gh`.

# Apply tag policy and verify deploy

## Summary

Applies the `tag:v*` deployment policy to the live `github-pages` environment using the setup script, then verifies the release Pages deploy end to end (policy present, `deploy` job succeeds, Pages URL serves the game).

## User story

As a release runner, I want pushing a `v*` release tag to deploy to GitHub Pages without environment-protection rejection, so that the release PR's checks pass and the ship wrapper merges the PR automatically; and as a player, I want every release published automatically at the project Pages URL.

## Context

- Parent acceptance criteria **AC1** (tag policy present) and **AC3** (deploy succeeds end to end) are verified by this item.
- Evidence of the current failure: workflow run `35993333739` (`event: push`, `headBranch: v0.1.5`) — `build` succeeded, `deploy` failed with zero steps due to environment protection.
- The active `gh` token has `repo` scope and the repository reports `admin: true`, so the script can apply the policy directly; if the token lacks admin the operator applies it manually and this item records the exact command.

## Scope

In scope:

- Running the setup script against `SorraTheOrc/AI_Hell`.
- Verifying the policy via the GitHub API.
- Re-running the failed tag workflow (or pushing a fresh `v*` tag through the normal release flow) and confirming the Pages URL serves.

Out of scope:

- Editing the workflow or the ship skill.
- Broader Pages source configuration changes (only revisit if the deploy still fails after the policy is in place).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The `github-pages` environment has a deployment policy for tags matching `v*`, in addition to the existing `dev` branch policy; `gh api repos/SorraTheOrc/AI_Hell/environments/github-pages/deployment-branch-policies` outputs both `branch:dev` and `tag:v*`.
- Deploy succeeds end to end: re-running workflow run `35993333739` (tag `v0.1.5`) completes with both the `build` and `deploy` jobs `success`, and `https://sorratheorc.github.io/AI_Hell/` serves the game.
- If the historical run cannot be re-run, a fresh `v*` tag is pushed through the normal release flow and its `deploy` job succeeds; the fallback taken is recorded.

# Implement — AsteroidSpawner (pure planner)

- **Type:** task
- **Priority:** medium
- **Parent:** AH-0MUDYS2SZ004H123

## Summary

Create `src/waves/AsteroidSpawner.ts` — a pure (no Phaser dependency) planner module that computes when and where asteroids should spawn based on the global wave index.

## Module Structure

### Exported types

```typescript
export interface SpawnEvent {
  sizeTier: 'large' | 'medium';
  x: number;
  y: number;
  vx: number;
  vy: number;
}
```

### Exported function

```typescript
export function computeSpawns(
  globalWaveIndex: number,
  gameWidth: number,
  gameHeight: number,
  waveTimeLimit: number,
  rng: () => number,
): SpawnEvent[];
```

## Algorithm (per spec)

### 1. Per-wave count

Start at 2. Every time the large weight reaches the reset threshold, double: `2 → 4 → 8 → …`.

### 2. Size weighting

- Medium weight fixed at 80.
- Large weight starts at 20 and increases by +20 per wave.
- When large weight reaches 2 × medium (160), reset to 80:20 and double the count.

Formula: `largeWeight = min(20 + 20 * (globalWaveIndex % wavesPerReset), 160)` where `wavesPerReset` depends on when the reset threshold is hit.

### 3. Spawn timing

- Divide the wave into N equal segments (N = count).
- Anchor for asteroid i is `i / N`.
- Apply ±5% jitter, clamped to [0, 0.95].
- First asteroid constrained to first 10% of wave.
- Times must be ordered and non-duplicated.

### 4. Offscreen edge + velocity

- Choose random edge uniformly (top/bottom/left/right).
- Place asteroid at random point along that edge, offset outward by `halfSize + margin` so fully outside viewport.
- Give inward-directed velocity: perpendicular to spawn edge with ±30° spread, at the tier's canonical speed.
- The inward component must dominate so it enters the playfield promptly.

### 5. Tuning constants (exported for easy retuning)

```typescript
export const ASTEROID_SPAWN_BASE_COUNT = 2;
export const ASTEROID_SPAWN_BASE_LARGE_WEIGHT = 20;
export const ASTEROID_SPAWN_MEDIUM_WEIGHT = 80;
export const ASTEROID_SPAWN_LARGE_WEIGHT_INCREMENT = 20;
export const ASTEROID_SPAWN_LARGE_WEIGHT_RESET = 160;
export const ASTEROID_SPAWN_JITTER_FRACTION = 0.05;
export const ASTEROID_SPAWN_MAX_JITTER_FRACTION = 0.95;
export const ASTEROID_SPAWN_FIRST_ASTEROID_MAX_FRACTION = 0.10;
export const ASTEROID_SPAWN_INWARD_ANGULAR_SPREAD = Math.PI / 6; // ±30°
export const ASTEROID_SPAWN_OUTWARD_MARGIN = 10; // px beyond half-size
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- `computeSpawns` returns exactly `count` events for any `globalWaveIndex >= 0`.
- Spawn count starts at 2 for `globalWaveIndex` 0–6, doubles at 7 (4), consistent with weight escalation.
- Large weight increases by +20 per wave; resets when it reaches 2× medium weight (160).
- First spawn time fraction is ≤ 0.10; subsequent times are spread across the wave with jitter.
- All spawn positions are fully offscreen (distance from viewport ≥ asteroid half-size + margin).
- All velocity vectors have inward components (toward the viewport centre).
- Output is deterministic for a given `globalWaveIndex`, dimensions, and RNG sequence.
- No Phaser runtime dependencies — pure TypeScript functions only.

- Covers parent AC2 — A wave begins with 2 asteroids by default; every spawned asteroid appears **offscreen** (fully outside the viewport on a random edge) and drifts inward into the playfield.
- Covers parent AC3 — Spawn timing: the first asteroid spawns within the first 10 % of the wave window and the second around 50 %; for higher counts spawn times are spread across the wave with randomised jitter and remain ordered/non-duplicated.
- Covers parent AC4 — Size weighting: asteroids are large or medium, weighted toward medium (baseline 80:20). The large weight increases by +20 each wave; when it reaches 2× the medium weight, weights reset to 80:20 and the per-wave count doubles (2 → 4 → 8 → …).

## Key Files

- `src/waves/AsteroidSpawner.ts` — new module

# Implement — PlayScene asteroid spawner integration

- **Type:** task
- **Priority:** medium
- **Parent:** AH-0MUDYS2SZ004H123

## Summary

Integrate `AsteroidSpawner` into `PlayScene.tick(dt)` so asteroids spawn at computed times during regular waves.

## Changes to PlayScene

### 1. Spawner state

Track planned spawns for the current wave:
```typescript
private pendingAsteroidSpawns: SpawnEvent[] = [];
private asteroidsSpawnedThisWave = 0;
```

### 2. Wave start — plan spawns

At the start of each regular wave (when `beginGame()` is called or when `onEnemyDestroyed()` returns `waveCleared` / `levelCleared`):

```typescript
private planAsteroidSpawns(): void {
  const wm = this.waveManager;
  if (!wm.currentWave() || wm.bossTriggered || wm.bossActive || wm.bossDefeated) {
    this.pendingAsteroidSpawns = [];
    this.asteroidsSpawnedThisWave = 0;
    return;
  }
  this.pendingAsteroidSpawns = computeSpawns(
    wm.globalWaveIndex,
    GAME_WIDTH,
    GAME_HEIGHT,
    WAVE_TIME_LIMIT_SECONDS,
    this.rng,
  );
  this.asteroidsSpawnedThisWave = 0;
}
```

### 3. Tick loop — release due spawns

In `tick(dt)`, after the wave timer increments:

```typescript
// Asteroid spawner — release any due spawns
while (
  this.asteroidsSpawnedThisWave < this.pendingAsteroidSpawns.length
) {
  const next = this.pendingAsteroidSpawns[this.asteroidsSpawnedThisWave];
  const spawnTime = next.x * WAVE_TIME_LIMIT_SECONDS; // reusing x as time fraction...
  // Actually: computeSpawns returns SpawnEvent with time info
  // Release when elapsed >= spawnTime
  break;
}
```

Actually, the spawn time needs to be stored in the SpawnEvent. Let me refine: the `SpawnEvent` already has timing info embedded. The scene checks: `if (waveElapsed >= spawnTimeFraction * WAVE_TIME_LIMIT_SECONDS)` then spawn.

### 4. Spawn execution

When a spawn is due:
1. Call `scene.spawnAsteroidAt(event.x, event.y, event.vx, event.vy)` — or add a new helper that accepts velocity.
2. Register the spawn with `WaveManager.registerDynamicSpawn(1)`.
3. Increment `asteroidsSpawnedThisWave`.

### 5. Pause / transition / boss exclusion

Skip asteroid spawning when:
- `transitionTimer > 0` (during transitions)
- `this.paused` (scene is paused)
- `bossTriggered` or `bossActive` (boss encounter)

### 6. Wave start hook

Call `planAsteroidSpawns()` whenever a new regular wave begins:
- After `beginGame()`
- After `onEnemyDestroyed()` returns `waveCleared`
- After `onEnemyDestroyed()` returns `levelCleared`

## Acceptance Criteria

- Asteroids spawn at the correct times during each wave (verified by tick-driven test).
- Spawned asteroids are registered with WaveManager as dynamic spawns.
- No asteroids spawn during boss encounters.
- No asteroids spawn during transitions or when paused.
- Existing asteroid behaviours (splitting, timeout survival, transition collidability, boss-entry cleanup) are preserved.
- The spawner uses the scene's injectable `rng` for determinism.

- Covers parent AC1 — Every regular wave of every level (Levels 1–5) spawns asteroids from the random offscreen spawner; the boss encounter spawns none.
- Covers parent AC5 — Spawned asteroids are registered with `WaveManager` as dynamic spawns so wave-clear accounting includes them, and existing asteroid behaviours (splitting, timeout survival, transition collidability, boss-entry cleanup) are preserved.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — integrate spawner into tick loop

Implement the beat clock module (`src/utils/beat.ts`)

## Summary
Create a new pure, unit-testable beat clock module that derives a beat period from a configurable BPM (default 80 BPM → 750 ms/beat), tracks a beat anchor/time origin, and exposes quantisation helpers.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **AC1** — Module at `src/utils/beat.ts` exposes `beatPeriodMs` (derived from configurable BPM, default 80), `nextTick(elapsedTime, interval)`, and `shotTimeFor(currentTime, interval)` helpers.
- [ ] **AC2** — All helpers are pure and deterministic given an input time — no `Date` or frame coupling.
- [ ] **AC3** — The beat anchor is configurable (defaults to 0/scene start) and advances with game time (pauses with the game).
- [ ] **AC4** — Unit tests cover: period from BPM, quantisation boundaries/edge cases, config override changing cadence.
- [ ] **AC5** — Tests assert that `nextTick(t, interval)` returns the smallest multiple of `interval` at/after `t`, and `shotTimeFor` snaps to the correct grid tick.
- [ ] **Traces to parent AC1** — [ ] **AC1 — Pure, configurable 80 BPM beat clock.** A new pure, unit-testable module (e.g. `src/utils/beat.ts`) derives the beat period from a **configurable** BPM (default **80 BPM** → 750 ms/beat), tracks a beat anchor/time origin, and exposes a quantisation helper that maps an arbitrary elapsed time to the next beat/subdivision tick (`nextTick(t)`, `isOnBeat/fireTimeFor(interval, t)`, etc.). No `Date`/frame coupling; deterministic given an input time.

## Constraints
- No audio or visual beat indicators — silent internal scheduling only.
- Must work with Phasers delta-time model (ms-based).
- Default BPM: 80 (beat period: 750 ms). All per-weapon intervals are exact subdivisions.

## Key Files
- `src/utils/beat.ts` — **NEW** — pure beat clock module.
- `src/utils/beat.test.ts` — **NEW** — unit tests.

## Risks
- Minimal: the module is pure and self-contained. Edge cases: large dt values (frame drops), zero elapsed time.

Each weapon fires at an exact subdivision: cannon 2/beat (375 ms), spread 1/beat (750 ms), dual 1/beat (750 ms), rapid 6/beat (125 ms). Add a catalogue-wide test asserting every fire rate divides evenly into the beat period.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **AC1** — All `WEAPON_*_FIRE_RATE` constants in `src/utils/weapons.ts` become derived from the beat period (e.g. `beatPeriodMs / subdivisions`), not hard-coded literals.
- [ ] **AC2** — `WEAPON_CATALOGUE` fire rates match the producer-specified values: cannon 375 ms (2/beat), spread 750 ms (1/beat), dual 750 ms (1/beat), rapid 125 ms (6/beat).
- [ ] **AC3** — A catalogue-wide invariant test asserts `beatPeriodMs % fireRateMs === 0` for every weapon in `WEAPON_CATALOGUE`.
- [ ] **AC4** — Existing weapon tests still pass after the refactor (no behaviour change beyond timing).
- [ ] **AC5** — New weapons added to the catalogue must satisfy the invariant; the test fails if they do not.
- [ ] **Traces to parent AC3** — [ ] **AC3 — Per-weapon subdivisions + catalogue-wide invariant.** Each weapon's fire interval is an exact subdivision of the beat: **cannon 375 ms (160 BPM, 2/beat)**, **spread 750 ms (80 BPM, 1/beat)**, **dual 750 ms (80 BPM, 1/beat)**, **rapid 125 ms (480 BPM, 6/beat)**. A catalogue-wide test asserts every `WeaponDefinition.fireRateMs` satisfies `beatPeriodMs % fireRateMs === 0` (equivalently `fireRateMs × n === beatPeriodMs` for a positive integer `n`), so the future 20 BPM quarter-time weapon and any other new weapon are on-grid by construction.

## Key Files
- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — fire rates derived from beat period.
- `src/utils/weapons.test.ts` — invariant test.

## Risks
- Low: existing tests will verify no unintended behaviour changes. The rapid weapon (125 ms) is unchanged; cannon, spread, and dual rates change slightly.

Replace Player.tryFire per-weapon cooldowns with phase-locked beat scheduling

## Summary
Replace the independent per-weapon cooldown model in `Player.tryFire` with phase-locked scheduling on the shared beat clock. A weapons next shot time is the smallest multiple of its interval at/after the current beat-clock time. Collection may delay the first shot to the next grid tick (by design). All active weapons share the same anchor so they stay phase-locked.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **AC1** — `Player.tryFire(dt)` no longer uses independent per-weapon cooldowns — every shot is snapped to the shared beat clock.
- [ ] **AC2** — All simultaneously active weapons fire on the same shared grid (no independent, drifting cooldowns).
- [ ] **AC3** — A weapon collected mid-beat fires its first shot on the next grid tick (by design).
- [ ] **AC4** — Cumulative and timed weapon semantics are unchanged (collection, expiry, reset all work as before).
- [ ] **AC5** — Tests assert every emitted shot time is an exact grid tick, verified with multiple active weapons.
- [ ] **Traces to parent AC2** — [ ] **AC2 — All player fire is globally quantised.** Player auto-fire (`Player.tryFire` and its callers in `CombatScene`/`GymWeapons`) emits shots only on ticks of the shared beat clock, phase-locked to the scene/beat anchor — never off-grid — regardless of when a weapon is collected or the frame rate. All simultaneously active weapons fire on the same shared grid (no independent, drifting cooldowns). Tests assert every emitted shot time is an exact grid tick.

## Key Files
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — `tryFire` / cooldown model → phase-locked scheduling.
- `src/entities/Player.test.ts` — grid-tick emission tests.

## Risks
- Medium: this changes the core fire model. Must preserve cumulative/timed weapon semantics. Tests must verify phase-locking with multiple active weapons.

# Create Dev Utilities gym scene with curve editor and wave preview

## Context

The runtime auto-sequencer (AH-0MUDIWETP003XC3X) is fully implemented but not wired into the game. There is no way for designers or testers to interact with it visually. This work item creates a gym scene that provides a hands-on interface for designing and previewing difficulty curves.

discovered-from:AH-0MUDIWETP003XC3X

## Goal

Add a new **Dev Utilities** category/section to the gym index, and create a gym scene within it that provides:

1. **Curve editor** — an interactive way to define the target difficulty curve (array of scores, one per wave)
2. **Regenerate button** — when clicked, runs the sequencer against the current curve and displays the resulting waves
3. **Wave list** — shows each generated wave with its enemy composition, target difficulty, and the resulting wave
4. **Edit-to-clear behaviour** — if the curve is edited, the wave list is cleared and replaced with an instruction to click the regenerate button

## Scope

- Add a **Dev Utilities** column/section to the gym index (GymIndex.ts) — follows the same pattern as the existing ENEMIES and Bosses columns
- Create src/scenes/gym/GymCurveSequencer.ts (and its test file)
- The scene uses the existing sequencer() from difficultySequencer.ts
- Plain-DOM tuning panel overlay (same pattern as GymPlayer) for the curve editor
- Phaser canvas for the wave list display (Phaser text objects)

## Curve editor design

- Each wave in the curve is represented as a row with:
  - A numeric slider (0–100) for the target difficulty
  - A Remove button to delete that wave row
- An "Add Wave" button to append a new wave row at the end
- The "Regenerate" button runs the sequencer and populates the wave list below
- When the curve is edited (any slider moved, wave added/removed), the wave list is cleared and replaced with instruction text: "Edit made — click Regenerate to preview"

## Wave list display

- Each wave entry shows:
  - Wave number
  - Target difficulty
  - Enemy composition (enemy type, count)
  - Whether shooting is enabled
- Entries rendered as Phaser text objects, ordered top-to-bottom

## Non-goals

- Saving/loading curves (could be added later)
- Visual preview of enemy formations (text-only for now)
- Drag-to-reorder waves in the curve editor

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Gym index shows a "Dev Utilities" section** — a new column or section in the gym index listing gym scenes under the Dev Utilities category
2. **GymCurveSequencer scene is listed** under the Dev Utilities section and can be launched from the gym index
3. **Curve editor works** — user can add wave rows, remove wave rows, and adjust target difficulty via sliders (0–100)
4. **Regenerate button** — clicking it runs sequencer() with the current curve and candidate pool, populating the wave list
5. **Wave list is cleared on curve edit** — when the user edits the curve (any change), the wave list is replaced with instruction text to click regenerate
6. **Wave entries display correctly** — each shows wave number, target difficulty, enemy composition, and shooting status
7. **Back to index button** works (arrow-left INDEX)
8. **ESC returns to main menu** (consistent with other gym scenes)
9. **All tests pass** — the scene has unit tests verifying the curve editor and regenerate flow

## Revision — audit follow-up (2026-09-27)

Manual review rejected the first implementation with the following note:

> Rejected by manual review. Make the wave description a table, with column headings. Provide a help box in the bottom right summarizing each column.

Additional acceptance criteria:

10. **Wave preview is a table** — the wave preview renders a table with column headings (Wave, Target, Composition, Shooting) and one aligned row per wave.
11. **Column guide help box** — a help box anchored to the bottom-right of the canvas summarises each wave-table column.

## Revision — second audit follow-up (2026-09-27)

Manual review rejected the implementation again with the following note:

> Rejected by manual review. The UI works, but the generated levels are not good. Firstly, why do we have an actual and error value? Why don't we just create as close the target as possible? Secondly, the higher levels seem to just repeat the phaser with shooting.

Root cause confirmed by reproducing the sequencer output: `sequencer()` picked exactly one candidate group per wave and a single group's `enemyDifficulty` score saturates around 33 (e.g. `phaser×12`), so every target at or above ~40 produced the identical `phaser×12` wave — hence the large error values and the repetition.

Revised acceptance criteria:

12. **Wave generation reaches the target** — the preview table no longer shows redundant ACTUAL/ERROR columns; the table columns are WAVE / TARGET / COMPOSITION / SHOOTING. The sequencer composes a wave from one or more candidate groups so the wave's summed difficulty is within a small tolerance of the target for every target above the old single-group ceiling (previously capped at ~33) up to 100.
13. **Higher waves are varied** — waves with different (especially higher) targets produce meaningfully different enemy compositions instead of every high wave repeating the same archetype (e.g. `phaser` with shooting).

## Key Files

- src/scenes/GymIndex.ts — add Dev Utilities section
- src/scenes/gym/GymCurveSequencer.ts — new scene
- src/scenes/gym/GymCurveSequencer.test.ts — tests for the scene
- src/core/difficultySequencer.ts — sequencer (extended to compose multi-group waves)
- src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts — existing scorer (read-only)
- src/core/enemyConfig.ts — existing enemy configs for candidate pool
- src/utils/gymNavigation.ts — shared back-to-index navigation
- src/utils/gymDiscovery.ts — gym scene auto-discovery (no changes needed, scene auto-appears)
data.title: Create Dev Utilities gym scene with curve editor and wave preview
