# Intake brief — Document gym-parity principle in AGENTS.md

**Headline:** The producer directive that gym scenes are the canonical parity reference for the game is currently implicit in the architecture notes but never stated as a rule; this item adds an explicit, discoverable gym-parity principle to the repo-local `AGENTS.md` so future agents and contributors apply gameplay changes consistently across the gyms and the game.

## Problem statement

Operators repeatedly see behaviour drift between the gym scenes and the shipped game. The producer's directive is that gyms and the game must execute the same core code, and that gym behaviours are the parity reference. That principle is **not stated as a rule** in the repo-local `AGENTS.md`, so it is easy for a contributor to change gameplay in one scene without updating the corresponding gym(s) — or vice versa — without violating any documented rule.

Verification performed: `grep -ni 'gym\|parity\|reference' AGENTS.md` returns no gym-parity rule (only generic workflow/documentation references). The `AGENTS.md` "Architecture Notes for Agents" section does describe the shared combat core and states that "no production scene keeps a divergent copy", but it does not state a general gym-parity rule or name the gym directories it applies to.

## Users

- **As an agent/contributor**, when I change a gameplay behaviour I want an explicit rule telling me to apply it consistently to the corresponding gym scene(s) and the game, so I do not silently introduce drift.
  - *"As a developer, when I change a player/enemy/projectile/power-up behaviour I want to know the gyms are the parity reference, so I update both in the same change."*
- **As a producer/reviewer**, when I audit a gameplay change I want a documented rule to point to, so I can verify parity was considered.
  - *"As the producer, I want gym parity stated in AGENTS.md so it is enforceable in review, not just implicit in architecture notes."*

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** — `AGENTS.md` contains an explicit gym-parity rule stating that gyms are the canonical parity reference for the game and that any gameplay-behaviour change must be applied consistently to the corresponding gym scene(s) and the game, unless a documented reason exists to diverge.
- **AC2** — The rule names the gym scenes/directories it applies to (at minimum `src/scenes/gym/`, including `src/scenes/gym/core/`, and the game-side scene/shared core such as `PlayScene` and `src/scenes/core/`), so a reader knows exactly which files are in scope.
- **AC3** — A docs review (grep/search across `AGENTS.md`, `README.md` and `docs/`) confirms there is no contradictory guidance that permits gyms to intentionally diverge without a documented reason; any near-conflicts are reconciled or explicitly noted.
- **AC4** — Validation: a reviewer can quote the AC1 rule from the rendered `AGENTS.md` and confirm it matches the producer directive; automated check is a grep asserting the rule text and the named directories are present.
- **AC5** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- **AC6** — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Additive only.** Do not weaken, reorder or remove any existing workflow/safety rule in `AGENTS.md`.
- **Consistent with existing architecture notes.** The rule must agree with the existing "Architecture Notes for Agents" shared-core description (no production scene keeps a divergent copy).
- **Docs-only change.** No application behaviour or source code behaviour changes.
- **UK English** spelling throughout.
- **Placement:** `AGENTS.md` currently has no "Game Architecture Conventions" or "Coding Disciplines" heading, so the rule is expected to be a new short section (e.g. `## Game Architecture Conventions`) placed near the existing `## Architecture Notes for Agents` section; final heading/placement is an implementation decision.

## Existing state

- `AGENTS.md` (repo-local) documents the agent workflow and Worklog usage, plus an `## Architecture Notes for Agents` section describing the shared two-tier combat core (`CombatCoreScene` → `CombatScene`) and the shared drop/bullet/enemy-fire layers. It states scenes must not keep divergent copies but has no explicit gym-parity rule.
- The gym scenes live in `src/scenes/gym/` (`GymBoss`, `GymCurveSequencer`, `GymEnemies`, `GymMinerals`, `GymPlayer`, `GymPowerUpsCombat`, `GymPowerUpsUtility`, `GymWeapons`) with the generic base `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`; the dev index is `src/scenes/GymIndex.ts` and discovery is directory-dynamic via `src/utils/gymDiscovery.ts`.
- `README.md` documents the gym index as a dev-mode playground; `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` is the authoritative gym/enemy guide and already treats the shared core as the mechanism for parity.
- The wider parity effort is tracked by the epic **Gym↔game behavioural parity (AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA)** and the in-progress **Extend parity regression guard and cross-scene equivalence tests (AH-0MUII3GOO001XEBB)**.

## Desired change

Add a short, explicit rule to the repo-local `AGENTS.md` stating:

> Gyms are the canonical parity reference for the game. Any gameplay behaviour change must be applied consistently to the corresponding gym scene(s) and the game, unless a documented reason exists to diverge.

The rule should name the gym scenes/directories it applies to (`src/scenes/gym/`) and the game-side scene/shared core (`PlayScene`, `src/scenes/core/`).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `AGENTS.md` — Add a new `## Game Architecture Conventions` section (or equivalent) containing the gym-parity rule; place near `## Architecture Notes for Agents`.
- `src/scenes/gym/` — The gym scene directory the rule names as in-scope (AC2); includes `core/GymFormationScene.ts`.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — The shared core the parity rule points to.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — Generic gym base consuming the shared core.
- `README.md` — References the gym index; verify the new rule does not contradict it (AC3).
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — Authoritative gym guide; verify consistency (AC3).

## Related work

- **Gym↔game behavioural parity: eliminate remaining core-code duplication so every object behaves identically (AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA)** — parent epic; this documentation rule supports its enforcement.
- **Extend parity regression guard and cross-scene equivalence tests (AH-0MUII3GOO001XEBB)** — in-progress automated parity guard this rule complements.
- **Speed power up should increase all speeds (AH-0MUAYB9JS0025YUB)** — `discovered-from`; the parity-drift incident that motivated this item.
- **Document scheme-aware gym controls (AH-0MTFRQR42009TYE9)** — precedent docs-only gym change.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — authoritative guide for gym/enemy implementation.
- `AGENTS.md` § *Architecture Notes for Agents* — existing shared-core guidance to remain consistent with.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUAYB4EJ005CIYQ** – Power Ups scene title in index page (completed)
- **AH-0MUII3CXX0023H24** – Shared power-up drop layer (spawner, lifecycle, collection, magnet, P4 notice, cues) (completed)
- **AH-0MT94ULUU001NBW3** – Audit merge gate hard-codes npm run build; docs-only repos fail Phase 1 (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: ac3, acceptance, add, agents, always (+52 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: ac1, add, agents, always, anywhere (+46 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, add, always (+38 more)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** The producer directive in the work item ("gyms are the canonical parity reference") is authoritative and should be quoted essentially verbatim.
- **Risk (scope creep):** Reconciling unrelated architecture-note content in `AGENTS.md` is out of scope; record extra opportunities as linked work items instead.
- **Risk (contradiction):** AC3 may surface pre-existing text that reads as permitting divergence; if found, note it on the work item rather than silently rewriting architecture notes.
- **Risk (enforcement gap):** A docs rule alone does not enforce parity — the automated guard (AH-0MUII3GOO001XEBB) is the enforcement mechanism; this rule is the human/agent-facing complement.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- No clarifying questions were required. The seed context supplied the exact rule text, the acceptance criteria and the verification performed; all remaining facts (gym directory, game-side scene, related parity work) were obtained from repo/worklog search, per the interview contract's "do not ask questions answerable by repo search" rule.
- **OPEN QUESTION:** none.
- Research summary: `src/scenes/gym/` confirmed as the gym scene directory (`GymFormationScene.ts` under `core/`); `AGENTS.md` headings confirmed to contain no gym-parity rule and no "Coding Disciplines"/"Game Architecture Conventions" heading; the parity epic AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA (stage `plan_complete`) and guard AH-0MUII3GOO001XEBB (in-progress) confirmed as related work.

---

## Plan review (@plan, auto-complete path)

Effort/risk pre-check returned `decision: skip` (effort **Extra Small**, risk **Low**), so this docs-only item is small enough to implement directly and no child decomposition was created. The six automated review stages were run against the existing content:

1. **Requirements & AC alignment** — all six ACs trace to the Desired change and Constraints, and every requirement has a corresponding AC (rule text → AC1; in-scope directories → AC2; docs consistency → AC3; verification → AC4; related docs → AC5; suite → AC6). No missing, contradictory or invented ACs.
2. **Completeness** — description and `## Acceptance Criteria` present; the `**Key Files (predicted)**` section is syntactically valid (`validate_key_files_format` reports no issues / `validate_key_files_in_description` is empty) and every listed path exists (`AGENTS.md`, `src/scenes/gym/`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts`, `README.md`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`).
3. **Sequencing & dependencies** — no children and no dependency edges; this is a single docs work unit. The AC4 grep verification is to be added together with the `AGENTS.md` edit so it fails before and passes after.
4. **Scope sizing** — one deliverable increment (a short `AGENTS.md` section + the AC3 docs-consistency review + the AC4 grep assertion). No further breakdown needed.
5. **Acceptance & testability** — AC1/AC2 are pass/fail via the AC4 grep assertion; AC3/AC5 are documentation reviews; AC6 is the full suite. No criterion was so vague that it needed rewriting.
6. **Polish & handoff** — description is clear, well formatted and actionable; UK English throughout.

### Clarifications recorded during review (additive; no intent change)

- **Factual correction to Existing state / Constraints.** The intake brief states that the repo-local `AGENTS.md` `## Architecture Notes for Agents` section "describes the shared two-tier combat core" and "states scenes must not keep divergent copies". Verified this is **not** in `AGENTS.md` (`grep -c 'CombatCoreScene\|Gym' AGENTS.md` → 0). The shared-combat-core narrative lives in `README.md` (the "Shared combat core" / shared-layer notes around lines 361–397) and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`; the `AGENTS.md` `## Architecture Notes for Agents` section covers the Worklog data-storage architecture only.
  - *Impact:* none for the core deliverable — the rule is still added to `AGENTS.md`, and "place near `## Architecture Notes for Agents`" remains valid. The AC3 consistency check must therefore be run against `README.md` and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, both of which already state that the game and gyms must not keep divergent copies (i.e. they are aligned, not contradictory).

# Wire the runtime auto-sequencer into the game's wave generation

## Problem statement

The runtime auto-sequencer (`src/core/difficultySequencer.ts`, AH-0MUDIWETP003XC3X) is a standalone pure-core library — nothing in the playable game calls it. Enemy composition is still hard-coded in `src/waves/Formations.ts` (`LEVELS`) and driven through `WaveManager` by `PlayScene`, so every run uses the same fixed waves. This item wires the sequencer into a playable run so wave composition is generated at runtime from a target difficulty curve, behind an opt-in config toggle, with the static campaign preserved as the default and the fallback.

## Users

- As a **player**, when the feature is enabled, enemy waves should follow a difficulty curve so each run ramps up smoothly instead of using identical fixed enemy counts. (Default-off means shipped behaviour is unchanged until enabled.)
- As a **designer**, I want to define the campaign's levels, names, wave counts and per-wave difficulty targets in a CSV config, so I can tune the difficulty ramp and campaign shape without editing `Formations.ts`.

## Decisions confirmed at intake

1. **Opt-in toggle, default off.** Static `LEVELS` remains the shipped default; generated waves only drive the run when the toggle is enabled in config. A follow-on work item covers *mixing* generated and scripted levels within one campaign: **Support mixed generated and scripted levels in a campaign (AH-0MUH7Q6HN0006QPD)** (sibling, `discovered-from`).
2. **Per-level curves with configurable per-level wave counts.** One `sequencer()` call per level; the curve length sets the wave count.
3. **Fully data-driven campaign skeleton.** The curve config also defines the level count and level names (not just targets). The boss is still triggered after the final configured level (existing `WaveManager` behaviour).
4. **CSV-backed config.** A new `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` is loaded through the existing `configStore`/CSV pipeline (editable in dev via `/api/csv/...`, bundled read-only in production).
5. **Defaults seeded from current calibration.** The baked-in default targets are derived from the current `LEVELS` measured scores (`levelDifficulty`/`enemyDifficulty`) spread non-decreasingly across each level's waves.

## Existing state

- `WaveManager` already accepts injected `LevelDefinition[]` via its constructor and `setLevels()`, defaulting to static `LEVELS`; it owns plan/spawn/progression and the boss trigger.
- `sequencer(curve, candidates, options)` returns one `ShootableWave` per curve entry, each with one adjusted group and a `shootEnabled` flag; `options.defaultShootEnabled` applies to the whole call, which is why generation is done **per level** (so Levels 1–3 and 4–5 can differ).
- `AdjustedGroup` extends `WaveGroup`, so `ShootableWave.groups` maps structurally to `WaveDefinition.groups`.
- Config tunables live in two pipelines: CSV-backed `configStore`/`csv.ts`/Vite plugin (enemies, ship) and the localStorage-backed `rules.ts` (`GameRules`).
- GDD §2.4 — Levels 1–3 do not fire; §2.5 — Levels 4–5 do. §3.2 fixes level themes.

## Desired change

At run start, `PlayScene` reads the config. When the (opt-in) toggle is disabled it uses static `LEVELS` exactly as today. When enabled it builds a `LevelDefinition[]` from the difficulty-curve config by calling `sequencer()` once per configured level with `defaultShootEnabled = levelNumber >= 4`, converts each `ShootableWave` to a `WaveDefinition`, injects the result into `WaveManager`, and drives the run from it. Any empty/degenerate config falls back to static `LEVELS`.

## Constraints

- **Pure core stays pure.** `difficultySequencer.ts` is not modified (read-only call site).
- **Determinism.** Generation must be a pure function of config + candidate pool; no RNG.
- **No behavioural change when the toggle is off.** Existing `WaveManager`/`PlayScene`/campaign tests must pass unchanged.
- **CSV is the source of truth in dev**; production reads the bundled copy; malformed rows must not crash.
- Follow the existing config/CSV patterns (codec, plugin, store) rather than inventing a new persistence path.
- UK English in prose; Markdown in the work item.

## Assumptions

- The global opt-in toggle is a scalar tunable and will live in the existing `GameRules` settings store (`sequencedWavesEnabled`, default `false`); the per-level curve values/targets live in the CSV. Per-level source mixing is deferred to AH-0MUH7Q6HN0006QPD.
- The campaign fire rule is derived from the (1-based) level number: `level <= 3` ⇒ `shootEnabled=false`, `level >= 4` ⇒ `true`. With a data-driven skeleton this applies to any configured levels beyond 5 as firing levels; per-level `shootEnabled` overrides are out of scope.
- "Configurable curve" is satisfied by the CSV-backed config plus the baked-in default; runtime UI editing is AH-0MUGXDVPH005TIZL.

## Acceptance criteria

- **WaveManager accepts injected definitions** — `WaveManager` is driven by generated `LevelDefinition`/`WaveDefinition` data; with no override supplied it uses static `LEVELS` exactly, and existing `WaveManager` tests pass unchanged.
- **Opt-in toggle** — with the toggle disabled (the default) the run uses static `LEVELS` and behaves as today; with it enabled the run uses generated definitions (test asserts both paths). **Superseded (2026-09-28):** the shipped default becomes on with explicit opt-out per AH-0MUJSUTLA006Q8E1 (see Plan update); the original wording is retained for traceability.
- **Runtime generation runs** — at run start, with the toggle enabled, the game builds per-level curves from the curve config and calls `sequencer()` once per level, obtaining a `SequencerResult` per level.
- **CSV-backed, data-driven config** — `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` defines level number, level name and per-wave targets (curve length ⇒ wave count); it is loaded through the existing CSV/configStore pipeline and is editable in dev / read-only in production. Malformed or missing rows fall back to the baked-in default curve without crashing.
- **Generated waves drive the run** — the groups produced by the sequencer are what `PlayScene` spawns (verified via the spawn plan / `WaveManager.planSpawns()` or a test harness), not the static `LEVELS`.
- **Curve is configurable** — changing the configured/default curve changes the produced wave composition; two distinct curves yield different plans (test asserts this).
- **Campaign fire rule** — generated levels 1–3 have `shootEnabled=false`; levels 4+ have `shootEnabled=true` (test asserts both).
- **Determinism** — generating the campaign twice with the same config and candidate pool yields identical level/wave definitions.
- **Fallback is safe** — an empty/degenerate curve config, an empty curve, or an empty candidate pool falls back to static `LEVELS` and the game does not crash (test covers the fallback).
- **Testing/validation** — new unit/integration tests cover the codec, campaign builder, conversion, fire rule, determinism and fallback, and they are meaningful and passing.
- **Documentation** — all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- **No regressions** — the full project test suite passes with the new changes (`npm test`).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` — existing sequencer; read-only call site (`sequencer`, `defaultCandidatePool`, `ShootableWave`, `AdjustedGroup`).
- `src/core/csv.ts` — add a difficulty-curve codec (parse/serialize + validation, mirroring `EnemyConfig`).
- `src/core/configTypes.ts` — add the difficulty-curve row/config types (leaf module, no imports).
- `src/core/configStore.ts` — load `difficulty-curves.csv` through the existing dev/bundled pipeline and expose an accessor.
- `src/core/rules.ts` — add the opt-in `sequencedWavesEnabled` tunable (default `false`) to `GameRules`.
- `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` — **new** CSV defining levels, names, wave targets (data-driven skeleton).
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` — **new**: build the curve config/pool and convert `SequencerResult` per level into `LevelDefinition[]` (plus fallback).
- `src/waves/WaveManager.ts` — confirm/verify injected-definition support (minimal or no change).
- `src/waves/Formations.ts` — static `LEVELS`: default/fallback and level metadata source for seeding defaults.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — build + inject the generated campaign at run start when the toggle is enabled.
- Vite CSV plugin / dev write endpoint — extend to serve the new CSV if the existing generic path does not already cover it.
- Test files: `src/core/csv.test.ts`, `src/core/configStore.test.ts`, `src/waves/sequencedLevels.test.ts` (**new**), `src/waves/WaveManager.test.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **CSV pipeline scope** — extending the codec/plugin/store is the largest cost; mitigated by mirroring the existing `EnemyConfig` codec/plugin exactly and reusing the generic write endpoint where possible.
- **Default-curve calibration drift** — seeding from measured `LEVELS` scores could diverge from the static campaign if either changes; mitigated by a test asserting the default generated campaign is non-decreasing and stays in 0–100.
- **Fallback correctness** — a partial/degenerate CSV must never produce an unplayable campaign; mitigated by an explicit fallback test and a single guard at the PlayScene boundary.
- **Scope creep** — runtime curve editing (AH-0MUGXDVPH005TIZL) and mixed generated/scripted campaigns (AH-0MUH7Q6HN0006QPD) are explicitly out of scope; extra opportunities are recorded as linked work items rather than absorbed here.
- **Assumption (toggle location)** — the opt-in toggle lives in the `GameRules`/settings store rather than the CSV; revisit only if the producer prefers an all-CSV toggle.

## Out of scope

- Player-state adaptation (adjusting the curve from player performance).
- Runtime curve editing UI (AH-0MUGXDVPH005TIZL).
- Replacing boss / asteroid spawning logic.
- Per-level generated-vs-scripted mixing (AH-0MUH7Q6HN0006QPD) — **now in scope**, generalised to per-wave generation modes by AH-0MUJSUQD8003FSUT (see Plan update).

## Related work

- **Implement runtime auto-sequencer for dynamic difficulty adjustment (AH-0MUDIWETP003XC3X)** — delivered the sequencer this item wires in (`discovered-from`).
- **Support mixed generated and scripted levels in a campaign (AH-0MUH7Q6HN0006QPD)** — follow-on enabled by the opt-in toggle (sibling).
- **Create Dev Utilities gym scene with curve editor and wave preview (AH-0MUGXDVPH005TIZL)** — sibling designer tool; previews curves but does not affect the game.
- **Design a mechanism for calculating how hard an enemy is to survive (AH-0MTZWZ7MC002B01K)** — delivered the `enemyDifficulty`/`levelDifficulty` scorer and campaign calibration that seed the default curve.
- **Config store / CSV pipeline (AH-0MTZWZ9TE009CVUA)** — the persistence pattern the new curve CSV follows.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §2.4/§2.5 fire rules, §3.2 level themes.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — enemy archetypes/formations.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q (Round 1): Does the generated sequence replace `LEVELS` outright, or sit behind a toggle?**
  - Answer (operator): **(b) opt-in, default off** — shipped behaviour stays unchanged until a designer enables it. Additionally the operator asked for a follow-on work item allowing a campaign to **mix generated and scripted levels**.
  - Source: interactive reply.
  - Follow-up: created **Support mixed generated and scripted levels in a campaign (AH-0MUH7Q6HN0006QPD)**.

- **Q (Round 1): Per-level curves or one whole-run curve?**
  - Answer (operator): **(b) per-level curves with configurable per-level wave counts.**
  - Source: interactive reply.
  - Research: the sequencer takes a single `defaultShootEnabled` for a whole call and returns one group per curve entry — a whole-run curve cannot vary the fire rule by level. Read `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts`.

- **Q (Round 1): Where does the curve (and its override) live?**
  - Answer (operator): **(b) extend the CSV `configStore` with a new difficulty-curve file.**
  - Source: interactive reply.
  - Research: `configStore`/`csv.ts` are CSV-backed and read-only in production; `rules.ts` is the localStorage tunables store. Read `src/core/configStore.ts`, `src/core/csv.ts`.

- **Q (Round 2): When generated mode is enabled, does the campaign skeleton stay fixed?**
  - Answer (operator): **(a) config also defines level count and names — fully data-driven campaign.**
  - Source: interactive reply.
  - Note: boss still triggers after the final configured level via existing `WaveManager` behaviour.

- **Q (Round 2): How editable is the new difficulty-curve CSV?**
  - Answer (operator): **as recommended** — route it through the existing CSV pipeline (editable in dev, bundled read-only in production).
  - Source: interactive reply.

- **Q (Round 2): Where do the default target values come from?**
  - Answer (operator): **as recommended** — seed per-level defaults from the current `LEVELS` measured scores, spread non-decreasingly across waves.
  - Source: interactive reply.
  - Research: `levelDifficulty(LEVELS[i].waves).score` in `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts`; campaign calibration regression in `src/waves/enemyDifficulty.campaign.test.ts`.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MTCP1CKB00480BD** – Diver jumps on return from dive (completed)
- **AH-0MT7V5UH90023XWR** – Clarify enemy health / one-hit destruction model in GDD (completed)
- **AH-0MU0F1T2H003B4K0** – Swarm are too powerful when shooting (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: acceptance, accepts, actual, adjusting, allow (+182 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: accepts, affect, asteroid, auto, back (+161 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: 0mudiwetp003xc3x, actual, archetypes, asserts, asteroid (+155 more)

## Plan update (2026-09-28) — follow-on children

Four follow-on children were attached to this item after its first audit, because the feature is in_review on `dev` but not yet released to `main` and the changes below revise its shipped behaviour. They have now been planned and are ready for implementation in dependency order:

1. Per-wave generation modes: curve-fixed, hand-authored fixed and dynamic runtime regeneration (AH-0MUJSUQD8003FSUT) — open/intake_complete.
2. Curve generator: per-wave generation-mode control with read-only derived difficulty (AH-0MUJSUT8P008UPQM) — blocked by AH-0MUJSUQD8003FSUT.
3. Retune the default difficulty curve and seed campaign for playability (AH-0MUJSUTXI008NP8K) — blocked by AH-0MUJSUQD8003FSUT.
4. Enable sequenced wave generation by default with a mixed-mode initial campaign (AH-0MUJSUTLA006Q8E1) — blocked by AH-0MUJSUQD8003FSUT, AH-0MUJSUT8P008UPQM and AH-0MUJSUTXI008NP8K.

### Superseded decision (recorded, not removed)

**Decision 1 (Opt-in toggle, default off)** and the **Opt-in toggle** acceptance criterion above are superseded by **Enable sequenced wave generation by default with a mixed-mode initial campaign (AH-0MUJSUTLA006Q8E1)**: the shipped default becomes `sequencedWavesEnabled = true` with an explicit opt-out. The criterion above is retained for traceability; the authoritative behaviour is default-on with opt-out, verified by that child, which also updates the README / GDD / design-doc default-off statements.

### Scope reconciliation

**Support mixed generated and scripted levels in a campaign (AH-0MUH7Q6HN0006QPD)** (open/in_review) is superseded and absorbed by (1): its per-level `source` (`generated`/`scripted`) is generalised to a per-wave `generation` (`curve`/`fixed`/`dynamic`) mode, mapping `scripted` → `fixed` and `generated` → `curve`, with the legacy `source` column accepted for backward compatibility. The producer should confirm closing AH-0MUH7Q6HN0006QPD as superseded.

# Goal

Fix the audit runner's parent-first flow so that child `partial` verdicts caused by unserviced in-main-slot items are treated as "not assessed" rather than blocking the parent's readiness-to-close decision, and add diagnostic clarity.

# Background

In `--child-in-main-slot` mode (default), child Phase-1 AC screens and Phase-2 deep analysis emit `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` items for the invoking agent session. In non-interactive runs (e.g. downtime workers), these items are never serviced, leaving all child AC verdicts as `partial`.

Currently, `_build_issue_json` treats ALL `partial` verdicts as unacceptable, causing the parent to report "Ready to close: No" even when all parent ACs are met, because the child partials (from unserviced in-main-slot work) are counted as failures.

# Implementation Plan

## 1. Track in-main-slot partial verdicts

Add a `verdict_reason` field to child AC results when they are `partial` due to in-main-slot unserviced work. The `_phase1_review_child_acs` and `_deep_analyze_child` functions already set `verdict: "partial"` with evidence like `"pending (main-session review)"` in in-main-slot mode. We need to mark these explicitly with `verdict_reason: "unserviced-in-main-slot"`.

## 2. Handle partials in `_build_issue_json`

Modify `all_ac_acceptable` computation to skip child ACs whose `partial` verdict has `verdict_reason == "unserviced-in-main-slot"`. These should be treated as "not assessed" and NOT block the parent's readiness-to-close decision.

## 3. Add diagnostic output

In the audit summary/JSON output, surface a clear diagnostic that distinguishes:
- Children with `partial` verdicts from unserviced in-main-slot work → "not assessed"
- Children with genuine `partial` or `unmet` verdicts → "not-ready"

Add a `children_assessment` section to the `_build_issue_json` output listing `unserviced_in_main_slot` child IDs and `genuine_not_ready` child IDs.

# Acceptance Criteria
- AC2: Parent audit treats in-main-slot unserviced partials as "not assessed" (does NOT block ready-to-close)
- AC3: Audit output includes diagnostic distinguishing unserviced-in-main-slot partials from genuine failures

# Constraints
- Must not change behaviour of interactive runs (where agent CAN service in-main-slot items)
- Must be backward-compatible with persisted audit results

# Key Files
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_phase1_review_child_acs`, `_deep_analyze_child`, `_build_issue_json`
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_child_in_main_slot.py` — existing in-main-slot tests
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_freshness.py` — freshness tests (verify no regression)

# Support mixed generated and scripted levels in a campaign

## Problem statement

**Wire the runtime auto-sequencer into the game's wave generation (AH-0MUH6LEYY0054E63)** makes the campaign all-or-nothing: with `sequencedWavesEnabled` off every level uses the hand-authored static `LEVELS`, and with it on *every* level is generated from the difficulty-curve config. A designer cannot hand-tune the levels that matter (onboarding, boss lead-in, a specific set-piece) while letting the sequencer ramp the rest. This item lets a single campaign **mix** generated and scripted levels, selected per level.

## Users

- As a **designer**, I want to mark individual levels as generated or scripted, so I can hand-tune onboarding and set-piece levels while the sequencer handles the rest.
- As a **player**, I want the campaign to keep its hand-authored early levels but ramp difficulty in later levels, so each run is both learnable and challenging.
- As a **maintainer**, I want a single, data-driven campaign definition whose generated and scripted sources are explicit and testable, so the two paths cannot silently diverge.

## Decisions confirmed at intake

1. **Selector is an explicit `source` column in `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv`** (`generated` | `scripted`). `source` defaults to `generated` when absent, so the existing 4-column CSV and `defaultDifficultyCurves()` keep working unchanged. For `scripted` rows `targetDifficulty` is optional/ignored (the level's waves come from `LEVELS`, not the curve). A level number must declare one consistent source; rows that disagree are malformed.
2. **Campaign skeleton starts from static `LEVELS`.** The merged campaign contains all static levels 1–5 (used verbatim when a level is `scripted` or unlisted), overrides a level when configured as `generated`, and appends configured generated levels numbered beyond `LEVEL_COUNT` in ascending order. Result is sorted ascending by `level`.
3. **Fallback is per-level.** A `generated` level with an empty/malformed curve (or a `sequencer` throw) falls back to that level's static `LEVELS` definition when one exists; a generated level with no static counterpart (number beyond `LEVEL_COUNT`) is skipped. Whole-campaign fallback to static `LEVELS` only when the candidate pool is empty or the resulting campaign would be empty. No path may yield an unplayable campaign or crash.

## Existing state

- **Campaign builder** — `buildSequencedLevels(rows?, candidates?)` in `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` groups `DifficultyCurveRow[]` by level, calls the read-only `sequencer()` once per generated level with `defaultShootEnabled = level >= FIRST_FIRING_LEVEL (4)`, converts `ShootableWave.groups` to `WaveGroup`s and returns `LevelDefinition[]`. On empty/degenerate input or a sequencer throw it returns static `LEVELS` (whole-campaign fallback). It has **no notion of a per-level source**.
- **Config** — `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` is one row per `(level, wave)` with columns `level,levelName,wave,targetDifficulty`; loaded by `loadDifficultyCurves()` (`src/core/configStore.ts`) through the CSV pipeline (dev `/api/csv/...`, bundled `?raw` in production) with `defaultDifficultyCurves()` computed from the static `LEVELS` calibration as the fallback. Types live in `src/core/configTypes.ts` (`DifficultyCurveRow`); codec/validator in `src/core/csv.ts` (`parseDifficultyCurves` / `serializeDifficultyCurves` / `validateDifficultyCurveRow`). Malformed files fall back wholesale to the computed default curve.
- **Static campaign** — `LEVELS` in `src/waves/Formations.ts`: five `LevelDefinition`s (names, waves, `shootEnabled`). Levels 1–3 do not fire; 4–5 do (GDD §2.4/§2.5).
- **Wiring** — `PlayScene` exposes `resolveCampaignLevels(rules, build)`: toggle off ⇒ static `LEVELS`; toggle on ⇒ `buildSequencedLevels()`, falling back to `LEVELS` on empty/throw. `GameRules.sequencedWavesEnabled` (default `false`) lives in `src/core/rules.ts`. `WaveManager` accepts injected `LevelDefinition[]` and progresses by **array index** — `WaveManager.level` is `index + 1`, so `LevelDefinition.level` is display metadata and the merged array must be ordered ascending.

## Desired change

Extend the campaign builder so each level's source is selectable, and merge the two sources into one ordered `LevelDefinition[]`:

- A level marked **`generated`** is produced by `sequencer()` from that level's curve rows (as today, `shootEnabled` from the level's fire rule).
- A level marked **`scripted`** is taken **byte-for-byte from static `LEVELS`** (its own waves and `shootEnabled`) and is never passed to the sequencer.
- All static levels remain present unless overridden; generated levels beyond the static five are appended. See the confirmed decisions above.

When `sequencedWavesEnabled` is **off**, behaviour is unchanged: static `LEVELS` exactly. Mixed mode is only reachable with the toggle on.

## Acceptance criteria

- **Explicit source selector** — `DifficultyCurveRow`/`parseDifficultyCurves`/`serializeDifficultyCurves`/`validateDifficultyCurveRow` support a `source` field (`generated` | `scripted`) that defaults to `generated` when absent; the existing 4-column CSV and `defaultDifficultyCurves()` still parse and round-trip, and `source` survives a codec round-trip; `targetDifficulty` is required only for `generated` rows (ignored for `scripted` rows), and a level whose rows declare conflicting `source` values is treated as malformed (whole-file fallback to the computed default).
- **Mixed merge** — a config that marks one level scripted and another generated yields a campaign containing both: the scripted level deep-equals the matching static `LEVELS` definition (name, waves, groups, spacing, positions and `shootEnabled`), and the generated level's waves come from `sequencer()`.
- **Campaign skeleton** — all static levels 1–5 are present unless overridden; a configured generated level numbered beyond `LEVEL_COUNT` is appended; the returned array is ordered ascending by `level`.
- **Generated equivalence and determinism** — a generated level inside a mixed campaign is identical to the all-generated builder output for the same curve and candidate pool, and building the same mixed config twice yields identical definitions (no RNG/clock/I-O).
- **Fire rule per source** — generated levels 1–3 have `shootEnabled=false` and 4+ `true`; scripted levels keep `LEVELS`' own flags (test asserts both).
- **Per-level fallback is safe** — a generated level with an empty/malformed curve falls back to its static `LEVELS` definition while the rest of the mixed campaign is preserved; a generated level with no static counterpart is skipped; an empty candidate pool or an empty resulting campaign falls back to static `LEVELS`; none of these crash (test covers each case).
- **Runtime wiring** — with `sequencedWavesEnabled` on and a mixed config, `resolveCampaignLevels`/`PlayScene` run the mixed campaign; with it off they run static `LEVELS` exactly (test asserts both paths).
- **Testing/validation** — new/updated unit and integration tests cover the selector codec, mixed merge, scripted deep-equality, generated equivalence, skeleton ordering, fire rule, determinism and every fallback branch, and they are meaningful and passing.
- **Documentation** — all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, the README, `docs/Game Design Document.md` and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (the new `source` column and mixed-campaign behaviour).
- **No regressions** — the full project test suite must pass with the new changes (`npm test`).

## Constraints

- **Pure core stays pure** — `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` must not be modified (read-only call site).
- **Determinism** — generation remains a pure function of config + candidate pool; scripted levels are static data.
- **No behavioural change when the toggle is off** — existing `WaveManager`/`PlayScene`/campaign tests pass unchanged.
- **CSV pipeline is the source of truth** — the new field goes through the existing codec/`configStore`/Vite plugin pattern; malformed rows must not crash.
- **Backwards compatibility** — the existing 4-column `difficulty-curves.csv` and `defaultDifficultyCurves()` must keep working unchanged.
- **Ordering** — the merged campaign is ordered ascending by `level` because `WaveManager` progresses by array index.
- UK English in prose; Markdown in the work item.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` — per-level source selection and scripted/generated merge; keep the fallback guard.
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.test.ts` — mixed-campaign tests (source selection, scripted deep-equality, generated equivalence, skeleton ordering, fallback).
- `src/core/configTypes.ts` — add `source: 'generated' | 'scripted'` to `DifficultyCurveRow`.
- `src/core/csv.ts` — extend `DIFFICULTY_CURVE_COLUMN_ORDER`, `parseDifficultyCurves`, `serializeDifficultyCurves` and `validateDifficultyCurveRow` for the optional `source` field.
- `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` — add the `source` column (all existing rows `generated`).
- `src/core/configStore.ts` — keep `defaultDifficultyCurves()` and `resolveDifficultyCurves()` consistent with the defaulted `source`.
- `src/waves/Formations.ts` — static `LEVELS` referenced as the scripted source (read-only).
- `src/core/rules.ts` — existing `sequencedWavesEnabled` toggle (unchanged).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `resolveCampaignLevels` consumes the mixed builder (verify).
- `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts` — validation for the new optional column.
- Test files: `src/core/csv.test.ts`, `src/core/configStore.test.ts`, `src/data/csv-seed.test.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`.
- Docs: `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§2.4/§2.5), `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (§9 sequencer), `README.md`.

## Related work

- **Wire the runtime auto-sequencer into the game's wave generation (AH-0MUH6LEYY0054E63)** — the opt-in wiring this builds on; defers mixed campaigns to this item.
- **Implement runtime auto-sequencer for dynamic difficulty adjustment (AH-0MUDIWETP003XC3X)** — delivered `sequencer()`.
- **Campaign builder: config to generated level definitions (AH-0MUITS0VD000DVSV)** — delivered `buildSequencedLevels()` (completed).

- **Create Dev Utilities gym scene with curve editor and wave preview (AH-0MUGXDVPH005TIZL)** — designer curve tool; out of scope here.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §2.4/§2.5 fire rules, §3.2 level themes.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — §9 enemy difficulty scoring / sequencer.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Config-schema churn** — the `source` field changes `DifficultyCurveRow`, the codec and the CSV just defined by AH-0MUITRZZE000OYQE; mitigated by defaulting the field to `generated` so existing rows/tests are unaffected and the 4-column form stays valid.
- **Optional `targetDifficulty` for scripted rows** — validation must require a target only for `generated` rows; a scripted row's target is ignored. Tests must pin both.
- **Level numbering vs display** — `WaveManager.level` is the array index + 1, so appended generated levels display by position, not by their configured `level` number. The merged array is kept ascending; this caveat is documented rather than changing `WaveManager`.
- **Mixed-source rows** — a level whose rows disagree on `source` is malformed; the existing all-or-nothing resolver falls back to the computed default (generated) curve. A test pins this.
- **Scope creep** — runtime curve editing (AH-0MUGXDVPH005TIZL) and any sequencer-algorithm change are out of scope; extra opportunities are recorded as linked work items.
- **Assumption (toggle interaction)** — mixed mode is only active when `sequencedWavesEnabled` is on; when off, static `LEVELS` is used unchanged.
- **Assumption (scripted source is `LEVELS`)** — scripted levels are referenced by level number into static `LEVELS`; no new hand-authored wave data is introduced.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q (Round 1): How should the per-level source selector (generated vs scripted) be declared?**
  - Answer (producer): **(a) explicit `source` column in `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` (`generated` | `scripted`)**.
  - Source: asynchronous producer reply.
  - Consequence: `DifficultyCurveRow`/codec/validator/CSV gain an optional `source` (default `generated`); `targetDifficulty` becomes optional for `scripted` rows.
- **Q (Round 1): What determines the campaign skeleton and ordering when mixing?**
  - Answer (producer): **(a) start from all static `LEVELS`, override configured levels per source, append generated levels numbered beyond `LEVEL_COUNT`**.
  - Source: asynchronous producer reply.
  - Consequence: levels 1–5 always present; configured generated levels override; extra generated levels appended ascending; array ordered by `level`.
- **Q (Round 1): What is the fallback scope when a generated level has no usable curve?**
  - Answer (producer): **(a) per-level — use that level's static `LEVELS` definition if one exists, otherwise apply a safe guard**.
  - Source: asynchronous producer reply.
  - Consequence: one bad generated level does not discard the rest of the campaign; whole-campaign fallback only for an empty candidate pool or empty result.
- **Assumption (documented, not asked): mixed mode is only active while `sequencedWavesEnabled` is on.** Evidence: `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` reaches `buildSequencedLevels()` only through `resolveCampaignLevels`'s toggle-on branch (AH-0MUITS1SM008GPR9, completed).


## Open questions

- **OPEN QUESTION (non-blocking, for producer):** How should a level marked
  `scripted` but numbered beyond `LEVEL_COUNT` (no matching static `LEVELS`
  definition) be handled? Intake decision 2 only *appends* generated levels
  beyond `LEVEL_COUNT`, so a scripted level 6+ has no source. Assumed safe
  default (documented, pending confirmation): skip it — consistent with a
  generated level that has no static counterpart. This affects only an
  unconfigured edge case; the pinned ACs are implementable without the answer.

## Plan: changelog

  approval gate not requested). Clarified AC 1 to pin `targetDifficulty`
  optionality for `scripted` rows and the per-level mixed-source malformed

# Intake brief — Flaky PlayScene wave-transition test (isTransitioning timing)

**Headline:** The PlayScene integration suite intermittently asserts `isTransitioning() === false` immediately after the `killAllEnemies()` helper clears a wave. The flake is a timing/ordering nondeterminism in how a wave-clear starts the transition (not a gameplay bug), and it makes the full-suite gate untrustworthy under parallel load. Remove the nondeterminism at its source and prove reliability with repeated parallel runs, without weakening any transition coverage.

## Problem statement

`src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` contains ~19 assertions of the form `expect(scene.isTransitioning()).toBe(true)` immediately after `killAllEnemies(scene)`. Under full-suite parallel CPU load these intermittently fail with `AssertionError: expected false to be true`. Three occurrences are already recorded on this item (2026-09-25/26) across *different* transition tests, so this is a shared timing/ordering race in transition-start detection after clearing a wave, not a single fragile assertion:

- `AC5 — clearing a wave starts a transition, then spawns the next wave` (line 443 at the failing revision).
- `AH-0MU7JTG9R002ZWA6 AC4 — the timer resets per wave and is hidden during transitions` (line 665 at the failing revision).
- `AH-0MU7JTF9W008B8HW AC4 — the next wave spawns and gameplay resumes after the pause` (line 594 at the failing revision).

Every reported instance passed on a forced fresh `run_tests.py --scope full --force --rerun-failures`, confirming the failure is load-sensitive. A flaky full-suite gate erodes trust in the project's primary correctness signal and can mask or falsely raise real regressions.

Original failure log (preserved from the item):

```
FAIL  src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts > PlayScene — playable run (AH-0MU7305Z2003NII3) > AC5 — clearing a wave starts a transition, then spawns the next wave
AssertionError: expected false to be true // Object.is equality
 ❯ src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts:443:37
    441|     killAllEnemies(scene);
    442|     // Wave 1 wiped → a transition is running (no new enemies yet).
    443|     expect(scene.isTransitioning()).toBe(true);
```

## Users

- **Developer / CI gate** — needs the verification suite to be a reliable pass/fail signal.
  - *As a developer, I want the PlayScene transition tests to give the same result on every run, so a green suite actually means my change is safe.*
- **Producer / reviewer** — needs to trust the `test` skill's full-suite gate before `in_review`.
  - *As a producer, I want flaky failures eliminated rather than re-run until green, so review decisions are based on evidence and not luck.*
- **Tester** — needs the wave-transition behaviour coverage kept intact while the flake is removed.
  - *As a tester, I want the same transition assertions to still execute, so fixing the flake does not silently drop coverage.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Root cause identified and documented.** The flakiness source is demonstrated with evidence (a failing reproduction under parallel load plus the code path that produces the nondeterministic state), and recorded in a comment on this item. The analysis explicitly distinguishes test-harness nondeterminism from any production accounting/ordering bug in `PlayScene`/`WaveManager`.
- [ ] **AC2 — Transition-start detection made deterministic.** The wave-clear → transition-start path is deterministic under parallel load: after a wave is cleared (or within a bounded, explicitly awaited/driven step) `isTransitioning()` reflects the transition reliably. The fix follows the established deterministic `scene.tick(dt)` + poll idiom already used for prior flakes (AH-0MTFTIZX7005DNFW), not wall-clock waits.
- [ ] **AC3 — Coverage preserved (no weakened assertions).** All existing wave-transition assertions remain exercised; no assertion is deleted, loosened, skipped, or replaced by a tautology. If a shared helper (e.g. `killAllEnemies`/`finishTransition`) changes, it must still drive the real transition path, and the `PlayScene` transition suites must still pass.
- [ ] **AC4 — Reliability evidence under parallel load.** The full suite (`/skill:test`, `npm test`) passes on 3 consecutive runs (matching the precedent bar in AH-0MTFSM3IR001QR0C), and the focused `PlayScene.test.ts` transition tests pass repeatedly under load (documented run count/command). Where the flake was reproducible before the fix, the reproduction is re-run and shown green.
- [ ] **AC5 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `README.md`, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (notably the `src/test/gameHarness.ts` boot behaviour and the deterministic-tick convention if touched).
- [ ] **AC6 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.** Run the complete suite via `/skill:test` (`npm test`) and confirm zero failures.

## Constraints

- **Do not mask the flake.** Weakening, deleting, or skipping assertions to make the suite green is explicitly out of scope.
- **Preserve gameplay behaviour.** This is a test-determinism / accounting-correctness fix; observable game behaviour must not change.
- **Prefer the established idiom.** Deterministic accumulated `scene.tick(dt)` + condition polling over real wall-clock waits, per the precedent items (AH-0MTFTIZX7005DNFW, AH-0MTFSM3IR001QR0C).
- **Scope discipline.** Prefer a PlayScene-local fix. Only change the shared boot harness (`src/test/gameHarness.ts`) if root-cause evidence points there, and then re-run the full suite because it affects every Phaser suite.
- **Minimum churn.** Match existing style; do not delete unrelated dead code (report it instead).
- **No `CHANGELOG.md` edits** (managed by the ship/release pipeline).
- **Push only to `dev`.**

## Existing state

Confirmed by inspection (2026-09-27, HEAD `493357b` on `dev`, clean tree):

- `src/test/gameHarness.ts` `bootScene()` boots a real `Phaser.Game` and waits a **fixed real-time `setTimeout(150)`** (`bootDelay`) while Phaser's requestAnimationFrame loop is live. Comment in `gameHarness.ts` says it "waits for the scene to become active"; test comments elsewhere acknowledge the "Phaser loop draining a few frames during the boot delay". This is a known nondeterminism surface (also noted in `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.test.ts:151` — "formationX drifts during bootDelay (~150ms)").
- `PlayScene.test.ts` helpers:
  - `killAllEnemies(scene)` (line ~78) loops up to 500 times: find first alive enemy, `spawnPlayerBullet(enemy.x, enemy.y, 0, 0)`, `scene.tick(0.016)` — exits when `getAliveCount() === 0`.
  - `finishTransition(scene)` (line ~87) only ticks if `scene.isTransitioning()`; a silently-absent transition therefore surfaces as a later assertion failure.
  - `bootPlay()` (line ~191) calls `bootScene()` then *after* boot disables the random asteroid spawner.
- Transition machinery in `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`:
  - `tick(dt)` computes `transitioning = this.transitionTimer > 0` **once at the top**; `_handleCollisions()` runs only when not transitioning; `_handleAsteroidCollisions()` runs during a transition.
  - `_advanceAfterKill()` → `waveManager.onEnemyDestroyed()` → on `waveCleared`/`levelCleared` calls `_startTransition()` (sets `transitionTimer = LEVEL_TRANSITION_SECONDS` = 1.5 s, hides timer, shows banner).
  - `_advanceAfterTimeout()` replays `wm.enemiesAlive` destructions after a wave-timeout detonation.
  - `isTransitioning()` returns `this.transitionTimer > 0` (line ~1638).
- Accounting in `src/waves/WaveManager.ts`: `onEnemyDestroyed()` decrements `_enemiesAlive` and returns the `WaveEvent`; `registerDynamicSpawn()` / `unregisterDynamicSpawn()` adjust `_enemiesAlive` for dynamic spawns (asteroids/splits). A register/unregister desync would leave `_enemiesAlive > 0` with no live entities, so no `waveCleared` event and no transition.
- The first wave of the default campaign (`src/waves/Formations.ts`) is `noFire(group('scout', 'v', 6, …))` — 6 non-firing scouts, no asteroids when the spawner is disabled. The failing tests use `bootPlay()` with the spawner disabled, so random asteroid spawning is not the trigger in those tests.
- `vitest.config.ts` runs the suite with the default parallel pool (happy-dom + stubbed Phaser canvas); `PlayScene.test.ts` already raises its per-file timeout to 20 s (`vi.setConfig({ testTimeout: 20000 })`, added by AH-0MUIPP1UU000UT88) — that addressed timeouts, not this assertion flake.

## Desired change

1. **Reproduce under load.** Establish a reliable reproduction of the `isTransitioning() === false` flake (e.g. repeated/parallel `PlayScene.test.ts` runs or full-suite runs while the machine is loaded) so the fix can be validated before/after.
2. **Root-cause the nondeterminism** along the wave-clear → transition-start path. Leading hypotheses to confirm or eliminate with evidence:
   - **H1 (boot harness):** the live Phaser loop advances the scene an unpredictable amount during the fixed 150 ms `bootDelay`, so the scene state (enemy positions/drift, wave timer, already-killed enemies, diver states) feeding `killAllEnemies` is nondeterministic under load.
   - **H2 (kill helper ordering):** `killAllEnemies` asserts completion only via `getAliveCount() === 0`; if the final kill happens through a path (or ordering) that does not drive `_advanceAfterKill()`/`_startTransition()`, the transition never starts despite zero live enemies.
   - **H3 (production accounting/ordering):** a real `WaveManager` `_enemiesAlive` register/unregister desync (e.g. dynamic spawns) or transition-timer ordering bug leaves the wave not marked cleared.
3. **Fix at the root**, preferring deterministic tick-driven helpers (H1/H2) and correcting any genuine production accounting/ordering defect (H3). Keep assertions real.
4. **Add a regression guard** so the determinism cannot silently regress (e.g. a deterministic helper/assertion that fails loudly if a wave clear does not start the transition, or a documented repeated-run check).
5. **Verify** with repeated focused and full-suite runs under parallel load; record commands and results on the item.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/test/gameHarness.ts` — **primary suspect**: `bootScene()`/`bootDelay` real-time boot; freeze or deterministically drive the Phaser loop if H1 is confirmed.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — `killAllEnemies` / `finishTransition` / `bootPlay` helpers and the ~19 `isTransitioning()` assertions; make clearing/transition detection deterministic without weakening assertions.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `tick()` transition branch, `_advanceAfterKill`, `_advanceAfterTimeout`, `_startTransition`, `isTransitioning`; fix only if H2/H3 confirm a production ordering/accounting defect.
- `src/waves/WaveManager.ts` — `onEnemyDestroyed`, `registerDynamicSpawn`, `unregisterDynamicSpawn`, `enemiesAlive`; fix if H3 confirms a desync.
- `src/scenes/PlaySceneHUD.test.ts` / `src/scenes/PlayScenePause.test.ts` — sibling PlayScene suites to check for the same pattern (shared helper changes must not break them).
- `README.md` — whichever docs section describes the test harness / flaky-test policy, if the convention changes.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — fixing the harness globally.** Pausing/freezing the Phaser loop in `bootScene()` would make many suites deterministic but could alter suites that intentionally rely on real frames. *Mitigation:* scope first, add an opt-in/explicit deterministic mode, and run the full suite.
- **Risk — masking a production bug with a test-only change.** If H3 is real, a test-only fix would hide a gameplay accounting defect. *Mitigation:* AC1 requires the root cause to be distinguished and documented; if a production defect is found, fix it in production code.
- **Risk — over-decrement / early wave-clear.** If the fix touches `WaveManager` accounting, the inverse failure (transition starts with enemies still alive) must not be introduced; existing `AC5` alive-count assertions guard this.
- **Risk — flake not reproducible.** The item's first occurrence already passed on a forced fresh run. *Mitigation:* use parallel/loaded reproduction runs first; if still not reproducible, capture a state-dump/diagnostic and document the root cause from code analysis, with the deterministic helper as the defensive fix.
- **Risk — scope creep into a harness-wide refactor.** *Mitigation:* record extra opportunities as linked work items rather than expanding this one.
- **Assumption — root-cause-driven scope.** No single fix approach (test-only vs production) is mandated up front; the correct scope follows from AC1's root-cause finding. Based on the repo evidence, H1/H2 (test harness) are the most likely and the preferred first focus.
- **Assumption — reliability bar.** "Deterministic" is demonstrated by 3 consecutive green full-suite runs (project precedent) plus repeated focused runs under load.
- **Assumption — no gameplay change** is intended; if the root cause proves to be a production ordering/accounting bug, the resulting fix must preserve observable gameplay and be covered by existing transition tests.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUDCT7EU0061OSZ** — Extract shared combat core into standalone gym scenes (completed): the parent/discovery context. The first occurrence was reported during **AH-0MUH5GKAX00323IJ** — Refactor CombatScene to extend CombatCoreScene (completed), and was judged unrelated to that refactor.
- **AH-0MUGCP15V0008339** — Test — PlayScene spawner integration tests (completed): the PlayScene integration/spawner test suite this item hardens.
- **AH-0MU7JTG9R002ZWA6** — Wave time limit per wave (timer resets/hides during transitions): owns one of the failing tests.
- **AH-0MU7JTF9W008B8HW** — Player control during transitions: owns another failing test.
- **AH-0MU7JTEMC006QPSN** — Transient transition banner: another transition test in the same area.
- **AH-0MU8TWF1H007OG2L** — Carried-over asteroid behaviour during transition: the dynamic-spawn accounting this flake could interact with.
- **Precedent flake fixes (pattern to reuse):**
  - **AH-0MTFTIZX7005DNFW** — GymDiver AC1 wall-clock flaky: fixed by deterministic accumulated `scene.tick(dt)` + `DIVING`-state polling instead of `waitMs` (commit `c2aaa54`).
  - **AH-0MTFSM3IR001QR0C** — GymScout.test.ts flaky under full-suite parallel load (completed): deterministic ticks + polling; 3 consecutive green full-suite runs as the bar.
  - **AH-0MTFTJ01K000JG4I** — GymSwarm AC3 aimed-fire flaky under full-suite parallel load (completed).
- **AH-0MUIPP1UU000UT88** — Raise PlayScene integration-test timeout for full-suite load: prior, adjacent full-suite-load hardening of the same file (addressed timeouts, not this assertion flake).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUGCP15V0008339** – Test — PlayScene spawner integration tests (completed)
- **AH-0MUIG1AFG00938TV** – Test: shared mineral kill-drop rule (open)
- **AH-0MU8QVQQV006T0KI** – PlayScene: add per-weapon player fire audio cues (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: 0mudct7eu0061osz, ac5, acceptance, assertion, await (+72 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0mudct7eu0061osz, ac5, behaviour, bounded, cause (+57 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: 0mudct7eu0061osz, assertion, await, awaited, behaviour (+55 more)

## Traceability

- `discovered-from:AH-0MUDCT7EU0061OSZ`
- First observed during `AH-0MUH5GKAX00323IJ` (CombatScene refactor, completed) — judged unrelated to that refactor.

## Appendix — Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required for this intake. The seed context, the three recorded occurrences, and the repository evidence were sufficient to define the problem, users, acceptance criteria, constraints and predicted key files above. There is no blocking open question; the one design choice below is recorded for producer visibility.

- **Q (self-answered, non-blocking) — Scope: test-only determinism vs. production fix?**
  - **Answer / recommendation:** Root-cause-driven. Fix the test harness / `killAllEnemies` helpers if the cause is test nondeterminism (leading hypotheses H1/H2), but fix `PlayScene`/`WaveManager` in production if the cause is a genuine accounting/ordering defect (H3). Per AGENTS.md, documented reasonable assumptions are acceptable; the producer may override and require one specific scope.
  - **Source:** Repository inspection, operator-supplied item description ("Test (or the underlying transition trigger) made deterministic"), and AGENTS.md precedent (AH-0MTFTIZX7005DNFW).
  - **Research summary:** `bootScene()` waits a fixed real-time 150 ms with a live Phaser loop (H1); `killAllEnemies` asserts only `getAliveCount()===0` (H2); `WaveManager.registerDynamicSpawn`/`unregisterDynamicSpawn` can desync `_enemiesAlive` (H3). Handled as AC1 to be resolved with evidence rather than pre-decided.

# Enemy gym: P3 shield and P6 phase shift do not work when collected (hit-gating not shared)

## Seed intent (operator)

In the enemies gym scene some power-ups — at least phase shift (P6) and shield (P3) — do not work when collected. This suggests these scenes (at least the diver) are not using the same code as other scenes. Perform a root-cause analysis and ensure shared code is used so behaviour is the same in all scenes.

## Raw evidence

- Operator report: collecting P6 Phase Shift or P3 Shield in the enemy gym has no observable defensive effect (player still takes hits).
- Hint: 'at least the diver' — the Diver is an enemy-config key routed to the single reusable `GymEnemies` scene (GymIndex boots `GymEnemies` with `{ enemyKey }` for every non-boss enemy config).

## Problem statement

In the enemy gym scene (`GymEnemies`, used for every enemy config including the
Diver), collecting P3 Shield or P6 Phase Shift has no defensive effect: the
player still takes hits and loses a life. The effects are recorded in the shared
`EffectsRegistry` (the standalone HUD shows them active), but the shared combat
base's hit path never consults them for the formation-gym scenes, so the player
is not actually shielded or phased.

## Root cause analysis

- `PlayScene` and `GymPowerUpsCombat` each **override** `isPlayerPhased()` and
  `tryAbsorbPlayerHit()` to consult their `EffectsRegistry`.
- `GymFormationScene` (the base for `GymEnemies`, `GymBoss`, `GymMinerals`) does
  **not** override either hook, so it inherits the `CombatCoreScene` defaults
  `isPlayerPhased() → false` and `tryAbsorbPlayerHit() → false`.
- `CombatScene._handleCollisions()` calls `isPlayerPhased()` before the
  bullet-vs-player and body-vs-player passes, and `CombatScene._hitPlayer()`
  calls `tryAbsorbPlayerHit()` first. Both return the defaults in the formation
  gyms, so P3/P6 never gate a hit.
- Consequently the single reusable enemy gym scene (`GymEnemies` with
  `{ enemyKey }`, e.g. `diver`) records the collected effect but behaves
  differently from `PlayScene` and `GymPowerUpsCombat` — a divergence from the
  documented shared-core invariant in `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`
  §2.1 ("The shipped game and the gyms therefore cannot diverge on collision,
  auto-fire, drops, teleport or player-hit behaviour").
- Other power-ups are unaffected and confirm the diagnosis: P4 Bomb works
  (`_collectDrop` → shared `_clearEnemyBullets()`, wired through
  `getEnemyBullets()`/`setEnemyBullets()`); P5/P9 speed and fire-rate
  multipliers are applied in `GymFormationScene` (~line 1209); P7 Teleport works
  via the shared `_handleTeleport()`.
- Secondary divergence: `GymFormationScene` draws no shield bubble or phase
  ghost, so even once gating is fixed the player has no on-screen cue that P3/P6
  is active, unlike `PlayScene`/`GymPowerUpsCombat`.

## Users (user stories)

- As a player training against enemies in the enemy gym, when I fly over a P6
  Phase Shift drop I expect to pass through enemy bullets and enemy bodies
  without being hit, exactly as in the real run.
- As a player training in the enemy gym, when I fly over a P3 Shield drop I
  expect the next hit to be absorbed (one hit), with the shield popping and a
  brief invulnerability blink, without losing a life.
- As a maintainer, I expect phase/shield hit-gating to live in one shared place
  so a fix in one scene cannot silently miss the others.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — P6 phase immunity in the enemy gym:** With the power-up layer active in `GymEnemies` (any `enemyKey`, including `diver`), collecting P6 Phase Shift makes the player immune to enemy bullets and enemy body contact for the effect duration (no `playerHitCount` increment, no life loss, no respawn); on expiry the next hit lands normally. Verified by an automated test on a `GymFormationScene`-based scene.
- [ ] **AC2 — P3 shield absorbs one hit in the enemy gym:** Collecting P3 Shield causes exactly the next hit to be absorbed: the shield is consumed (registry no longer shielded), the post-hit invulnerability window starts, and the player does not lose a life; the following hit lands normally. Verified by an automated test on a `GymFormationScene`-based scene.
- [ ] **AC3 — single shared implementation:** Phase/shield hit-gating is implemented once in the shared combat base (`CombatCoreScene`/`CombatScene`) backed by the inherited `EffectsRegistry`; the now-redundant duplicate overrides in `PlayScene` and `GymPowerUpsCombat` are removed or reduced to scene-specific extras (e.g. per-type cue/VFX), and an equivalence test asserts `PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene` and `GymPowerUpsCombat` route phase/shield through the same shared hooks.
- [ ] **AC4 — consistent player feedback:** `GymFormationScene`-based scenes render the same shield-bubble (P3) and phase-ghost (P6) player visuals as `PlayScene`/`GymPowerUpsCombat`, so the active effect is observable in the enemy gym.
- [ ] **AC5 — documentation:** `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (and any other docs describing power-up/hit behaviour) is updated to state that shield/phase gating is shared and lists the new shared hooks.
- [ ] **AC6 — validation:** An automated test/validation criterion is satisfied across the affected scenes (new regression tests fail before the fix and pass after it).
- [ ] **AC7 — full suite:** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- All implementation must happen in the worktree created by
  `implement.py start`; build → test → commit order, never reversed.
- Do not regress the shipped game: `PlayScene` invulnerability duration
  (`PLAYER_RESPAWN_INVULNERABLE`, 1.5 s) and `GymPowerUpsCombat`
  (`COMBAT_HIT_INVULNERABLE_DURATION`, 0.8 s) must be preserved; shield-absorb
  must still pop the shield and start invulnerability.
- Preserve the existing shield/lives flow in `PlayScene` (shield absorb must not
  cost a life; an unabsorbed hit still runs the normal lose-life flow).
- No unrelated refactors; keep changes surgical and match existing style.
- CHANGELOG.md is excluded (release pipeline owns it); do not touch CI/CD.
- Written output in UK English.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — default `isPlayerPhased()` returns
  `false`; default `tryAbsorbPlayerHit()` returns `false`; `getEffectsRegistry()`
  returns a private `defaultEffectsRegistry`; `_collectDrop()` applies
  P3/P6 via `registry.applyCollect(drop.dropId)` and clears bullets for P4.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — `_hitPlayer()` calls
  `tryAbsorbPlayerHit()` then `onPlayerHit()`; `_handleCollisions()` skips
  bullet/body hits when `isPlayerPhased()`.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — overrides `isPlayerPhased()` (line ~1083) and
  `tryAbsorbPlayerHit()` (line ~1245, shield pop + `_startInvulnerability`).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` — overrides `isPlayerPhased()` (~504)
  and `tryAbsorbPlayerHit()` (~514).
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — owns its `effectsRegistry` and
  HUD; overrides `getEffectsRegistry()` only; **no** phase/shield overrides and
  **no** shield-bubble/phase-ghost visuals.
- `GymEnemies`, `GymBoss`, `GymMinerals` extend `GymFormationScene`; `GymIndex`
  routes every non-boss enemy config (including `diver`) to `GymEnemies`.

## Desired change

- Add registry-backed default `isPlayerPhased()` and `tryAbsorbPlayerHit()`
  (shield absorb → consume shield → start invulnerability → return `true`) to
  the shared combat base, so every `CombatScene` subclass inherits correct
  gating exactly once.
- Reduce `PlayScene` and `GymPowerUpsCombat` overrides to any genuinely
  scene-specific extras; otherwise delete them.
- Add the shared shield-bubble/phase-ghost rendering to `GymFormationScene`
  (or a shared combat visual) for feedback parity.
- Add regression tests proving AC1–AC3 and an equivalence test for the shared
  hook routing.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — registry-backed default
  `isPlayerPhased()` / `tryAbsorbPlayerHit()` (or move to `CombatScene` if a
  `Player` param is needed for the absorb VFX); document the shared gating.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — keep `_hitPlayer()`/`_handleCollisions()`
  unchanged; host any shared shield-pop cue/visual seam.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — inherit gating; add shield
  bubble + phase ghost visuals for parity.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — remove/trim now-redundant overrides.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` — remove/trim now-redundant overrides.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.test.ts` / `CombatScene.test.ts` — shared
  gating unit tests.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts` / `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.test.ts`
  — enemy-gym regression tests (phase immunity, shield absorb).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — assert shared hook routing.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — document shared shield/phase gating.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the operator's "continue" authorises the recommended shared-base

  de-duplication extent and the visual work change, not AC1–AC3.
- **Risk — shipped-game regression:** moving shield/phase gating into the base
  touches `PlayScene`; mitigated by preserving invulnerability durations and the
  shield/lives flow and by equivalence tests (AC3, AC7).
- **Risk — multi-hit semantics:** shield must absorb exactly one hit; an
  over-eager base default could absorb repeatedly. Mitigated by AC2 (second hit
  must land).
- **Risk — phase vs invulnerability interaction:** phase immunity and the
  post-hit blink must not mask each other; covered by AC1/AC4 and existing
  PlayScene tests.
- **Risk — scope creep:** other effect/visual divergences may be discovered;
  record these as linked work items rather than expanding this fix.
- **Non-goal:** reworking the power-up spawn/placement layer or the P4/P5/P7/P9
  effects (already working).

## Related work

- AH-0MUD8E015004C4JO — Unify PlayScene/GymFormationScene combat logic into a
  shared core scene base class (parent; completed). This bug is a gap in that
  consolidation: the hit-gating hooks were left as per-scene overrides.
- AH-0MUD9R3NB0093CBV — Extract player-hit lifecycle into CombatScene
  (completed) — the extraction that left `isPlayerPhased`/`tryAbsorbPlayerHit`
  abstract-per-scene.
- AH-0MUD9R3ZC0006M4I — Extract collision core and host bullet-vs-bullet impact
  feedback (completed).
- AH-0MTE8EBAH007GUO0 — Effects module: shield absorb, bomb clear, phase shift,
  teleport (completed).
- AH-0MTE8EBG3004QC66 — Combat gym scene: GymPowerUpsCombat with ship, scouts,
  spawner, effects (completed).
- AH-0MTE8EC2W004MPUW — Unit tests: hit response, collection gate, round-robin
  spawner (completed).

- AH-0MU8QV3O9008JVNQ — PlayScene: add P3 shield bubble visual + post-absorb

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (approach):** Should the fix centralise phase/shield hit-gating in the
  shared combat base (and de-duplicate `PlayScene`/`GymPowerUpsCombat`), or add
  local overrides only to `GymFormationScene`?
  — **Recommended:** centralise in the shared base — matches the operator's
