# Gym asteroids do not drop minerals — share the mineral kill-drop code with the game

## Headline

Gym asteroids do not drop minerals because the kill-drop rule lives only in the
game (`PlayScene`) while the gyms run a divergent copy. Extract the rule into one
shared helper used by both, and wire it into the gyms so they drop minerals
(small-asteroid single drop; non-asteroid 25–50 % re-drop) exactly as the game
does.

## Problem statement

Asteroids in the gym scenes do not drop minerals when destroyed, even though the
shipped game does and the gyms' own documentation says they should. The cause is
code divergence: the mineral **kill-drop** logic lives privately in `PlayScene`
and was never shared, while the gyms re-implemented the collection half of the
mineral layer and omitted the drop half. The fix is to make gym asteroids drop
minerals (per GDD §4.4.1) and to move the kill-drop logic into a single shared
helper used by both the game and the gyms, so the two can no longer drift.

## Users

- **As a player using the minerals gym**, when I destroy a small asteroid I want
  it to leave a mineral, so the gym demonstrates the real mechanic I see in the
  game.
- **As a player using the asteroid enemy gym**, when I destroy a small asteroid
  I want it to drop a mineral, so the gym matches the game's asteroid behaviour.
- **As a developer**, I want the mineral kill-drop logic to exist in exactly one
  shared place, so a gym and the game can never again disagree about whether an
  asteroid drops a mineral.
- **As a player**, when a non-asteroid enemy that has absorbed minerals is
  destroyed, I want it to re-drop a fraction of them, in the gym as in the game.

## Root cause (RCA summary)

- The shared base `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` provides the generic
  destruction seam (`onPlayerBulletHitsEnemy` → `onEnemyDestroyed`) but has no
  mineral concept.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` overrides `onEnemyDestroyed` and, in the private
  `_onEnemyKilled()`, implements the drops: small asteroid → `spawnMineralAt()`;
  large/medium asteroid → none (split children drop); non-asteroid enemy →
  `entity.spawnMineralDrops()` (25–50 % re-drop).
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` re-implements the mineral layer
  (`seedMinerals`, `_initMineralLayer`, `_updateMinerals`) but its
  `onEntityDestroyed` path only splits asteroids — it never spawns a mineral and
  never calls `spawnMineralDrops()` on death.
- `GymMinerals.ts` (asteroids-only) and `GymEnemies.ts` (generic enemy gym, used
  for the "Asteroid" config row) both extend `GymFormationScene`, so both are
  affected.
- Prior unification work (AH-0MUD8E015004C4JO) shared the combat core but left
  the mineral logic duplicated — exactly the divergence the operator suspected.
- The gym docstrings and GDD §6.4 already claim "small-asteroid mineral drops …
  enemy absorption/re-drop"; the earlier gym item (AH-0MUCST5HA0079APB) had this
  in its acceptance criteria but it was closed without the drop behaviour.

## Existing state

- `BaseEnemy.mineralRedropCount()` / `spawnMineralDrops()` already implement the
  25–50 % re-drop and are unit-tested (AH-0MUCST3QD002O9TA / AH-0MUCST1P10004EXM).
- `PlayScene.spawnMineralAt()` is public and used by the game and, in principle,
  by gyms.
- `Asteroid.collectMineral()` is a no-op (asteroids are inert to minerals) and
  `Asteroid.getSizeTier()` / `getSplitChildren()` exist.
- `GymFormationScene` already owns a mineral field, a hold, a HUD counter and the
  hold-full choice overlay, and seeds 100 minerals on create.
- The rules config exposes `mineralCollectAmount`, `mineralHoldCapacity`,
  `mineralRedropFractionMin`/`Max`.

## Desired change

- Extract the mineral kill-drop rule into one shared helper used by **both**
  `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene` (and therefore every formation gym).
  The helper decides, for a destroyed enemy, how many minerals to spawn and
  where: small asteroid → exactly one at the death site; large/medium asteroid →
  none; non-asteroid enemy → the configured fraction of minerals absorbed,
  scattered at the death site.
- Wire the helper into the gym destruction path so gym asteroids (and other
  gyms' enemies) drop minerals exactly as the game does.
- Leave gameplay values and balance unchanged; reuse the existing rules tunables.
- Keep the game's observable behaviour identical (pure refactor there), and keep
  the existing mineral tests green.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Gyms drop on small-asteroid destruction.** Destroying a small asteroid
  in `GymMinerals` and in the `GymEnemies` asteroid-config row spawns exactly one
  mineral at the asteroid's position (matching `PlayScene`). Large/medium
  asteroids do not drop directly; their small split children do. Verified by a
  scene test that destroys a small asteroid and asserts the live mineral count
  increases by one at that position, and by a test that a large/medium asteroid
  splits without a direct drop.
- **AC2 — Gyms re-drop for non-asteroid enemies.** In a gym, a non-asteroid
  enemy that has absorbed minerals re-drops between the configured
  `mineralRedropFractionMin`/`Max` fraction of them (never more than collected)
  at its death site. Verified by a deterministic test injecting a seeded RNG.
- **AC3 — Single shared code path.** The mineral kill-drop rule (small-asteroid
  drop + non-asteroid re-drop) is implemented once in a shared helper/module and
  consumed by both `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene`; `PlayScene`'s private
  kill-drop block delegates to it. Verified by a parity/equivalence test and by
  the repo-wide duplicate-body guard passing.
- **AC4 — No game behaviour regression.** `PlayScene` mineral behaviour
  (small-asteroid drop, non-asteroid re-drop, collection, absorption, hold-fill
  choice) is unchanged; the existing `PlayScene` mineral tests stay green.
- **AC5 — Tests are added and green.** New/extended tests cover AC1–AC3 in the
  gym suites (`GymMinerals.test.ts`, `GymEnemies.test.ts`,
  `GymFormationScene.test.ts`) and all pass.
- **AC6 — Documentation updated.** The GDD (§4.4.1 and §6.4), the
  `GymMinerals`/`GymFormationScene` docstrings and any relevant README/docs
  entries describe the shared mineral kill-drop code and the gym behaviour.
- **AC7 — Full project test suite passes.** `npm test` (the full suite) passes
  with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Do not change balance/tuning values; use the existing rules config.
- Prefer a genuinely shared helper over per-scene copies (the operator selected
  the shared-helper approach); avoid introducing a second divergence.
- The extracted helper must not force gym-specific concerns (hold, HUD, choice)
  into the game, nor game-specific concerns (score, waves) into the gym.
- Tests must be meaningful and deterministic (TDD preferred); no snapshot-only
  or trivially-true assertions.
- Written output and docs in UK English.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — likely host for, or hook to, the shared
  mineral kill-drop helper (shared base of game and gyms).
- `src/scenes/core/<new mineral helper>.ts` (or `src/core/minerals.ts`) — the
  single shared implementation of the kill-drop rule.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — refactor `_onEnemyKilled()` mineral block to
  delegate to the shared helper (no behaviour change).
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — call the shared helper from the
  destruction path; add dropped minerals to the gym's mineral field.
- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts` — reuse `spawnMineralDrops()` / `mineralRedropCount()`.
- `src/entities/Asteroid.ts` — reuse `getSizeTier()` / `getSplitChildren()`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymMinerals.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/__tests__/PlayScene.minerals.test.ts` — tests.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §4.4.1 / §6.4 wording and gym docstrings.

## Related work

- `AH-0MUBVGI62004ED9Q` — parent mechanic (asteroids drop minerals; hold; choice).
- `AH-0MUCST5HA0079APB` — asteroids-only mineral gym; its AC claimed small-asteroid
  drops and enemy re-drop, but the drop half was not implemented (this item closes
  that gap).
- `AH-0MUD8E015004C4JO` — prior unification of PlayScene/GymFormationScene combat
  logic into a shared core; this item extends the same principle to minerals.
- `AH-0MUCST3QD002O9TA` — mineral rules tunables and per-enemy mineral count.
- `AH-0MUCST1P10004EXM` — tests for enemy mineral count and re-drop distribution.
- `AH-0MUCST3BS0007CPT` — Mineral collectable entity and constants.
- `AH-0MUHMXWGC0058BO4` — ability items (Dual Shot/Teleport/Phase Shift) not
  functioning; a distinct gym-sharing defect, not a mineral drop issue.
- `AH-0MUHM66ES0027QQV` — enemy gym P3/P6 hit-gating not shared; a distinct
  gym-sharing defect, not a mineral drop issue.

## Out of scope

- Fixing the distinct gym-sharing defects `AH-0MUHMXWGC0058BO4` (ability items)
  and `AH-0MUHM66ES0027QQV` (enemy gym P3/P6 hit-gating).
- Any change to mineral balance/tuning values or the hold/choice reward pool.
- Reworking the reward/choice flow itself; only the drop-on-kill wiring changes.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk:** the clean shared boundary is unclear because the game and gyms differ
  in hold/HUD/choice/score concerns. **Mitigation:** share only the field +
  collection/absorption + kill-drop mechanics, keep hold/score/choice in the
  scenes, and cover the seam with parity tests.
- **Risk:** scope creep into the two related gym-sharing defects
  (`AH-0MUHMXWGC0058BO4`, `AH-0MUHM66ES0027QQV`). **Mitigation:** keep those out
  of scope; they are separate work items.
- **Risk:** the refactor could change `PlayScene` behaviour subtly.
  **Mitigation:** AC4 requires the existing mineral tests to remain green and a
  parity test to pin the shared rule.
- **Assumption:** gyms should behave exactly like the game for mineral drops
  (operator confirmed the non-asteroid re-drop should be included).
- **Assumption:** the shared helper is the preferred approach over a local gym
  patch (operator selected the shared helper).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Non-asteroid enemy re-drop in gyms — include it, or asteroids only?" —
  **Answer (operator):** "Yes, include it." Source: interactive reply. Context:
  the re-drop mechanism already exists (`BaseEnemy.spawnMineralDrops`) but is not
  wired into gyms; including it keeps the shared path complete.
- Q: "Refactor boundary — shared helper used by both PlayScene and
  GymFormationScene, or a local gym patch?" — **Answer (operator):** "Shared
  helper." Source: interactive reply. Context: RCA confirms the divergence, so a
  shared helper prevents recurrence.
- Q (operator-initiated): "Check whether a work item exists for the previously
  raised issue about enemy drops; if so, close it." — **Answer/Research:** no
  open work item matching "enemy drops" exists in the worklog. All drop/mineral
  items are already `completed` (`AH-0MUBVGI62004ED9Q`, `AH-0MUCST5HA0079APB`,
  `AH-0MUCST1P10004EXM`, `AH-0MUCST3QD002O9TA`, etc.). The only related *open*
  items are `AH-0MUHMXWGC0058BO4` (ability items) and `AH-0MUHM66ES0027QQV`
  (enemy gym hit-gating), both distinct defects and left open. No item closed.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUA8BK1E001UZUC** – Apply rebindable keys to gameplay and menus (completed)
- **AH-0MUGCSQKU003R4WW** – Update documentation — asteroid spawn mechanic (completed)
- **AH-0MT7QQGBU008V4R0** – Write the Game Design Document (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: asteroid, asteroids, code, destruction, diverge (+31 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: asteroid, asteroids, code, destruction, diverge (+27 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: asteroid, asteroids, code, destruction, diverge (+25 more)

## Plan: decomposition (2026-09-26)

**Pre-check:** effort Small / risk Medium → planning required (`plan_helpers.py plan-if-needed` → `decision: plan`). Plan-approval gate → `request_approval: false` (risk Medium is below the gate's High threshold), so no approval pause was required; the plan proceeded straight to the automated review stages.

### Child work items (dependency-ordered, test-first)

| # | Work item | Type | Depends on |
|---|-----------|------|------------|
| 1 | Test: shared mineral kill-drop rule — `AH-0MUIG1AFG00938TV` | task | — |
| 2 | Shared mineral kill-drop helper + PlayScene/BaseEnemy refactor — `AH-0MUIGTRFY002JDDS` | task | 1 |
| 3 | Test: gyms drop minerals on kill — `AH-0MUIGTRVA0072TWW` | task | 2 |
| 4 | Wire gyms to the shared mineral kill-drop helper — `AH-0MUIGTSAX00096Y4` | task | 3 |
| 5 | Documentation update + full-suite verification — `AH-0MUIG16QK003MSNO` | docs | 4 |

The dependency graph is a verified DAG (test → impl → test → impl → docs/verify). Test/verification items precede their implementation items.

### AC traceability (parent AC → child items)

- **AC1 (gyms drop on small-asteroid destruction):** 3, 4
- **AC2 (gyms re-drop for non-asteroid enemies):** 3, 4
- **AC3 (single shared code path):** 1, 2, 4
- **AC4 (no game behaviour regression):** 2
- **AC5 (tests added and green):** 1, 3
- **AC6 (documentation updated):** 4, 5
- **AC7 (full project test suite passes):** 5

Coverage review (`tree_coverage.py run-coverage-review`): `recommendation: proceed`, 100 % of parent ACs covered.

### Design decisions & assumptions (documented, not open questions)

- **Shared helper location:** `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.ts` exporting `resolveMineralKillDrops(scene, entity, rng): Mineral[]`, consumed by `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene`. Rationale: it needs scene/`Mineral`/`Asteroid` types and sits with the shared combat core (`CombatScene`), matching the item's predicted Key Files.
- **Scatter reuse:** `BaseEnemy.spawnMineralDrops()` delegates to the shared scatter maths, keeping its public API and RNG draw order so `PlayScene` behaviour is byte-for-byte identical for non-asteroid re-drops.
- **Gym RNG seam:** `GymFormationScene` gains an injectable scene RNG (default `Math.random`) so gym drop tests are deterministic; configuration already accepts an `rng` for the power-up layer, but a scene-level seam is required for mineral drops.
- **All destruction paths drop once:** the gym drop is invoked from both `onEnemyDestroyed` and `explodeRandom`, so EXPLODE (which bypasses `onEnemyDestroyed`) matches the game's bullet/ram paths without double-dropping.
- Balance/tuning values are unchanged; only the wiring and the shared helper are added.

The remaining unknowns are implementation-level design choices, resolved above as documented assumptions rather than requirements questions. # Ability items not functioning: Dual Shot, Teleport, Phase Shift

## Problem statement

Three collectable effects granted through the mineral hold-full reward flow do
not behave as the Game Design Document (GDD §2.3/§4.4/§4.5) describes:
**Dual Shot** (weapon drop) does not take effect in the main game, and
**P7 Teleport** and **P6 Phase Shift** are inert when collected in the
minerals gym. Repo investigation shows these are three distinct defects with
two shared root causes (choice display/apply divergence; mineral-gym combat
effects not wired), not cosmetic/reskin issues.

## Users

- **As a player in the main game**, when my mineral hold fills I want the
  power-up/weapon I pick in the "HOLD FULL — CHOOSE A POWER-UP" overlay to be
  the exact one applied, so my choice is honoured.
- **As a player in the minerals gym**, when a mineral reward grants me
  P7 Teleport I want S/↓ to consume a stored use and warp me to safety, so the
  reward is usable.
- **As a player in the minerals gym**, when a mineral reward grants me
  P6 Phase Shift (or P3 Shield) I want the intangibility/absorption to
  actually protect me, so the reward is usable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Displayed choice equals applied choice (main game + gyms).**
  When the hold-full choice overlay is shown, the option label the player
  selects is the exact option applied. Verified by a deterministic test
  (injected strategy + seeded RNG) that stubs `MineralChoiceScene` display
  options and asserts the option returned by `selectMineralChoice` equals the
  option shown/selected at the same index.
- **AC2 — P7 Teleport works in the minerals gym.** After a P7 Teleport is
  granted via the hold-full choice in `GymMinerals`, pressing S (or ↓)
  consumes one stored use, moves the player to the resolved safe spot, and
  grants P6 Phase Shift. Verified by a `GymMinerals` test that applies P7 via
  the choice path, invokes the teleport key/`triggerTeleport`, and asserts:
  stack decremented, player position changed, `registry.isPhased === true`.
- **AC3 — P6 Phase Shift protects in the minerals gym.** While P6 is active,
  enemy bullets and enemy bodies do not register a hit. Verified by a
  `GymMinerals` test that activates P6, places a bullet/body on the player, and
  asserts `playerHitCount` is unchanged.
- **AC4 — P3 Shield absorbs in the minerals gym (scope assumption, see
  below).** While P3 is active, the first hit is absorbed, the shield pops,
  and `playerHitCount` is unchanged; the next hit registers. Verified by test.
- **AC5 — No regression in existing power-up flows.** The full power-up gym
  (`GymPowerUpsCombat`), utility gym, and main-game teleport/phase/shield paths
  continue to pass their existing suites.
- **AC6 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the
  changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site
  entries (in particular the GDD §4.5 hold-full choice and §6.4 gym behaviour
  notes if wording drifts).
- **AC7 — Validation.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Teleport activation keys are fixed by the GDD: **S / ↓**.
- Must not regress `GymPowerUpsCombat`, `GymPowerUpsUtility`, `PlayScene`, or
  `PauseScene` pause/resume semantics.
- The choice overlay must remain pointer- and keyboard-operable (numbered keys
  and click), and must keep its opaque backdrop / z-order behaviour.
- All implementation must occur in the worktree created by
  `implement.py start AH-0MUHMXWGC0058BO4` (implement skill), with
  build → test → commit ordering.

## Existing state (root-cause analysis from repo investigation)

1. **Main-game choice display/apply divergence (Dual Shot symptom).**
   `PlayScene.openMineralChoice()` stores
   `this.mineralChoiceOptions = this.mineralChoiceStrategy.choose(3, this.rng)`
   and then launches the overlay with only `{ origin: 'PlayScene' }`
   (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`). `MineralChoiceScene.init()` therefore draws its
   **own, independent** options via `randomChoiceStrategy.choose(3)`
   (`src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts`). `MineralChoiceScene.select(index)`
   forwards only the **index** to `play.selectMineralChoice(index)`, which
   applies `play.mineralChoiceOptions[index]` — a different draw from the label
   shown. The player can therefore pick the displayed "Dual Shot" and have a
   different (often invisible/inert) option applied. The gym path does not have
   this bug because `GymFormationScene.openMineralChoice()` passes `options`
   and an `onSelect` callback.

2. **P7 Teleport inert in the minerals gym.**
   `GymMinerals`'s `asteroidFormationConfig()` omits the `powerUps` config key,
   so `GymFormationScene.powerUpsEnabled` stays `false`. Consequently:
   `_initPowerUpLayer()` returns early and **never binds** the S/↓ keys;
   `_updatePowerUpLayer()` returns early and **never calls** `_handleTeleport()`;
   and `canTeleport()` returns `powerUpsEnabled` (`false`). P7 stacks granted
   via the hold-full choice can never be consumed. (`GymPowerUpsCombat` binds
   the keys and overrides the hooks, which is why it works there.)

3. **P6 Phase Shift / P3 Shield inert in the minerals gym.**
   `GymFormationScene` does **not** override `isPlayerPhased()` or
   `tryAbsorbPlayerHit()`, so `CombatCoreScene`'s defaults (`false`) are used
   even though `EffectsRegistry.isPhased` / `isShielded` are `true`. The
   mineral reward can grant these effects, but `_handleCollisions()` never
   honours them. (`GymPowerUpsCombat` and `PlayScene` override both hooks.)

4. Working reference implementations already exist for all three fixes:
   `GymPowerUpsCombat` (key binding, `isPlayerPhased`, `tryAbsorbPlayerHit`),
   `PlayScene` (phase/shield/teleport), and the gym choice path
   (`options` + `onSelect`).

## Desired change

- Make the hold-full choice a single source of truth so the option displayed is
  the option applied in `PlayScene` (and keep the gym's `options`/`onSelect`
  path working).
- Make P7 Teleport operational in `GymMinerals`: bind S/↓ and run
  `_handleTeleport()` whenever a player exists and a teleport stack is stored,
  independent of the opt-in power-up **drop** layer; allow
  `canTeleport()` when `hasTeleport()` is true.
- Wire the shared `EffectsRegistry` into `GymFormationScene`'s combat hooks so
  P6 (and P3) granted via the mineral reward choice are honoured
  (`isPlayerPhased()` → `registry.isPhased`; `tryAbsorbPlayerHit()` → shield pop).
- Add the regression tests in the ACs above.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `openMineralChoice()` must pass the stored
  `mineralChoiceOptions` (and the active strategy) to the overlay so display and
  apply agree.
- `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` — accept the caller-supplied options
  consistently; optionally forward the selected `ChoiceOption` alongside the
  index.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — bind teleport keys whenever a
  player is present; call `_handleTeleport()` each tick independent of the
  power-up drop layer; permit `canTeleport()` when a stack is stored; override
  `isPlayerPhased()` and `tryAbsorbPlayerHit()` to read the registry.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymMinerals.ts` — config check; no change expected if the base
  scene is fixed, but confirm the mineral gym opts in to the teleport/hook
  behaviour.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` / `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` —
  review hook defaults only if a base-level (non-gym) fix is cleaner.
- Tests: `src/scenes/__tests__/MineralChoiceScene.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/__tests__/PlayScene.minerals.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/gym/GymMinerals.test.ts` (new cases), plus any shared-hook tests.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUBVGI62004ED9Q** — *Asteroids drop collectable minerals that fill the
  ship's hold and grant a power-up choice* (parent feature; defines the
  hold-full choice contract this work fixes).
- **AH-0MUCST2VY004T6QQ** — *Test: Hold-full choice scene and PlayScene wiring*
  (test contract for the choice overlay; does not cover the display/apply index
  divergence).
- **AH-0MT7UY5UR002LD5U** — *Redesign P7 Dash: make collectable teleport
  power-up* (P7 semantics: stored FIFO, S/↓, P6 on arrival).
- **AH-0MTC2P6G3007PJ40** — *Create combat gym scene for combat-coupled
  power-ups (P3/P4/P6/P7)* (reference implementation in `GymPowerUpsCombat`).
- **AH-0MU8QVC9Y008R8I5** — *PlayScene: add P6 phase-shift ghost visual*
  (PlayScene phase visual; confirms phase is functional there).
- Automated related-work report: `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-AH-0MUHMXWGC0058BO4.md`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (scope):** "minerals gym" means `GymMinerals` (asteroids +
  mineral hold), not `GymPowerUpsCombat`. Evidence: the user distinguished
  "the main game" from "the minerals gym", and `GymMinerals` is the gym that
  offers the hold-full mineral reward choice without field power-up drops.
- **Assumption (scope):** P3 Shield and any other combat power-up granted via
  the mineral reward choice in `GymMinerals` are in scope because they share
  the `isPlayerPhased`/`tryAbsorbPlayerHit` root cause. If the producer wants
  the narrower fix only, drop AC4. **OPEN QUESTION** (see Appendix).
- **Risk:** S is also the "down" movement key in the 4-directional scheme;
  adding teleport binding to `GymMinerals` must use `JustDown` semantics so it
  never fires continuously while moving down, and must not double-consume
  stacks.
- **Risk:** fixing the main-game choice changes the effective option pool
  semantics (the drawn options become authoritative); tests must inject a
  deterministic strategy/RNG to avoid flakiness.
- **Risk:** a base-level change to `GymFormationScene` could regress gyms that
  rely on `powerUpsEnabled` gating (e.g. `GymEnemies`, `GymBoss`). Mitigation:
  gate teleport on `hasTeleport()` rather than on the drop layer, and run the
  full gym suites.
- **Scope-creep risk:** any other defects found while fixing (e.g. HUD display
  of permanent weapons, shield bubble in `GymMinerals`) should be recorded as
  separate linked work items (`discovered-from:AH-0MUHMXWGC0058BO4`), not
  expanded into this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q: Which gym is the "minerals gym"?** — Answer (agent research, from repo):
  `GymMinerals`, key `GymMinerals` (asteroids-only + 100 seeded minerals + the
  hold-full choice). Evidence: `src/scenes/gym/GymMinerals.ts`,
  `GymFormationScene._initMineralLayer`, and the distinct
  `GymPowerUpsCombat`/`GymPowerUpsUtility` scenes.
- **Q: Is the "Dual Shot" symptom caused by the displayed-vs-applied option
  divergence?** — Answer (agent research, from repo): yes, the main-game path
  draws options twice (`PlayScene.openMineralChoice` and
  `MineralChoiceScene.init`) and applies by index only. Evidence:
  `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:1902`, `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts:38,104`.
- **Q: Should P3 Shield (and other combat effects) granted via the mineral
  choice in `GymMinerals` also be fixed?** — Answer (assumed): yes, same root
  cause; documented in AC4. **OPEN QUESTION** for producer confirmation — the
  operator report named only Teleport and Phase Shift.
- **Q: Are field power-up drops expected in `GymMinerals`?** — Answer (agent
  research, from repo): no; the gym omits the `powerUps` config and relies on
  the mineral hold-full choice to grant effects. The fix must therefore not
  require enabling the full drop layer.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-09-26 — Planned `AH-0MUHMXWGC0058BO4`: created 8 child work items
  (3 test, 3 fix, 1 regression-validation, 1 docs), wired test-first
  dependency edges (`Fix*` depends on `TC*`; regression and docs depend on all
  three fixes), and ran the six automated review stages. AC coverage review
  returned `proceed` at 100% (all 7 parent ACs mapped to child ACs). Planning
  paused at the plan-approval gate (risk = High) with one open scope question
  (P3 Shield inclusion) — see Appendix below.

## Appendix: Planning session (2026-09-26) — OPEN QUESTIONS

The parent already records earlier clarifying questions above. This planning
run added the following, which remain **unanswered** pending producer input:

- **OPEN QUESTION — Plan approval.** Effort = Small, Risk = High, so the
  plan-approval gate requires producer confirmation of the 8-child plan below
  before implementation proceeds. Directed to: producer. Why it matters:
  the plan has not been accepted/edited; implementation must not start until
  the gate is passed.
- **OPEN QUESTION — P3 Shield scope.** Should P3 Shield (and other combat
  effects) granted via the mineral reward choice in `GymMinerals` be fixed
  alongside P7 Teleport and P6 Phase Shift? The operator report named only
  Teleport and Phase Shift; the plan currently includes P3 via AC4 and child
  fix `Fix: Wire P6 Phase Shift / P3 Shield hooks in GymFormationScene`.
  If narrower scope is preferred, drop AC4 and the P3 acceptance criteria from
  that child. Directed to: producer. Why it matters: it determines whether the
  shield-absorption test and hook wiring are in scope.

### Proposed child plan (8 children)

1. TC: Test — MineralChoiceScene display/apply alignment (`AH-0MUIB8JAU0091RTN`)
2. Fix: Wire mineral choice options from PlayScene to MineralChoiceScene (`AH-0MUIBAKHJ007KTVT`)
3. TC: Test — P7 Teleport in GymMinerals (`AH-0MUIBBLO8001U1O4`)
4. Fix: Wire P7 Teleport key binding and handler in GymFormationScene (`AH-0MUIBCS240050MDH`)
5. TC: Test — P6 Phase Shift / P3 Shield in GymMinerals (`AH-0MUIBEU5X002BHBK`)
6. Fix: Wire P6 Phase Shift / P3 Shield hooks in GymFormationScene (`AH-0MUIBGV41002YTQA`)
7. Regression: Full project test suite passes (`AH-0MUIBI6FH005A92G`)
8. Docs: Update documentation for mineral choice and gym effect fixes (`AH-0MUIBNN07007S7LD`)

## Appendix: Planning session (2026-09-26) — RESOLVED

Producer approved the plan and confirmed scope in-session.

- **Q: Do you approve the proposed 8-child plan?** — Answer (producer):
  "LGTM (in scope)". Final: **APPROVED**; the 8-child plan stands as proposed.
- **Q: Should P3 Shield be in scope?** — Answer (producer): "in scope".
  Final: **P3 Shield IS in scope**; AC4 and the P3 acceptance criteria on
  `AH-0MUIBGV41002YTQA` remain (supersedes the earlier "assumed / OPEN
  QUESTION" note above).

**Plan: changelog (update)** — 2026-09-26: plan approved by producer; P3
Shield confirmed in scope; stage advanced to `plan_complete`; needs-producer-
review cleared. No new children added (plan unchanged).

data.description:
# Intake brief — Harvester enemy

**Headline:** Add a Harvester enemy archetype — a large, slow, roaming enemy
that actively seeks and absorbs the nearest mineral and survives five player
bullets — backed by data-driven regular-enemy health, wired into both the
shipped game and the enemy gym, and integrated into the campaign as a rare
roaming spawn.

## Problem statement

The bestiary currently has no enemy that competes with the player for
minerals. Non-asteroid enemies already absorb any mineral they happen to
overlap (GDD §4.4.1), but none deliberately hunts the field. The Harvester
introduces a mineral-denial threat: it actively drives to the nearest mineral,
is large (easy to hit and quick to absorb), slow to cross the screen, and
durable (five hits), forcing the player to spend ammunition and attention on it
before it strips the field.

## Users

- **As a player**, I want a durable enemy that actively steals minerals, so
  that collecting minerals becomes a contest rather than a free pickup.
- **As a player**, I want the Harvester to be large and slow, so that the
  five-hit cost is fair and readable rather than punishing.
- **As a designer**, I want to tune the Harvester (size, colour, speed,
  health, score) through the existing CSV/enemy-config pipeline without
  touching scene code.
- **As a developer**, I want multi-hit health and mineral seeking to be shared,
  data-driven capabilities, so future multi-hit or seeking enemies are cheap
  and the game and gyms cannot diverge.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — New `harvester` archetype is registered and discoverable.** A
  `harvester` row exists in `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` with a matching seed
  fallback in `src/core/configDefaults.ts`, is mapped in
  `src/entities/enemyFactory.ts`, appears in the gym index, and spawns/renders
  in `GymEnemies`. Regular-enemy health is data-driven: a `health` column is
  added to the CSV schema/codec (`src/core/csv.ts`) and `EnemyConfig`
  (`src/core/configTypes.ts`), defaulting to 1 so existing enemies are
  unchanged. Verified by config/CSV tests and a gym spawn test.
- [ ] **AC2 — Mineral-seeking behaviour.** The Harvester always steers toward
  the **nearest live mineral anywhere on the field** at its configured (slow)
  speed and absorbs it on overlap using the existing enemy-absorption rule
  (`collectMinerals`), incrementing its tracked mineral count. It does **not
  fire**, and it cannot take minerals from the player's hold. When no mineral
  exists it holds station / continues its idle drift. Verified by deterministic
  entity + scene tests that place minerals and assert the Harvester closes
  distance and consumes them, and that it fires no bullets.
- [ ] **AC3 — Five-hit destruction with readable feedback.** The Harvester has
  `health = 5` and survives exactly five player-bullet hits. Each non-lethal hit
  consumes the bullet and triggers the existing bullet-impact feedback; the
  fifth hit destroys it, plays destruction audio/VFX exactly once, awards
  **≈ 400** score, advances wave accounting, and re-drops 25–50 % of absorbed
  minerals per the existing rule. The shared multi-hit path must correctly
  finalise the kill (`onEnemyDestroyed`, destruction audio) — a gap that exists
  today. Verified by a five-hit test and a single-destruction/single-audio
  regression test.
- [ ] **AC4 — Existing enemies are unchanged.** All current 1-HP enemies
  (Scout, Diver, Tank, Phaser, Swarm, Asteroid) remain destroyed by one hit and
  their tests stay green.
- [ ] **AC5 — Game ↔ gym parity.** The Harvester's seek, absorption and
  five-hit destruction run through the same shared code path in `PlayScene` and
  in `GymEnemies` (per the gym-parity principle); no scene re-implements the
  behaviour.
- [ ] **AC6 — Campaign integration.** The Harvester is available in the gym
  **and** appears in the campaign as a rare roaming spawn in later levels
  (Levels 4–5), registered with the `WaveManager` so wave-clear accounting is
  correct. Verified by a wave/level test.
- [ ] **AC7 — Testing/validation.** New unit/integration tests cover: config
  codec round-trip (including the new `health` column), factory mapping, seek
  target selection (nearest mineral; none present), absorption counting,
  five-hit destruction, and a `PlayScene` + `GymEnemies` parity check. Full
  project test suite must pass with the new changes.
- [ ] **AC8 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect
  the changes, including the Game Design Document health model and enemy
  catalog (§2.3, §4.1, §4.4.1, §4.5, §6.5), the
  `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` catalog and add-an-enemy checklist
  (§1/§8), the README enemy list, and code comments.

## Constraints

- **Data-driven:** tuning lives in the CSV/enemy-config pipeline; no new
  per-enemy scene or hard-coded archetype branch.
- **Single source of truth:** no duplication of collision, mineral-collection,
  or health logic — this is a hard requirement of the gym-parity epic
  (`AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA`).
- **No regression:** existing 1-HP enemies and their tests must be untouched
  semantically; `health` defaults to 1.
- **GDD consistency:** the health-model change must be documented explicitly so
  the GDD no longer claims "all regular enemies are 1 HP"; P4 Bomb still deals
  **no** damage to enemies.
- **Surgical:** match existing entity/config/scene style; do not delete
  unrelated dead code (report it instead).
- **UK English** in all written output and documentation.
- **Gating:** implementation proceeds only through `/skill:implement`; this
  intake does not authorise code changes.

## Existing state (verified 2026-09-27 against HEAD)

- Enemy archetypes are **data, not code**: `EnemyConfig` (`src/core/configTypes.ts`),
  one CSV row per archetype (`src/data/enemy-configs.csv`), seed fallbacks in
  `src/core/configDefaults.ts`, factory mapping in `src/entities/enemyFactory.ts`.
- All regular enemies are **1 HP** (destroyed by a single bullet) and the GDD
  states this explicitly (`docs/Game Design Document.md` §2.3, §4.1, §6.5).
  Only the Boss is multi-hit (4-phase). There is an optional `takeDamage?()`
  seam on entities (`CombatCoreScene`, `CombatScene`, `GymFormationScene`), but
  the shared generic path currently calls it **without** running
  `onEnemyDestroyed()`/destruction audio when the entity finally dies — that
  is a gap this work must close for a multi-hit regular enemy to score, drop
  minerals and advance waves correctly.
- The Asteroid is the precedent for a **non-formation roamer**: it has
  `formationKind: single`, overrides `updatePosition(dt)` (called by the gym
  and game before `applyFormationPosition`) and `applyFormationPosition` is a
  no-op. Asteroids use the same random offscreen spawner
  (`src/waves/AsteroidSpawner.ts`) registered with the `WaveManager`.
- Minerals already exist: `Mineral` (`src/entities/Mineral.ts`), collection and
  non-asteroid absorption in `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts`
  (`collectMinerals`), kill re-drop in `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.ts`,
  and the 25–50 % re-drop fraction in `src/core/rules.ts`. `BaseEnemy` already
  tracks `mineralCount` / `collectMineral()` / `mineralRedropCount()`.
- The shared enemy-fire dispatcher (`src/entities/enemyFire.ts`) already
  mentions the "planned Harvester" as the example of a one-line wiring change.

## Desired change

1. Generalise enemy health data-driven: add a `health` CSV column + codec +
   `EnemyConfig.health` (default 1), and make the shared collision path
   correctly finalise a multi-hit kill (audio, `onEnemyDestroyed`, drops, wave
   accounting).
2. Add a `Harvester` entity (`health = 5`) that roams (like the Asteroid) and
   steers toward the nearest live mineral, absorbing it on overlap; no firing.
3. Register the archetype (CSV + seed + factory + score ≈ 400) and expose it in
   the gym.
4. Integrate it into the campaign as a rare roaming spawn in later levels,
   registered with the `WaveManager`.
5. Update the GDD/ENEMY design docs/README for the health-model and enemy
   catalog changes.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` — New `harvester` row (`health = 5`); add a
  `health` column to every row (default 1).
- `src/core/configTypes.ts` — `health` field on `EnemyConfig`.
- `src/core/csv.ts` — `health` column in `ENEMY_COLUMN_ORDER`, coercion and
  validation.
- `src/core/configDefaults.ts` — `harvester` seed fallback (+ default health 1
  for existing seeds).
- `src/entities/Harvester.ts` — New roamer entity: slow seek movement, large
  body, five-hit health, no firing.
- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts` — Shared multi-hit health / `takeDamage`
  behaviour (or a small shared health helper).
- `src/entities/enemyFactory.ts` — Map `harvester` → `Harvester`.
- `src/entities/enemyFire.ts` — No-firing archetype handling (the Harvester
  must not fall back to the aimed shot).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — Finalise a multi-hit kill through
  `onEnemyDestroyed` + destruction audio; supply the live mineral field to
  seeking entities.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — Wire seeking/minerals, score value, roamer
  movement, wave/score accounting.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` + `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.ts` —
  Expose the same mineral list/seek seam and multi-hit path.
- `src/waves/Formations.ts` / `src/waves/AsteroidSpawner.ts` /
  `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` — Campaign roaming-spawn integration.
- `src/core/constants.ts` — `SCORE_VALUES.harvester` ≈ 400.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`,
  `README.md` — Documentation updates.
- Tests: `src/entities/Harvester.test.ts`,
  `src/entities/enemyFactory.test.ts`, `src/core/csv.test.ts`,
  `src/core/enemyConfig.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`.

## Related work

- `AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA` — Gym↔game behavioural-parity epic (critical, open).
  This work must consume the shared cores it establishes and must not add a new
  divergence.
- `AH-0MUII3BBW000XZ46` — Shared enemy-fire dispatch (completed). Names the
  Harvester as the exemplar of one-line fire wiring.
- `AH-0MUII3DHM008L7JF` — Shared mineral layer: collection, hold/overflow,
  choice overlay (completed).
- `AH-0MUHMT5JC004WRSB` — Gym asteroids do not drop minerals / shared
  kill-drop rule (open); relevant to the re-drop path.
- `AH-0MU8BZ2ZM004J47F` — E6 Asteroid non-formation roamer (completed).
  Precedent architecture for a roaming enemy.
- `AH-0MT7V5UH90023XWR` — Clarify enemy health / one-hit destruction model in
  GDD (completed). The GDD's 1-HP rule is revised by this work (see Resolved
  decisions).
- `AH-0MTZWZ7MC002B01K` — Enemy difficulty scoring (completed). Health is not
  currently a scored factor.
- `AH-0MUJPTR7Q0070BDT` — Add a health factor to the enemy difficulty index
  (created, low priority, `discovered-from:AH-0MUI820PM0038HS2`). Tracks the
  difficulty-scoring follow-up so it does not creep into this item.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — multi-hit kill does not finalise.** The current
  `onPlayerBulletHitsEnemy` `takeDamage` branch skips `onEnemyDestroyed` and
  destruction audio. Mitigation: extend the shared seam and pin it with a test
  so score/wave/drop/audio happen exactly once on the killing blow.
- **Risk — seek seam duplication.** Giving the entity the mineral list must be
  done once in the shared collision/tick path, not copied into each scene
  (parity epic). Mitigation: add a single `setSeekTargets`/equivalent seam
  alongside the existing `setAimTarget`.
- **Risk — health-model regression.** Generalising health could accidentally
  weaken the one-hit guarantee for existing enemies. Mitigation: `health`
  defaults to 1 and a regression test asserts one-hit destruction for every
  existing archetype.
- **Risk — difficulty under-scoring.** `enemyDifficulty` has no health factor.
  Mitigation: tracked separately as `AH-0MUJPTR7Q0070BDT`.
- **Risk — scope creep into wave/level design.** Wiring a new roamer into the
  campaign can balloon. Mitigation: scope is a rare roaming spawn in Levels 4–5
  only; the gym demonstration is the tuning surface.
- **Assumption — "collects it" reuses existing absorption.** The Harvester
  absorbs the mineral on overlap and tallies it; on death it re-drops 25–50 %
  per the existing rule.
- **Assumption — no dedicated health bar.** Feedback for non-lethal hits is the
  existing bullet-impact VFX (plus bullet consumption) rather than a drawn
  health bar; the producer's Q1 sub-question was not separately answered, so
  this minimal readable feedback is the default and can be revisited.
- **Assumption — tuning values are implementation/gym choices.** "Large" and
  "slow" are the requirements; exact px size/speed/colour are chosen and tuned
  in the gym (indicative: size ≈ 40–48 px, speed ≈ 20–30 px/s).
- **Assumption — the Harvester does not fire.**

## Resolved decisions (producer, 2026-09-27)

1. **Health model — data-driven.** Add a `health` column to the enemy-config
   pipeline and generalise multi-hit destruction for regular enemies; update the
   GDD. P4 Bomb continues to deal no damage to enemies. No dedicated health bar
   (minimal impact feedback); see Assumptions.
2. **Mineral-seeking semantics — literal seek.** Always seek the nearest live
   mineral anywhere on the field; absorb on overlap; no firing; cannot steal
   from the player's hold; existing 25–50 % re-drop applies.
3. **Spawn / campaign integration — gym + rare campaign roamer.** Available in
   the gym and added as a rare roaming spawn in later levels.
4. **Score / difficulty — score ≈ 400; difficulty health factor deferred.** The
   `enemyDifficulty` health factor is a separate follow-up
   (`AH-0MUJPTR7Q0070BDT`).

## Appendix — clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (blocking) — Health model.** "A five-hit regular enemy contradicts the
  GDD's explicit 1-HP model. Options: (a) generalise health data-driven (new
  `health` CSV column + config type/codec + GDD update; P4 Bomb still deals no
  damage); (b) Harvester-only code constant; (c) other. Sub-question: should
  each non-lethal hit show a health indicator, or is ordinary hit feedback
  enough?" — **Answer (operator, interactive reply): "1. a".** Decision:
  data-driven `health` column + GDD update; P4 unchanged. Sub-question left to
  the minimal-feedback assumption above.
- **Q2 (blocking) — Mineral-seeking semantics.** "Options: (a) always seek the
  nearest live mineral anywhere on the field; absorb on overlap; no firing;
  cannot steal from the player's hold; re-drop 25–50 % per the existing rule;
  (b) only within a detection radius; (c) also fire at the player." — **Answer
  (operator, interactive reply): "2. a".**
- **Q3 (blocking) — Spawn / campaign integration.** "Options: (a) available in
  the gym and added to the campaign as a rare roaming spawn in later levels;
  (b) gym-only for now; (c) a fixed formation group." — **Answer (operator,
  interactive reply): "3. a".**
- **Q4 (non-blocking) — Score and difficulty weight.** "Recommended: score
  ≈ 400 (durable, between Tank 300 and Boss phases) and a linked follow-up to
  add a `health` factor to `enemyDifficulty`." — **Answer (operator,
  interactive reply): "4. a".** Follow-up item created:
  `AH-0MUJPTR7Q0070BDT`.
- Q (self-directed, repo research): "Is the Harvester already tracked or
  referenced?" — Research: `wl search harvester` and repo grep. Result: only
  this item and a code comment in `src/entities/enemyFire.ts` naming the
  "planned Harvester"; `src/entities/enemyFire.test.ts` uses `'harvester'` as
  a fallback-key example. No duplicate work item exists.
- Q (self-directed, repo research): "Does multi-hit support already exist for
  regular enemies?" — Research: inspected `CombatScene.onPlayerBulletHitsEnemy`,
  `GymFormationScene` `FormationSceneEntity.takeDamage`, and `Boss.takeDamage`.
  Result: an optional `takeDamage` seam exists, but the shared generic path
  does not finalise a kill (`onEnemyDestroyed`/destruction audio) — a gap to
  close (see Risks).
- Q (self-directed, repo research): "How do minerals and roaming enemies
  currently work?" — Research: read `mineralLayer.ts`, `Mineral.ts`,
  `mineralKillDrops.ts`, `BaseEnemy` mineral accounting, `Asteroid.ts` and
  `AsteroidSpawner.ts`. Result: absorption + re-drop and the non-formation
  roamer/spawner patterns both exist and are reusable; the only new capability
  is *seeking* the nearest mineral.

## Goal
Fix the displayed-vs-applied option divergence in the main-game mineral choice overlay so the player sees and gets the same option.

## Root Cause
`PlayScene.openMineralChoice()` draws options via `this.mineralChoiceStrategy.choose(3, this.rng)` and stores them in `this.mineralChoiceOptions`, but only passes `{ origin: 'PlayScene' }` to the MineralChoiceScene overlay. `MineralChoiceScene.init()` then draws its own independent options via `randomChoiceStrategy.choose(3)` when `options` is absent. `selectMineralChoice(index)` applies `play.mineralChoiceOptions[index]` — a different draw from the label shown.

## Implementation
1. In `PlayScene.openMineralChoice()`: pass `options: [...this.mineralChoiceOptions]` and `strategy: this.mineralChoiceStrategy` to MineralChoiceScene.init().
2. Confirm `MineralChoiceScene.init()` uses the passed options when present (already does: `data.options ?? strategy.choose(3)`).
3. Optionally forward the full `ChoiceOption` object from select() (not just index) for robustness.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **AC1 — Displayed choice equals applied choice (main game + gyms):** deterministic test asserts selectMineralChoice returns the option shown at the same index.
- **AC-F1:** When PlayScene opens the mineral choice, the displayed options match `this.mineralChoiceOptions`.
- **AC-F2:** Selecting an option by index applies the correct stored option.
- **AC-F3:** The gym path (which already passes options) is unaffected.

## Key Files
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — openMineralChoice()
- `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` — init(), select()

## Goal
Make P7 Teleport operational in the minerals gym by wiring key binding, handler invocation, and canTeleport override.

## Root Cause
GymMinerals' asteroidFormationConfig() omits the `powerUps` config key, so GymFormationScene.powerUpsEnabled stays false. Consequently:
- _initPowerUpLayer() returns early and never binds the S/keys
- _updatePowerUpLayer() returns early and never calls _handleTeleport()
- canTeleport() returns powerUpsEnabled (false)

## Implementation
1. In GymFormationScene, bind the teleport key (S/Down) whenever a player exists, independent of powerUpsEnabled.
2. In GymFormationScene, call _handleTeleport() each tick whenever hasTeleport() is true, independent of powerUpsEnabled.
3. Override canTeleport() to return hasTeleport() in addition to powerUpsEnabled.
4. Ensure _handleTeleport() triggers P6 Phase Shift on arrival (as per GDD and AH-0MT7UY5UR002LD5U).

## Risks
- S is also the "down" movement key; use JustDown semantics to avoid double-consumption.
- Must not affect other gyms that rely on powerUpsEnabled gating.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **AC2 — P7 Teleport works in the minerals gym:** after a P7 Teleport is granted, stack decremented, player position changed, isPhased true.
- **AC-F4:** Pressing S or Down consumes one teleport stack and moves the player to a safe spot.
- **AC-F5:** P6 Phase Shift is granted on arrival.
- **AC-F6:** No regression in other gyms (GymPowerUpsCombat, GymEnemies, GymBoss).

## Key Files
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — _initPowerUpLayer, _updatePowerUpLayer, canTeleport, _handleTeleport
- `src/scenes/gym/GymMinerals.ts`
- `src/scenes/core/EffectsRegistry.ts`

## Goal
Wire the shared EffectsRegistry into GymFormationScene's combat hooks so P6 (Phase Shift) and P3 (Shield) granted via the mineral reward choice are honoured.

## Root Cause
GymFormationScene does not override isPlayerPhased() or tryAbsorbPlayerHit(), so CombatCoreScene's defaults (false) are used even though EffectsRegistry.isPhased / isShielded are true. The mineral reward can grant these effects, but _handleCollisions() never honours them.

## Implementation
1. Override isPlayerPhased() in GymFormationScene to return registry.isPhased.
2. Override tryAbsorbPlayerHit() in GymFormationScene to:
   - Return true (absorb) when registry.isShielded is true and pop the shield.
   - Delegate to the parent/hook chain for other logic.
3. Follow the pattern from GymPowerUpsCombat.ts which already overrides these hooks correctly.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **AC3 — P6 Phase Shift protects in the minerals gym:** while P6 is active, enemy bullets and bodies do not register a hit; playerHitCount unchanged.
- **AC4 — P3 Shield absorbs in the minerals gym:** first hit absorbed and shield pops, playerHitCount unchanged; next hit registers.
- **AC-F7:** While P6 Phase Shift is active, enemy bullets and bodies do not register hits.
- **AC-F8:** While P3 Shield is active, the first hit is absorbed and the shield pops; the next hit registers.
- **AC-F9:** No regression in other gyms (GymPowerUpsCombat, GymEnemies, GymBoss, PlayScene).

- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — isPlayerPhased(), tryAbsorbPlayerHit()

- `src/scenes/core/EffectsRegistry.ts` — isPhased, isShielded

# Add enemy-gym phase/shield gating regression tests

## Context

Parent: AH-0MUHM66ES0027QQV — Enemy gym: P3 shield and P6 phase shift do not work when collected (hit-gating not shared).

Test-first slice of the parent bug. In `GymFormationScene` (the base of `GymEnemies`, `GymBoss`, `GymMinerals`) the inherited `isPlayerPhased()` / `tryAbsorbPlayerHit()` defaults return `false`, so P6 Phase Shift and P3 Shield collected in the enemy gym are recorded in the `EffectsRegistry` (the HUD shows them active) but never gate a hit. This item adds the regression tests that prove the gap and become the red-to-green proof for the sibling implementation item.

## User story

As a maintainer, I want failing regression tests that pin the expected enemy-gym behaviour for P3/P6, so the fix cannot silently regress again and a fix in one scene cannot silently miss the others.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 — P6 phase immunity in the enemy gym: with the power-up layer active in a `GymFormationScene`-based scene (any `enemyKey`, including `diver`), collecting P6 Phase Shift makes the player immune to enemy bullets and enemy body contact for the effect duration (no `playerHitCount` increment, no life loss, no respawn); on expiry the next hit lands normally.
- [ ] AC2 — P3 shield absorbs one hit in the enemy gym: collecting P3 Shield causes exactly the next hit to be absorbed — the shield is consumed (registry no longer shielded), the post-hit invulnerability window starts, and the player does not lose a life; the following hit lands normally.
- [ ] AC6 — validation: an automated test/validation criterion is satisfied across the affected scenes (new regression tests fail before the fix and pass after it); the red evidence is recorded in a work-item comment.
- [ ] The tests exercise a real enemy key route (`GymEnemies` with `enemyKey: 'diver'`) and/or a `GymFormationScene` stub, so the single reusable enemy gym scene is covered.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts` — behavioural regression tests on the stub formation scene with the power-up layer enabled.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.test.ts` — diver-route regression test on the real reusable enemy gym scene.

## Deliverables

- New and updated tests only (no production code changes in this item).

# Centralise phase/shield hit-gating in shared combat base

## Context

Parent: AH-0MUHM66ES0027QQV — Enemy gym: P3 shield and P6 phase shift do not work when collected (hit-gating not shared).

`PlayScene` and `GymPowerUpsCombat` each override `isPlayerPhased()` / `tryAbsorbPlayerHit()`; `GymFormationScene` does not, so it inherits `CombatCoreScene`'s `false` defaults and the enemy gym never gates a hit. Move the registry-backed gating into one shared place so every `CombatScene` subclass cannot diverge.

## User story

As a maintainer, I expect phase/shield hit-gating to live in one shared place, so a fix in one scene cannot silently miss the others.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC3 — single shared implementation: phase/shield hit-gating is implemented once in the shared combat base (`CombatCoreScene`/`CombatScene`) backed by the inherited `EffectsRegistry`; the now-redundant duplicate overrides in `PlayScene` and `GymPowerUpsCombat` are removed or reduced to scene-specific extras, and an equivalence test asserts `PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene` and `GymPowerUpsCombat` route phase/shield through the same shared hooks.
- [ ] AC2 — P3 shield absorbs one hit in the enemy gym: the shield absorb consumes exactly one shield, starts the post-hit invulnerability, and never costs a life; the following hit lands normally; invulnerability durations are preserved (`PlayScene` 1.5 s, `GymPowerUpsCombat` 0.8 s) and the unabsorbed hit still runs the normal lose-life flow.
- [ ] AC7 — full suite: full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
- [ ] `GymFormationScene` and its subclasses (`GymEnemies`, `GymBoss`, `GymMinerals`) inherit correct gating with no per-scene override.
- [ ] The play scene's shield-absorb destruction cue is preserved via a scene-specific hook (for example `onShieldAbsorbed()` default no-op) so `GymPowerUpsCombat` behaviour is unchanged.
- [ ] The regression tests from the test-first sibling item pass.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — concrete registry-backed hooks plus an optional `onShieldAbsorbed()` seam.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — update hook docs; keep safe non-combat defaults for direct subclasses (`GymPowerUpsUtility`, `GymWeapons`).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — remove the two overrides; keep the absorb cue via the seam.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` — remove the two overrides.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.test.ts` — unit tests for the shared hooks.

## Deliverables

- Production code plus updated unit tests.

# Test: shared mineral kill-drop rule

Test-first task for AH-0MUHMT5JC004WRSB (AC3, AC5).

## Goal

Write deterministic unit + guard tests that pin the contract of the shared mineral kill-drop rule **before** it is implemented, so `PlayScene` and the gyms provably share one rule.

## Required coverage

- Small asteroid (`getSizeTier() === 'small'`) → exactly one mineral drop at the asteroid's death position.
- Large and medium asteroid → no direct drop (their small split children drop).
- Non-asteroid enemy that absorbed N minerals → re-drops between `mineralRedropFractionMin` and `mineralRedropFractionMax` of N, never more than N, at the death site, using a seeded RNG for determinism.
- Non-asteroid enemy with 0 absorbed minerals → no drops.
- Re-drop scatter stays within `MINERAL_REDROP_SCATTER_RADIUS` of the death site.

## Assumption

Shared helper module path: `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.ts` exporting `resolveMineralKillDrops(scene, entity, rng): Mineral[]` (operator selected the shared-helper approach — see the parent item's Appendix).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC3 — Single shared code path.** The mineral kill-drop rule (small-asteroid drop + non-asteroid re-drop) has one production definition that both `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene` consume, and a repo-wide guard asserts it.
- **AC5 — Tests are added and green.** New tests cover the shared rule and the guard; `npm test` for the new files passes.
- The unit tests are deterministic (seeded RNG, no reliance on `Math.random`) and cover every bullet under Required coverage.
- Tests fail before the implementation task lands and pass once it does.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.test.ts` — new.

# Test: gyms drop minerals on kill

Test-first task for AH-0MUHMT5JC004WRSB (AC1, AC2, AC5).

## Goal

Write deterministic gym tests that fail while the gyms do not drop minerals, pinning the behaviour the gym-wiring task must deliver.

## Required coverage

- Destroying a small asteroid in `GymMinerals` and the `GymEnemies` asteroid row (via the shared destruction path and via the EXPLODE button) increases the live mineral count by exactly one at the asteroid's position.
- A large/medium asteroid splits into its children without a direct mineral drop.
- No double drop: a single destruction produces exactly one drop (not one per path).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Gyms drop on small-asteroid destruction.** Destroying a small asteroid in `GymMinerals` / `GymEnemies` asteroid row spawns exactly one mineral at its position.
- **AC2 — Gyms re-drop for non-asteroid enemies.** In a gym, a non-asteroid enemy re-drops a configured fraction of the absorbed minerals at its death site.
- **AC5 — Tests are added and green.** New tests cover the gym drop behaviour; `npm test` for the gym suites passes.
- Tests assert the drop position and count, not merely that the count increased, and are deterministic (seeded RNG).
- Tests fail before the gym-wiring task lands and pass after it.

# Intake brief — Gym↔game behavioural-parity audit

**Headline:** A full evaluation of the scene layer found twelve places where the shipped `PlayScene` and the gym scenes still run **divergent copies of the same behaviour**. This epic tracks extracting each into one shared implementation (or explicitly recording an intentional difference), so that every object behaves identically in every scene and new divergence is caught by an automated guard.

## Problem statement

Operators continue to see errors caused by differences between gym scenes and the game scene. The producer directive is that **gyms and the game must execute the same core code**; the only legitimate difference is that a gym enables a **constrained set of features** (one enemy type, the enemy editor, fixed formations, no campaign/wave progression). Prior epics (`AH-0MUD8E015004C4JO`, `AH-0MUDCT7EU0061OSZ`) unified the eight combat/lifecycle methods onto `CombatCoreScene`/`CombatScene`, but the audit below shows that a second tier of behaviour — player control, enemy fire dispatch, projectile lifecycle, power-up drops, minerals, the boss, teleport and the gym base seams — is still duplicated and has already drifted.

## Users

- **As a player**, when I practice in a gym I want every object (player, enemies, asteroids, boss, minerals, power-ups, bullets) to behave exactly as it does in the game, so the gym is a truthful training ground.
- **As a developer**, when I change a behaviour I want to change it in exactly one place, so a scenario cannot drift from the shipped game.
- **As a tester**, I want an automated parity guard that fails when a scene re-introduces a duplicate of a shared method, so regressions are caught before release.
- **As the producer**, I want the "gyms are the parity reference" principle enforced by code structure and tests.

## Evaluation method

Reviewed every production scene under `src/scenes` (`PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene` and its subclasses `GymEnemies`/`GymBoss`/`GymMinerals`, `GymPlayer`, `GymWeapons`, `GymPowerUpsCombat`, `GymPowerUpsUtility`) plus the shared cores `CombatCoreScene`/`CombatScene`, and the entity/config layer (`enemyFactory`, `BaseEnemy`, `Asteroid`, `Boss`, `Mineral`, `powerups/*`). Compared method inventories, dispatch tables, per-frame sequences and copy-pasted bodies, and cross-checked against the existing worklog so as not to duplicate open items.

## Findings — the gap register

| # | Gap | Evidence (divergent copies) | Impact |
|---|-----|------------------------------|--------|
| 1 | **Player-control step duplicated** | Input→timers→multipliers→physics sequence re-implemented in `PlayScene.tick`, `GymFormationScene.tick`, `GymWeapons.tick`, `GymPowerUpsUtility.tick`, `GymPowerUpsCombat.tick`; `GymPlayer.update` inlines the input-map branch instead of the shared `_readPlayerInput` | Player movement/fire-rate differs between scenes; GymPlayer does not share any control code |
| 2 | **Enemy fire dispatch duplicated** | `PlayScene._fireFor` and `GymEnemies.collectBullets` both hard-code `enemyKey → tryFire*`; `GymPowerUpsCombat._tickScouts` re-implements it again with a **fake fixed 16 ms clock** (`_nextFireTime += 16`) instead of the scene clock | A new enemy type must be wired twice; gym/combat fire cadence is frame-count-based, not time-based |
| 3 | **Projectile lifecycle duplicated** | Enemy-bullet wrap+expiry loop in `PlayScene._advanceBullets`, `GymFormationScene.tick`, `GymPowerUpsCombat._advanceEnemyBullets`; player-bullet advance via `advanceAndCull` in `PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene._advancePlayerBullets`, `GymWeapons._advanceBullets`/`advanceBullets` | Wrap/expiry fixes reach one scene only |
| 4 | **Power-up drop layer duplicated & drifted** | Spawner build (`PlayScene._buildDropSpawner` ≈ `GymFormationScene._buildDefaultPowerUpSpawner`); lifecycle+collection (`PlayScene._updateDrops`/`_collectIfOverlapping` ≈ `GymFormationScene._updatePowerUpLayer`/`_collectOverlappingDrops` ≈ `GymWeapons.advanceDrops`/`collectOverlapping` ≈ `GymPowerUpsCombat.advanceDrops`/`_collectOverlapping` ≈ `GymPowerUpsUtility.advanceDrops`/`_collectOverlapping`); **P9 magnet** only in `PlayScene` + `GymPowerUpsUtility`; **P4 bomb notice** only in `PlayScene` + `GymPowerUpsCombat`; **per-type pickup cues** only in `PlayScene`, `GymWeapons`, `GymPowerUpsUtility` | P9/P4/cue behaviour differs between gyms; five copies of the collect loop |
| 5 | **Mineral layer duplicated & drifted** | `PlayScene._handleMinerals` ≈ `GymFormationScene._updateMinerals`; `openMineralChoice`/`selectMineralChoice` duplicated with different contracts (`GameState` + overflow + `MineralChoiceScene{origin,options,strategy}` vs a local `mineralHold` capped and reset to 0 + `MineralChoiceScene{onSelect}`); `MineralChoiceScene` carries both interfaces | Hold overflow, choice wiring and reward application differ between game and gym |
| 6 | **Boss integration diverges** | `PlayScene._updateBoss(dt)` runs inside `tick`; `GymBoss.update` calls `super.tick(dt)` **then** advances the boss, so `GymBoss.tick()` never advances the boss; `PlayScene.getAdditionalTeleportBodies` avoids the boss for P7, `GymBoss` does not; `PlayScene._spawnMinions` (phase minions) has no gym equivalent | Boss behaves differently (bullet timing, teleport safety, minions) in the gym |
| 7 | **Teleport duplicated** | `GymPowerUpsCombat.triggerTeleport` is a full override of the shared `CombatScene.triggerTeleport`, bypassing `canTeleport()` and the hit-radius hooks (hard-codes `ENEMY_HIT_RADIUS`/`BULLET_HIT_RADIUS`) | Teleport safety logic can drift; the gym override is not exercised by shared tests |
| 8 | **Asteroid split duplicated** | Identical `onEntityDestroyed` split closures in `GymEnemies.ts` and `GymMinerals.ts` | A split-physics change must be made twice |
| 9 | **Gym base seams bypassed via casts** | `GymEnemies._onRespawn` reaches into private `entities`/`playerBullets` and re-implements `GymFormationScene._respawnFormation`; `_onTogglePlayer` casts to mutate the base's private `player`/spawn coords | Duplicate respawn logic; fragile casts |
| 10 | **Restart/teardown parity** | `PlayScene._resetRunState` calls `effectsRegistry.reset()`; `GymFormationScene` only recreates the registry when the power-up layer is enabled, and never resets it on teardown, so `GymMinerals`/`GymEnemies` keep permanent effects across a restart | Stale effects after restart in gyms without field drops |
| 11 | **GymPlayer not on the shared control core** | `GymPlayer` extends `Phaser.Scene` and inlines the scheme→input mapping; no shared player tick | The "player" object is the one object with a genuinely separate code path in one gym |
| 12 | **No automated parity guard for the second tier** | The existing `definesMethod` guard (`CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) covers only the original eight methods; none of the shared helpers above are guarded, and the cross-scene equivalence test covers only a subset of behaviours | Future divergence is invisible until a user reports a bug |

> **Already tracked (do not duplicate):** mineral **kill-drop** rule — `AH-0MUHMT5JC004WRSB` (+ children `AH-0MUIGTRFY002JDDS`, `AH-0MUIG1AFG00938TV`, `AH-0MUIGTRVA0072TWW`, `AH-0MUIGTSAX00096Y4`, `AH-0MUIG16QK003MSNO`); "gym-parity principle in AGENTS.md" — `AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1`; beat-clock fire scheduling — `AH-0MUAYB8EH005RJ8B` (+ blocked children). These are referenced as related/blocking rather than re-created.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Each gap in the register has a single shared implementation.** Gaps 1–11 are closed by extracting the duplicated behaviour into the shared core/module or by consuming an existing shared hook; no production scene re-implements a shared behaviour. Verified by the extended duplicate-body guard and by prototype-identity assertions.
- [ ] **AC2 — Behavioural gaps are closed (or explicitly documented as intentional).** Every behavioural difference identified in gaps 1–11 (P9 magnet in formation gyms, P4 notice, per-type pickup cues, boss-in-`tick`, boss teleport avoidance, teleport gating, hold overflow, restart effect reset, GymPlayer input) is either made identical to the game or recorded as an intentional, approved difference in the epic description and the relevant child.
- [ ] **AC3 — Cross-scene equivalence for every object.** Automated tests boot both `PlayScene` and each gym and assert identical outcomes for the player, each enemy archetype, asteroids (incl. split), the boss, minerals (collection/hold/choice), power-ups (spawn/lifecycle/collect/magnet/bomb/cues) and projectiles under the same input and `dt`.
- [ ] **AC4 — Regression guard.** The repo-wide duplicate-body guard is extended to cover every newly shared method/helper, and a permanent test fails if any production scene re-introduces a copy.
- [ ] **AC5 — No behaviour regression in the game.** `PlayScene` behaviour and all existing tests remain green; any change to game behaviour is called out explicitly in the epic and approved as canonical.
- [ ] **AC6 — Documentation.** `docs/Game Design Document.md` §6.4, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, the gym docstrings and `README.md` describe the shared behaviour modules, the hooks a gym implements, and the constrained-feature (not divergent-code) nature of gyms.
- [ ] **AC7 — Full project test suite passes.** The complete suite (`/skill:test`, `npm test`) passes with zero failures and no newly-flaky tests.

## Constraints

- **Single source of truth:** extract genuinely shared behaviour; do not trade one duplication for another. A shared module must not force game-only concerns (score, waves, lives) into gyms, nor gym-only concerns (editor, fixed formations) into the game.
- **Minimum churn / surgical:** match existing style; do not delete unrelated dead code (report it instead).
- **Preserve public/test seams** (e.g. `getBullets`, `advanceBullets`, `getDrops`, `getCollectAnimations`, `spawnDrop`, `triggerTeleport`, `getPlayerHitCount`, help/back handles).
- **Generics/type-safety:** the shared core is generic (`<TEnemy, TBullet, TDrop>`); additions must not weaken typing.
- **Determinism:** tests drive `tick(dt)`; shared behaviour must be driven by the supplied `dt` and the scene clock — no frame-count fake clocks.
- **UK English** in all written output and docs.
- **Gating:** implementation proceeds only through `/skill:implement`; this item does not authorise code changes.

## Existing state (verified 2026-09-26 against HEAD)

- Shared cores exist: `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` (input, auto-fire, drop collection) and `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` (collisions, hits, teleport); `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene` extend `CombatScene`; `GymPowerUpsCombat` extends `CombatScene`; `GymWeapons`/`GymPowerUpsUtility` extend `CombatCoreScene`.
- The eight-method duplicate guard and cross-scene equivalence tests live in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`; `src/test/duplicateBodyGuard.ts` hosts `definesMethod`/`collectProductionSourceFiles`.
- `GymEnemies` is the single config-driven enemy gym (one row per enemy config on the index); `GymMinerals` is asteroids-only; `GymBoss` is the dedicated 4-phase boss gym; `GymPlayer` is the bare-bones tuning scene.
- Entity classes (`Player`, `Scout`, `Diver`, `Tank`, `Phaser`, `Swarm`, `Boss`, `Asteroid`, `Mineral`) are already shared; the divergence is entirely at the **scene integration** layer.
- Open related items: `AH-0MUHMT5JC004WRSB` (mineral kill-drop), `AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1` (document parity principle), `AH-0MUAYB8EH005RJ8B` (beat-clock fire scheduling).

## Desired change

Extract/consume shared behaviour for gaps 1–11 and extend the guard for gap 12, via the dependency-ordered child items below. Do not redesign gym feature gating: a gym may still enable only a subset of features and disable others (e.g. scoring), but the code running for an enabled object must be the same code as the game.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` / `CombatScene.ts` — host shared player tick, projectile lifecycle, and teleport hooks.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — delegate duplicated bodies to the shared helpers.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — consume shared helpers; expose protected seams; reset registry.
- `src/scenes/gym/{GymEnemies,GymBoss,GymMinerals,GymPlayer,GymWeapons,GymPowerUpsCombat,GymPowerUpsUtility}.ts` — consume shared helpers, remove local copies/casts.
- `src/scenes/core/<new shared modules>.ts` — e.g. projectile lifecycle, power-up drop layer, mineral layer, enemy fire dispatch.
- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts` / `src/entities/enemyFactory.ts` — shared enemy-fire seam.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`, `src/test/duplicateBodyGuard.ts` — extend guard/equivalence.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §6.4, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, `README.md` — docs.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — over-abstraction.** Pushing gym-only features into the shared core couples the game to dev tooling. Mitigation: share behaviour only, keep features behind hooks/flags.
- **Risk — behaviour-change ambiguity.** Some divergences may be intentional. Mitigation: each is listed as an OPEN QUESTION below; the default assumption is "the game's behaviour is canonical" unless the producer says otherwise.
- **Risk — test churn.** Both scene suites reach into private internals. Mitigation: keep method names/visibility on the shared base; assert hooks/shared path rather than a class.
- **Risk — scope creep** into a full engine extraction (wave/level system, editor UI). Explicitly out of scope; record extra opportunities as linked items.
- **Assumption:** the shipped game is the canonical behaviour wherever a difference is found, except where an intentional divergence is already approved (e.g. `GymPowerUpsCombat` 0.8 s invulnerability).
- **Assumption:** gyms remain feature-constrained (no campaign/wave progression, optional scoring); "no difference" means no difference in the code path for enabled features, not "the gym must run the campaign".

## Related work

- `AH-0MUD8E015004C4JO` — Unify PlayScene/GymFormationScene combat logic into a shared core (completed, epic).
- `AH-0MUDCT7EU0061OSZ` — Extract shared combat core into standalone gym scenes (completed).
- `AH-0MUHM66ES0027QQV` — Enemy gym P3/P6 hit-gating not shared (completed) — prior example of this class of defect.
- `AH-0MUHMXWGC0058BO4` — Ability items not functioning (completed) — prior gym/game divergence in choice rewards.
- `AH-0MUD9R4BA004WQEM` — Cross-scene equivalence tests and duplicate-body verification (completed).
- `AH-0MU8QTLYN003JV8M` — Restore gym-game parity RCA (completed).
- `AH-0MUHMT5JC004WRSB` — Gym asteroids do not drop minerals (open) — the mineral kill-drop slice of gap 5.
- `AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1` — Document gym-parity principle in AGENTS.md (open) — supports AC6/governance.
- `AH-0MUAYB8EH005RJ8B` — Bullets should fall on the beat (open) — touches gap 2's fire clock.
- `AH-0MUGXDVPH005TIZL` — Dev Utilities gym scene (open) — future consumer of the shared modules.

## Open questions (canonical-behaviour doubts)

1. **P9 Magnet in formation gyms** — the game and `GymPowerUpsUtility` pull drops toward the ship; `GymFormationScene` (enemy/minerals/boss) does not. Adopt the game behaviour everywhere? *Recommended: yes.*
2. **P4 bomb notice** — game and `GymPowerUpsCombat` show "BOMB! Bullets cleared"; formation gyms do not. Adopt everywhere? *Recommended: yes.*
3. **Per-type pickup cues** — game/weapon/utility gyms play per-type activation cues; formation gyms play only the generic chime. Adopt the game's cue set? *Recommended: yes.*
4. **Boss minions** — the game spawns phase minions (`planMinionSpawns`); `GymBoss` does not. Should the boss gym mirror minion spawning, or is that a deliberately constrained feature? *Recommended: mirror it (behaviour), possibly behind a toggle.*
5. **`GymPowerUpsCombat` invulnerability** — 0.8 s (local hook) vs the game's 1.5 s. Keep the approved exception or converge? *Recommended: keep the hook but document it explicitly as an intentional, approved difference.*
6. **Gym field-drop cadence** — the game drops on a kill chance; gyms drop on a timer. These are different spawn *sources*; is sharing only the lifecycle/collection correct? *Recommended: yes — keep distinct sources, share lifecycle/collection/magnet/notice/cues.*
7. **Mineral hold overflow** — the game carries overflow (`collected − capacity`); the formation gym resets the hold to 0. Adopt overflow? *Recommended: yes.*
8. **GymPlayer scope** — should the bare-bones player gym consume the shared player-control tick/input, or stay deliberately minimal? *Recommended: consume the shared input/physics helper; it need not add enemies.*
9. **Scoring in gyms** — gyms show `SCORE: n/a`. Confirm scoring remains a deliberately disabled feature (not a divergence to fix). *Recommended: yes, keep disabled.*
10. **Enemy-fire seam shape** — shared factory-level dispatcher vs a common `fire(now)` method on `BaseEnemy`. *Recommended: factory-level dispatcher (less invasive to the entity hierarchy).*

## Plan — child work items (dependency-ordered)

| # | Child item | Type | Priority | Depends on | Register gaps |
|---|-----------|------|----------|------------|---------------|
| 1 | Shared player-control step across all scenes | task | critical | — | 1, 11 |
| 2 | Shared enemy-fire dispatch using the real scene clock | task | critical | — | 2 |
| 3 | Shared projectile-lifecycle helper | task | critical | — | 3 |
| 4 | Shared power-up drop layer (spawner, lifecycle, collection, magnet, P4 notice, cues) | task | critical | 3 | 4 |
| 5 | Shared mineral layer (collection, hold/overflow, choice overlay) | task | critical | — | 5 (kill-drop tracked by `AH-0MUHMT5JC004WRSB`) |
| 6 | Boss integration on the shared tick (+ teleport avoidance, minions) | task | critical | 1 | 6 |
| 7 | Unify teleport: remove `GymPowerUpsCombat` override | task | critical | 3 | 7 |
| 8 | Shared asteroid-split helper and protected gym base seams | task | critical | — | 8, 9 |
| 9 | Restart/teardown parity across gyms | task | critical | — | 10 |
| 10 | Extend parity regression guard and cross-scene equivalence tests | task | critical | 1–9 | 12 |

The dependency graph is acyclic; items 1–3 are foundational, 4 depends on 3, 6 on 1, 7 on 3, and 10 verifies all others.

- The operator's seed instruction was explicit: "If in doubt about which is the correct behaviour leave this as an open question in the work item created." Accordingly, no blocking interview was held; the ten behavioural doubts are recorded above as numbered **Open questions** and repeated in the relevant child items.

# Shared player-control step across all scenes
